docs.title: Logbook Migration
docs.text: The logbook migration feature allows members who have purchased paper logbooks to migrate their existing signatures and skills to the digital system.

docs.title: Member-Initiated Migration
docs.text: Any member can submit a migration request to transfer skills from their physical logbook. Non-paid members can submit with empty skill entries to become paid members upon approval. Paid members must include skill entries to migrate their skills.

docs.title: Manager Direct Migration
docs.text: A trip manager (marshal with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission) can enter data directly for a member, bypassing the review cycle. The request is approved immediately upon creation.

docs.title: Create Migration Request
docs.text:
• POST /api/logbook-migrations/
  • Creates a new migration request.
  • Requires authentication.
  • Supports multipart/form-data for PDF upload.

docs.title: List Migration Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbook-migrations/
  • Lists migration requests for the authenticated user.
  • Admins/marshals with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission see all requests.
  • Query parameters: status, migration_type, member, target_level

docs.title: Get Migration Request Details
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/
  • Retrieves details of a specific migration request.

docs.title: Approve Migration Request
docs.text:
• PATCH /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/approve/
  • Approves a pending migration request.
  • Requires APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission.
  • Creates logbook entries and skill references on approval.
  • Sets member's paid_member to true if not already paid.

docs.title: Return Migration Request
docs.text:
• PATCH /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/return-request/
  • Returns a request to the member for amendments.
  • Requires APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission.

docs.title: Reject Migration Request
docs.text:
• PATCH /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/reject/
  • Rejects a pending migration request.
  • Requires APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission.

docs.title: Edit and Resubmit
docs.text:
• PUT /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/
  • Allows editing a returned request and resubmitting.
  • Only allowed when status is RETURNED.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Action Who Create own request, view own requests Authenticated members View all requests, approve/return/reject Users with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION Create MANAGER_DIRECT requests Users with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION

docs.title: Status Transitions
docs.text:
• PENDING → APPROVED (admin approves)
  • PENDING → RETURNED (admin sends back)
  • PENDING → REJECTED (admin rejects)
  • RETURNED → PENDING (member edits and resubmits)

docs.title: Digital Logbook
docs.text: The digital logbook allows members to track their progress and have their skills verified by trip leads.

docs.title: Create a Logbook Entry
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Creates a new logbook entry for a trip.
    • Requires CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES or CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission.

docs.title: View Logbook Entries for a Trip
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/viewlogbooks

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a list of members checked in to a trip, along with their associated logbook entry.

docs.title: View Logbook Entries for a Member
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/logbookentries

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a list of logbook entries for a specific member.
    • Each entry includes created_at and updated_at timestamps for audit trail purposes.
    • When skills are verified, LogbookSkillReference records are created with signed_by, entered_by, and entered_at fields.

docs.title: List Logbook Skills
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbookskills/

    Note: This endpoint uses a trailing slash (it is a router-registered ViewSet endpoint).

    • Retrieves a list of all available logbook skills (only active skills, ordered by order field).
    • The count_requirement field indicates the minimum number of sign-offs required for a skill.
    • The category field is an object containing the ID and name of the skill category.
    • Pagination: Standard pagination (default 20, max 500).

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description category integer Filter by skill category ID level_gte integer Skills for levels with ID >= this value level_lte integer Skills for levels with ID <= this value level_eq integer Skills for an exact level ID level_null boolean Skills with no level requirement (true or false)

docs.title: Logbook Entries ViewSet (CRUD)
docs.text:
The following router-registered endpoints provide full CRUD access to logbook entries:

  • GET /api/logbookentries/ - List all logbook entries, ordered by ID.
  • GET /api/logbookentries/{id}/ - Retrieve a single entry.
  • POST /api/logbookentries/ - Create a new logbook entry (alternative to POST /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries). Requires CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission. Body includes trip, member, comment, and skills_verified (array of skill IDs).
  • PUT/PATCH /api/logbookentries/{id}/ - Update an entry. Same permission checks as create.
  • DELETE /api/logbookentries/{id}/ - Delete an entry.

Note: Both the trip-specific endpoint (POST /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries) and the ViewSet endpoint (POST /api/logbookentries/) can be used to create entries. They apply the same permission checks.

docs.title: Logbook Skill References ViewSet
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbookskillreferences/ - List all skill reference records.
  • GET /api/logbookskillreferences/{id}/ - Retrieve a single skill reference.
  • Full CRUD is available (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) for authenticated users with appropriate permissions.

Skill Reference Fields: id, logbook_skill, member, trip, signed_by, entered_by, entered_at

docs.title: Logbook Entry Permissions
docs.text: Creating, updating, and deleting logbook entries is governed by a detailed permission system. The rules are as follows:

docs.title: Members Creating Entries for Themselves
docs.text:
• A member cannot create, update, or delete a logbook entry for themselves.
  • Exception: A member with the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission can create, update, or delete an entry for themselves, provided they are registered for the trip.

docs.title: Members Creating Entries for Other Members
docs.text:
• Trip Lead or Deputy Lead: A trip lead or deputy lead can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member, provided that the other member is registered for the trip. The lead/deputy lead does not need to be registered themselves.
  • Superuser (CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER): A member with this permission can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member, provided that the other member is registered for the trip.
  • Regular Member (with CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission): A regular member can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member if all of the following conditions are met:
  • The acting member is registered for the trip.
  • The other member is registered for the trip.
  • The acting member has the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission that applies to the trip's level.

docs.title: Skill Sign-Off Validation (when skills_verified are included in the request)
docs.text:
A user can sign off on skills for another user if any of the following are true:

  • They are the Trip Lead or Deputy Lead for the associated trip.
  • They have the SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS permission AND are registered for the associated trip themselves.
  • They have the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission (this permission bypasses all other skill sign-off checks).

If a user has permission to create or update a logbook entry but lacks the required skill sign-off permissions, the entire request will be denied if it includes skills_verified.

docs.title: Auto-Upgrade on First Logbook Entry
docs.text: When enabled via Global Settings, members can be automatically upgraded to the next level after their first logbook entry is created.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. A logbook entry is created for a member
  2. The system checks if:
  3. Auto-upgrade is enabled in global settings
  4. The member is at the configured source_level
  5. If conditions are met, the member is automatically upgraded to the target_level
  6. The member is also added to the target level's auto_group (if configured)

docs.title: Reverting Upgrade
docs.text: If a logbook entry is deleted and it was the member's only logbook entry, the upgrade is automatically reverted: 1. The system detects the deletion 2. Checks if the member has any remaining logbook entries 3. If no entries remain, the member is reverted to the source_level 4. The member is removed from the target level's auto_group (if different from source)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: See Global Settings for configuration details.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text: AD4x4 supports a maintenance toggle that responds to public app/API requests with 503 Service Unavailable and a short HTML page. The feature is implemented at the nginx layer, not in Django — so it keeps working even if the Django app or Huey workers are being restarted, migrated, or are otherwise unavailable. Django admin remains available during maintenance mode for operator access.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The nginx container inside the Docker Compose stack checks for a marker file on every incoming request:

  • If /etc/nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on exists → nginx returns 503 Service Unavailable with a Retry-After: 3600 header and a small HTML body for public app/API paths
  • /admin, /admin/..., and /static/admin/... bypass maintenance mode so operators can use Django admin while the public site is unavailable
  • If the file is absent → traffic flows through to Django and the static locations as normal

The marker directory (nginx/maintenance/) is mounted as a shared volume between the host and the nginx container in infra/docker-compose.yml, so creating or removing the marker from the host is immediately visible to nginx. The nginx if (-f ...) check is re-evaluated per request, so a config reload isn't strictly required for the state change to take effect — but both scripts run nginx -s reload anyway as a belt-and-braces measure so any in-flight keep-alive connections see a clean state.

The nginx block that implements the check lives in infra/nginx/secure/default.conf.template:

map $uri $maintenance_bypass {
    default 0;
    ~^/admin(?:/|$) 1;
    ~^/static/admin/ 1;
}

set $maintenance_mode 0;
if (-f /etc/nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on) {
    set $maintenance_mode 1;
}
if ($maintenance_bypass = 1) {
    set $maintenance_mode 0;
}
if ($maintenance_mode = 1) {
    return 503;
}
error_page 503 @maintenance;
location @maintenance {
    default_type text/html;
    add_header Retry-After 3600;
    return 503 '<html><body><h1>Maintenance</h1><p>We'll be back soon.</p></body></html>';
}

Because the if blocks are at the server {} level and run before location routing, public API endpoints, uploads, Swagger UI, and frontend assets are blocked in one sweep. The explicit maintenance_bypass map keeps Django admin and its static files available.

docs.title: Enabling maintenance mode
docs.text:
From the production host, with shell access as admin:

cd /home/admin/ad4x4/infra
./enable_maintenance_mode.sh

The script creates the marker file and reloads nginx:

#!/bin/bash
touch ./nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on
docker exec nginx nginx -s reload

The site starts returning 503 immediately. Verify from another machine:

curl -I https://ap.ad4x4.com/
# HTTP/2 503
# retry-after: 3600

docs.title: Disabling maintenance mode
docs.text:
From the production host:

cd /home/admin/ad4x4/infra
./disable_maintenance_mode.sh

The script removes the marker file and reloads nginx:

#!/bin/bash
rm ./nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on
docker exec nginx nginx -s reload

Normal traffic resumes immediately.

docs.title: Why nginx instead of a Django middleware
docs.text:
Putting the maintenance gate at nginx rather than a Django middleware has two operational advantages:

  • Nothing in Django needs to be running. The 503 is served even if the Django container is stopped, the database is mid-migration, Huey is stuck, or a release has just unhealthy-checked out. Those are the exact scenarios where maintenance mode matters most.
  • No request ever reaches Django during maintenance, so there is no database load and no risk of side effects from partially processed requests.

The trade-off is that there is no way for API clients to negotiate a structured maintenance window — the body is a static HTML page, not a JSON envelope with Retry-After metadata or a message key. Clients should match on 503 + Retry-After header to detect the state.

docs.title: Client behaviour
docs.text:
The mobile app and web clients should treat 503 responses during any request as a transient maintenance state and:

  1. Show a "We'll be back soon" screen with a manual retry affordance.
  2. Back off for at least the duration in the Retry-After header (currently 3600 seconds).
  3. Do not send these to Sentry / error reporting — they are expected operational states, not bugs, and will drown real errors.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• The marker file is on the production host, not in the Django database. There is no API endpoint to enable or disable maintenance mode. It's a deliberate ops-level action that requires shell access to the Hetzner host.
  • Static files under /static/ are blocked except /static/admin/. Admin static files stay available so Django admin remains usable. Frontend assets stay blocked because we do not want the public app UI to render half-loaded while the backend is unavailable.
  • There is no Django-level maintenance toggle. ConfigurableSettings does not have a maintenance_mode_enabled field, and there is no custom Django middleware for this purpose. Do not try to add one — the nginx-based flow is the authoritative mechanism, and a duplicate toggle would split-brain the state.
  • nginx -s reload is a belt-and-braces step. The if (-f ...) check is re-evaluated on every request even without reloading, but the reload guarantees all worker processes agree on the new state for in-flight keep-alive connections.
  • The Huey worker container is unaffected by maintenance mode — scheduled tasks and background notifications continue to run. If you need to stop Huey as well, that's a separate docker compose stop huey action.

docs.title: Related documentation
docs.text:
• API Concepts — 503 Service Unavailable — client-side behaviour and expected error shape
  • infra/README.txt — deployment runbook, covers redeploy flow and maintenance windows

docs.title: Meeting Points
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing meeting points.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Meeting points are predefined locations where trip participants can gather. The API provides endpoints for creating, viewing, updating, and deleting these points.

docs.title: List Meeting Points
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/
    • Retrieves a list of all available meeting points, ordered by name.
    • Caching: the response carries Cache-Control: public, max-age=600, so clients and intermediaries may cache the list for up to 10 minutes. If your UI must reflect a newly-created meeting point immediately, bypass the cache (e.g. with a cache-busting query param) or refetch after the TTL expires.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description name string Filter by exact name name__icontains string Filter by name (case-insensitive partial match) area string Filter by area code (e.g., DXB, AUH, NOR, AAN, LIW)

docs.title: Retrieve a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single meeting point.

docs.title: Create a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• POST /api/meetingpoints/
    • Creates a new meeting point. Requires the CREATE_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • Request Body: json { "name": "Al Faya", "lat": 24.733, "lon": 55.766, "link": "https://goo.gl/maps/...", "area": "AUH" } Note: The area field can be one of DXB, NOR, AUH, AAN, or LIW.

docs.title: Update a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Updates an existing meeting point. Requires the EDIT_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • The request body should contain the fields to be updated.

docs.title: Delete a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Deletes a meeting point. Requires the DELETE_MEETING_POINTS permission.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
This document outlines the API endpoints for member management, including searching for members, retrieving member profiles, and managing member information.

For authentication and registration details, please refer to the Authentication and Profiles document.

docs.title: Member List
docs.text:
You can retrieve a list of members using the standard ViewSet endpoint.

GET /api/members/

Authentication: Optional (public endpoint, but contact info requires authentication and permissions)

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description trip_count integer Filter by exact trip count trip_count__range string Filter by trip count range (e.g., 5,20) phone string Filter by exact phone number phone__icontains string Filter by partial phone number level__numeric_level integer Filter by exact numeric level level__numeric_level__range string Filter by numeric level range level__name string Filter by exact level name level__name__icontains string Filter by partial level name email string Filter by exact email address email__icontains string Filter by partial email (contains) first_name string Filter by exact first name first_name__icontains string Filter by partial first name last_name string Filter by exact last name last_name__icontains string Filter by partial last name level__id integer Filter by level ID nationality string Filter by exact nationality code city string Filter by exact city paid_member boolean Filter by payment status (true or false) last_visited__isnull boolean Filter by visit status (true = never visited, false = visited at least once) last_visited_after datetime Filter members who last visited after this date/time (ISO 8601) last_visited_before datetime Filter members who last visited before this date/time (ISO 8601) date_joined_after date Filter members who joined after this date (e.g., 2026-03-01) date_joined_before date Filter members who joined before this date (e.g., 2026-04-01) search string Text search across username, first name, last name, and email (case-insensitive partial match). Optional — omitting returns all members. ordering string Sort results. Accepted values: username, first_name, last_name, trip_count, level__numeric_level, date_joined, id, last_visited. Prefix with - for descending (e.g., -trip_count). Multi-field: -trip_count,username. Default: id. page integer Page number (default: 1) page_size integer Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Note: Vehicle-related filters (car_brand, car_year) are NOT supported. Vehicle data is managed separately via the Vehicles endpoints.

Success Response:

{
  "count": 100,
  "next": "http://api.example.com/api/members/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "username": "testuser",
      "firstName": "Test",
      "lastName": "User",
      "level": "Newbie",
      "tripCount": 5,
      "paidMember": true,
      "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

Note: In the list response, level is returned as a string (level name). In the detail response (/api/members/{id}/), level is a full object. Contact information (email, phone) is only visible to users with the VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission or when viewing their own profile.

docs.title: Search Members
docs.text:
Search for members by username, first name, or last name. This is useful for finding members when adding trip participants, looking up member profiles, or searching for trip leads.

GET /api/members/search

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description query string Yes Search term - must be at least 3 characters. Matches against username, first name, and last name (case-insensitive partial match) level integer No Level ID for filtering to include only members at a specific level min_level integer No Minimum numeric level for filtering (inclusive) max_level integer No Maximum numeric level for filtering (inclusive) page integer No Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Level Filtering Examples:

# Search for Newbies (level ID 10)
GET /api/members/search?query=john&level=10

# Search for members up to Intermediate (numeric level 100) inclusive
GET /api/members/search?query=john&max_level=100

# Search for members Intermediate (numeric level 100) and higher inclusive
GET /api/members/search?query=john&min_level=100

Request Example:

# Basic search
curl -X GET "http://localhost:8000/api/members/search?query=john&page=1&page_size=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Success Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 42,
  "next": "http://api.example.com/api/members/search?query=john&page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "username": "johndoe",
      "firstName": "John",
      "lastName": "Doe",
      "level": "Marshal",
      "tripCount": 25,
      "paidMember": true,
      "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Missing query):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_parameter_required"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Query too short):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_too_short"
}

Error Response (401 Unauthorized):

{
  "detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
}

Notes: - The search is case-insensitive and performs partial matching (contains) - Query must be at least 3 characters long - Results are ordered by trip_count (descending), then by id (ascending) - Results are paginated using standard pagination - Matches across username, first_name, and last_name fields using OR logic - Results can be filtered by level using level, min_level, or max_level parameters - Contact information (email, phone) is only visible to users with the VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission or when viewing their own profile - Permission Required: Users must have the SEARCH_MEMBERS permission to use this endpoint. By default, this is granted to Newbie level and above. ANIT members cannot use this endpoint.

docs.title: Member Profile Details
docs.text:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Success Response:

{
  "id": 1,
  "username": "testuser",
  "email": "test@example.com",
  "firstName": "Test",
  "lastName": "User",
  "phone": "1234567890",
  "dob": "2000-01-01",
  "iceName": "Jane Doe",
  "icePhone": "0987654321",
  "level": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Newbie",
    "numericLevel": 10,
    "minTripsForUpgrade": 5
  },
  "tripCount": 5,
  "avatar": null,
  "permissions": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "action": "search_members",
      "levels": []
    }
  ],
  "paidMember": true,
  "dateJoined": "2026-01-01T12:00:00",
  "city": "Dubai",
  "gender": "M",
  "nationality": "AE",
  "title": "",
  "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
}

Note: The profile detail does NOT include vehicle/car fields. Vehicles are managed separately via the Vehicles endpoints. The level field is a full object in the detail view, whereas it is a string in the list view.

docs.title: Update Member Profile
docs.text:
Update a member's profile. Users can only update their own profiles unless they are an administrator.

PATCH /api/members/{id}/

Request Body: The request body should contain the fields to be updated. Note that some fields like username, email, level, tripCount, and paidMember are read-only.

Success Response: A successful update will return a 200 OK status code and the updated profile data.

docs.title: Member Trip Counts
docs.text:
Retrieve a detailed breakdown of a member's trip counts by level.

GET /api/members/{id}/tripcounts

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Success Response: Returns a count of approved completed trips grouped by level, counting each trip once.

docs.title: Lead Search
docs.text:
Search for members who have permission to lead trips.

GET /api/members/leadsearch

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Query Parameters: - search - Search term (searches in username, first name, last name) - level - Level ID for filtering to include only members that have permission to lead for a given level

Success Response:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "username": "johndoe",
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "level": "Marshal",
    "tripCount": 25,
    "paidMember": true,
    "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
  }
]

Note: This endpoint returns up to 30 results without pagination. Returns a plain array, not a paginated object.

docs.title: Active Trip Leads
docs.text:
Retrieve unique leads of active trips.

GET /api/members/activetripleads

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Query Parameters: - level - Level ID for filtering to include only leads for trips for a specific level - min_numeric_level - Minimum trip numeric level for filtering - max_numeric_level - Maximum trip numeric level for filtering

Success Response:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "username": "johndoe",
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "level": "Marshal",
    "tripCount": 25,
    "paidMember": true,
    "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
  }
]

Note: This endpoint returns up to 50 results without pagination. Returns a plain array, not a paginated object.

docs.title: Member Trip History
docs.text:
Retrieve a member's trip history.

GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Query Parameters: - checked_in - Include only trips where member is checked in (default: false) - start_time - Filter by start time

Permissions: - Users can always view their own trip history. - To view another member's trip history, users need the VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY permission. - Superusers can view any member's trip history.

Response Fields:

Field Type Description id integer Trip ID title string Trip title description string Trip description startTime datetime Trip start time endTime datetime Trip end time lead object Trip lead {id, username} level object Level {id, name, numericLevel, minTripsForUpgrade, active, displayName} checkedIn boolean Whether the member is checked in for this trip image string/null Trip cover image URL meetingPoint object/null Meeting point {id, name, area, lat, lon, link} registeredCount integer Number of registered members capacity integer Trip capacity allowWaitlist boolean Whether the trip allows waitlisting approvalStatus string Approval status (A, P, C) isRegistered boolean Whether the target member is registered isWaitlisted boolean Whether the target member is on the waitlist

docs.title: Member Upgrade History
docs.text:
Retrieve a member's upgrade request history.

GET /api/members/{id}/upgraderequests

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Permissions: - Requires VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission or viewing own requests.

docs.title: Member Logbook Entries
docs.text:
Retrieve a member's logbook entries.

GET /api/members/{id}/logbookentries

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Permissions: - Users can always view their own logbook entries. - To view another member's logbook entries, users need the VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY permission. - Superusers can view any member's logbook entries.

docs.title: Member Logbook Skills
docs.text:
Retrieve a member's logbook skill references.

GET /api/members/{id}/logbookskills

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Permissions: - Users can always view their own logbook skills. - To view another member's logbook skills, users need the VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY permission. - Superusers can view any member's logbook skills.

docs.title: Member Trip Requests
docs.text:
Retrieve a member's trip requests.

GET /api/members/{id}/triprequests

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Permissions: - Users can always view their own trip requests. - To view another member's trip requests, users need the VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY permission. - Superusers can view any member's trip requests.

docs.title: Member Feedback
docs.text:
Retrieve a member's feedback submissions.

GET /api/members/{id}/feedback

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Permissions: - Users can always view their own feedback. - Superusers can view any member's feedback. - Non-superusers cannot view another member's feedback, regardless of other permissions.

docs.title: Member Payments
docs.text:
Manually update the paidMember field for a member.

POST /api/members/{id}/payments

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Permission: Requires EDIT_MEMBERSHIP_PAYMENTS permission.

Request Body:

{
  "paymentReceived": "true"
}

Success Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "payment_status_updated"
}

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: This document outlines the different types of push and email notifications sent by the backend.

docs.title: Registering for Push Notifications
docs.text:
To receive push notifications, the client application must register the device's FCM token with the backend. This is done by making a POST request to the /api/device/fcm/ endpoint.

POST /api/device/fcm/

Request Body:

{
    "registrationId": "your-fcm-token",
    "type": "ios"
}

The type can be ios, android, or web.

For more information on Firebase Cloud Messaging, please refer to the official documentation.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text:
• New Trip Notification: Sent when a new trip is created.
  • Trip Approval Notification: Sent when a trip is approved or rejected.
  • Accepted from Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are moved from the waitlist to the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Registered List: Sent to a member when they are removed from the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are removed from the waitlist for a trip.
  • New Trip Comment: Sent when a new comment is added to a trip. This is a push-only notification and is NOT stored in the notification log.

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• Upgrade Request Handled: Sent to a member when their upgrade request has been handled (approved or rejected).
  • Upgrade Request Created: Sent to the marshals when a new upgrade request is created.
  • Upgrade Request Reminder: A periodic reminder sent to the marshals about open upgrade requests.

docs.title: Club News
docs.text: • Club-Wide News: Sent to all members when a new club news item is published.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: • Feedback Notification: Sent to administrators when a member submits feedback via email/Telegram. This is not stored as a NotificationType log entry and does not appear in the notification history endpoint.

docs.title: NotificationType Enum Values
docs.text:
The type field in the notification object will contain one of the following enum values:

Value Description NEW_TRIP A new trip has been created. TRIP_APPR A trip has been approved or rejected. WAIT_ACC A user has been accepted from the waitlist. UPG_REQ_HAN An upgrade request has been handled. UPG_REQ_CRE A new upgrade request has been created. UPG_REQ_REM A reminder for an open upgrade request. CLUB_NEWS A new club news item has been published. REM_FROM_TRIP_REG A user has been removed from a trip's registered list. REM_FROM_TRIP_WAIT A user has been removed from a trip's waitlist.

Note: Trip comment notifications are sent via push only and do not appear in the notification log. There is no NEW_TRIP_COMMENT enum value in NotificationType.

docs.title: Notification History
docs.text:
A log of all notifications sent to a member is stored in the database. This allows the client application to display a history of notifications to the user.

GET /api/notifications/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

The endpoint returns the 20 most recent notifications for the authenticated user, ordered by timestamp descending.

Response Fields:

Field Type Description id integer Unique notification ID title string Notification title body string Notification body text timestamp datetime When the notification was created type string Notification type enum value (see table above) relatedObjectId integer ID of the related object (e.g., trip ID, upgrade request ID). Can be null. relatedObjectType string Type of the related object (e.g., "trip", "upgrade_request"). Can be null. isRead boolean Whether the notification has been read

Response Example:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "title": "Trip Approved",
    "body": "Your trip 'Desert Safari' has been approved.",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-15T10:00:00",
    "type": "TRIP_APPR",
    "relatedObjectId": 456,
    "relatedObjectType": "trip",
    "isRead": false
  }
]

Note: The endpoint returns a plain array of the 20 most recent notifications (no pagination wrapper). All field names use camelCase in the response.

docs.title: Marking Notifications as Read
docs.text:
To mark one or more notifications as read, the client can make a POST request to the /api/notifications/mark-as-read/ endpoint.

POST /api/notifications/mark-as-read/

Request Body:

{
    "notificationIds": [1, 2, 3]
}

The notificationIds field should contain a list of notification IDs to be marked as read. The endpoint will return a 204 No Content response on success.

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
    "detail": "notification_ids must be provided."
}

{
    "detail": "One or more notification IDs are invalid or do not belong to the user."
}

docs.title: Notification Settings
docs.text:
Members can configure their notification preferences.

GET /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Response:

{
  "clubNewsEnabledEmail": false,
  "clubNewsEnabledAppPush": true,
  "newTripAlertsEnabledEmail": false,
  "newTripAlertsEnabledAppPush": true,
  "newTripAlertsLevelFilter": [],
  "upgradeRequestReminderEmail": true,
  "tripChatEnabledAppPush": true,
  "lastUserActivity": "2026-03-15"
}

Fields:

Field Type Description clubNewsEnabledEmail boolean Receive club news via email clubNewsEnabledAppPush boolean Receive club news via push notification newTripAlertsEnabledEmail boolean Receive new trip alerts via email newTripAlertsEnabledAppPush boolean Receive new trip alerts via push notification newTripAlertsLevelFilter array Level IDs to filter trip alerts. Empty = all levels. upgradeRequestReminderEmail boolean Receive upgrade request reminders via email tripChatEnabledAppPush boolean Receive push notifications for trip chat messages lastUserActivity date Last user activity date (read-only, auto-updated). Note: This is a date-only field on the notification settings model. For datetime-precision activity tracking with filtering and ordering support, use the lastVisited field on the Member model — see Members.

PUT/PATCH /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings

Update notification settings. All fields except lastUserActivity are writable.

Request Body (example partial update):

{
  "clubNewsEnabledEmail": true,
  "newTripAlertsLevelFilter": [1, 2]
}

docs.title: Notification Purging
docs.text: To prevent the notification log from growing indefinitely, a periodic background task runs daily to purge old notifications. Any notification logs older than 60 days are automatically deleted from the database.

docs.title: Permissions, Groups, and Levels
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive overview of the permissions system used in the API. It details the different user groups, experience levels, and the specific actions each group is permitted to perform by default.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
The permissions system is built on three main concepts:

  • Groups: Users are assigned to one or more groups, which determine their general role and permissions.
  • Levels: Levels represent a user's experience or seniority within the club (e.g., Newbie, Intermediate, Marshal). Some permissions are restricted to certain levels.
  • Actions: These are specific permissions that grant the ability to perform a particular operation via the API (e.g., CREATE_TRIP, APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ).

Permissions are granted to groups, and can optionally be restricted to apply only to certain levels.

docs.title: Fetching User Permissions
docs.text:
To get the permissions for a specific user, you can retrieve their profile from the /api/members/{id}/ endpoint. The user's permissions are included in the permissions array in the response.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Example Response Snippet:

{
    "id": 1,
    "username": "testuser",
    ...
    "permissions": [
        {"id": 1, "action": "create_trip", "levels": []},
        {"id": 2, "action": "view_contact_info", "levels": []}
    ],
    ...
}

Note: Each permission entry is an object, not a plain string. The action field contains the lowercase DB value (e.g., "create_trip", not "CREATE_TRIP"). The levels field is an array of level objects ({id, name, numericLevel, minTripsForUpgrade}) for level-restricted permissions, or an empty array for permissions that apply to all levels.

docs.title: Groups and Levels
docs.text:
The following table lists the default groups and their corresponding experience levels:

Group Level Numeric Level Notes N/A Club Event 5 Level only; no default group ANIT ANIT 10 Auto-upgrade source level Newbies Newbie 10 Default for new users Intermediates Intermediate 100 Advanced Advance 200 Experts Expert 300 Disabled by default Explorers Explorer 400 Marshals Marshal 600 Board members Board member 800 Non-level Groups Trip managers N/A N/A Meeting point managers N/A N/A Media managers N/A N/A Upgrade request managers N/A N/A Site admins N/A N/A Super-users with all permissions

docs.title: Default Permissions by Group
docs.text: Here is a breakdown of the default permissions assigned to each group.

docs.title: Newbies
docs.text:
• Can search for members in the member directory.
  • Can search trips.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: • Can be a deputy lead for Intermediate, Advanced, Expert, and Explorer trips.

docs.title: Explorers
docs.text:
• Can create trips that require approval for the "Newbie" level.
  • Can create trips that do not require approval for Intermediate, Advanced, Expert, and Explorer levels.
  • Can create meeting points.
  • Can view contact information of other members.
  • Can view member trip history.
  • Can create logbook entries and sign off on skills for trips they lead or support.

docs.title: Marshals
docs.text:
• Can create trips without requiring approval.
  • Can create trips that require approval.
  • Can approve, edit, and delete trips.
  • Can edit trip media and trip registrations.
  • Can delete trip comments.
  • Can edit and delete meeting points.
  • Can view trips where they are lead or deputy lead.
  • Can view member trip history.
  • Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.
  • Can create logbook entries for Newbie, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert, and Explorer levels.
  • Can approve logbook migration requests.

docs.title: Board Members
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.
  • Can approve upgrade requests.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.

docs.title: Upgrade Request Managers
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, comment on, edit, and delete upgrade requests.
  • Can delete comments on upgrade requests.

docs.title: Trip Managers
docs.text:
• Can create, edit, approve, and delete trips.
  • Can edit trip registrations and delete trip comments.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.
  • Can view member trip history.
  • Have superuser permissions for creating logbook entries.

docs.title: Media Managers
docs.text: • Can edit trip media.

docs.title: Meeting Point Managers
docs.text: • Can create, edit, and delete meeting points.

docs.title: Site Admins
docs.text: • Have all permissions.

docs.title: Full List of Permissions (Actions)
docs.text:
The following table lists all possible actions in the system. The Action (DB value) column shows the exact lowercase string returned by the API in the action field.

Note: Action values are all lowercase (e.g., "create_trip"). Two values differ from their enum names: OVERRIDE_WAITLIST_SETTING → "override_waitlist" and CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_OTHERS → "create_upgrade_req_for_other" (singular).

docs.title: Groups API
docs.text: The Groups API provides read-only access to the list of user groups.

docs.title: List Groups
docs.text:
• GET /api/groups/
    • Retrieves a list of all groups, ordered by name.
    • Authentication: Optional (public for reading).

Example Response:

[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "Board members",
        "permissions": [1, 5, 12]
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "name": "Explorers",
        "permissions": [3, 7, 8, 11]
    }
]

docs.title: Retrieve a Group
docs.text:
• GET /api/groups/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single group.

Note: Groups are managed via Django Admin. The API does not support creating, updating, or deleting groups.

docs.title: Permission Matrix API
docs.text: The Permission Matrix API provides read-only access to the mapping between groups, actions, and levels.

docs.title: List Permission Matrix Entries
docs.text:
• GET /api/permissionmatrix/
    • Retrieves a list of all permission matrix entries, ordered by ID.
    • Authentication: Optional (public for reading).

Example Response:

[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "action": "create_trip",
        "levels": [1, 2, 3],
        "group": 5
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "action": "approve_trip",
        "levels": [],
        "group": 7
    }
]
Field Type Description id integer Unique entry ID action string Permission action identifier (see actions table above) levels array List of Level IDs this permission applies to. Empty array means it applies to all levels. group integer Group ID this permission is assigned to

docs.title: Retrieve a Permission Matrix Entry
docs.text:
• GET /api/permissionmatrix/{id}/
    • Retrieves a single permission matrix entry.

Note: The permission matrix is managed via Django Admin. The API does not support creating, updating, or deleting entries.

docs.title: How Permission Checks Work
docs.text:
When the system checks if a user has a specific permission:

  1. It finds all PermissionMatrix entries where the action matches and the user belongs to the associated group.
  2. If the entry has no levels attached (empty array), the permission applies to all levels.
  3. If the entry has specific levels, the permission only applies when the target member/trip is at one of those levels.
  4. Superusers bypass all permission checks.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: Get started with the AD4x4 API in 5 minutes. This guide is aimed at API consumers (frontend / mobile / integration developers). For running the Django backend itself — installing Python, configuring .env, running migrations, and starting the Huey background-task consumer — see the repository root README.md.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Backend running at http://localhost:8000 (see repo README.md for setup) or production at https://ap.ad4x4.com
  • Authentication: JWT Bearer token
  • Time zone: Asia/Dubai (UTC+4)

docs.title: Step 1: Authenticate
docs.text: The API uses JWT access + refresh tokens (via djangorestframework-simplejwt). You get both from a single login call, put the access token in every request, and call the refresh endpoint when the access token expires. Full detail — including rotation semantics, session management, and error codes — lives in API Concepts → Authentication.

docs.title: Log in and get your token pair
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/auth/login/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "login": "your_username_or_email",
    "password": "your_password"
  }'

login accepts either a username or an email (case-insensitive). POST /api/token/ is an alias that accepts the same body and returns the same shape.

Response (wrapped in the project's unified envelope like every other endpoint):

{
  "success": true,
  "message": {
    "access": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
    "refresh": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
  }
}

Store both tokens. The access token goes in the Authorization header; the refresh token is used to get a new access token when the current one expires.

docs.title: Use the access token in requests
docs.text:
curl -X GET http://localhost:8000/api/trips/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"

docs.title: Refresh an expired access token
docs.text:
Default access-token lifetime is 24 hours; refresh-token lifetime is 30 days. When an authenticated request returns 401, call:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/token/refresh/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"refresh": "YOUR_REFRESH_TOKEN"}'

The response contains a new access token AND a new refresh token:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": {
    "access": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
    "refresh": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
  }
}

⚠️ Refresh tokens rotate on use. The old refresh token is immediately blacklisted by the server. You must overwrite your stored refresh token with whatever the refresh response returns. Using the same refresh token twice will give you 401 from then on.

docs.title: Log out
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/auth/logout/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"refresh": "YOUR_REFRESH_TOKEN"}'

This blacklists only the supplied refresh token — other devices stay logged in. Use POST /api/auth/logout-all/ (no body) to kill every session for the user instead. See API Concepts → Authentication for the session-listing endpoint and the full logout semantics.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text: To ensure the stability and reliability of the AD4x4 API, we have implemented rate limiting at two levels: Nginx and Django REST Framework (DRF).

docs.title: Nginx Rate Limiting
docs.text: The rate limiting is configured in the Nginx default.conf.template file. The current limit is set to 100 requests per minute per IP address for most API endpoints, with stricter limits on registration endpoints.

docs.title: Django DRF Rate Limiting
docs.text:
The API also implements Django REST Framework throttling:

User Type Rate Anonymous users 100 requests/minute Authenticated users 200 requests/minute

docs.title: HTTP 429 Response
docs.text:
If you exceed the rate limit, the API will respond with an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests status code. When you receive this response, you should:

  • Stop sending requests: Do not send any more requests until the rate limit window has reset.
  • Inform the user: Display a message to the user indicating that they have exceeded the rate limit and should try again later.
  • Implement backoff: Consider implementing an exponential backoff strategy to gradually reduce the rate of your requests.

docs.title: Sponsorships
docs.text: The sponsorship system manages club sponsors and their associated branding assets. Sponsors are displayed on the frontend based on priority and active date range.

docs.title: Model Overview
docs.text: Field Type Description id Integer Unique identifier title CharField(100) Sponsor name description TextField Sponsor details or slogan priority Integer Display order (lower = higher priority) image ImageField Sponsor logo start_date DateField When sponsorship becomes active (default: today) end_date DateField When sponsorship expires (optional)

docs.title: List Active Sponsors
docs.text:
• GET /api/sponsors/
  • Authentication: Not required (public endpoint)
  • Pagination: Disabled

Note: The endpoint is /api/sponsors/ (not /api/sponsorships/).

Filtering: Only sponsors where end_date is null OR end_date > today are returned.

Ordering: Results are sorted by priority (ascending).

Response:

Returns a plain array (no pagination wrapper, no success/message envelope):

[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "title": "OffRoad Pro",
        "description": "Premium off-road equipment",
        "priority": 10,
        "image": "/media/avatars/2026/01/sponsor_abc123.jpg"
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "title": "Desert Tires",
        "description": "All-terrain tires for extreme conditions",
        "priority": 20,
        "image": "/media/avatars/2026/01/sponsor_def456.jpg"
    }
]

docs.title: Active Sponsor Check
docs.text:
A sponsor is considered active when:

end_date is None OR end_date > today

docs.title: Priority Ordering
docs.text: Lower priority values appear first in the list. Example: - Priority 10: Appears before priority 20 - Priority 100: Appears last

docs.title: File Upload Path
docs.text: Logos are stored at: avatars/{YYYY}/{MM}/{filename}

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
1. Homepage Banner: Display top 3-5 sponsors by priority
  2. Sponsor Gallery: Full list of all active sponsors
  3. Footer: Persistent sponsor logos

docs.title: Authorizing with a Bearer Token
docs.text:
To test the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI, you'll need to obtain a JWT access token and authorize your requests.

  1. Log in: Send a POST request to /api/auth/login/ with a login (username or email) and password. POST /api/token/ is an alias that accepts the same body. The response is wrapped in the project's unified envelope: json { "success": true, "message": { "access": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...", "refresh": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." } } Grab message.access for the next step. Keep message.refresh somewhere safe if you want to test the refresh flow.

  2. Authorize in Swagger:

    • Click the "Authorize" button at the top-right of the Swagger page.
    • In the dialog that appears, enter the word Bearer followed by a space and then the access token you received in the previous step. For example: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
    • Click "Authorize" to save the token.

Access tokens are valid for 24 hours (configurable via ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES); refresh tokens last 30 days (REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS). When the access token expires, hit POST /api/token/refresh/ with the refresh token to get a fresh pair. Refresh tokens rotate on use — the response returns a new refresh token and blacklists the old one, so always store whatever the refresh endpoint hands back. Full detail in API Concepts → Authentication.

Once you've authorized, you can make requests to any of the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI.
