docs.title: Top 10 highest-impact fixes (sorted by what to do this week)
docs.text: # Title File:line Severity Blast radius Frontend impact 2-line recommendation 1 Gate LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet behind a permission matrix check api/views/views_logbook.py:26-29 critical medium low Switch to ReadOnlyModelViewSet or add a permission class that checks SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS and forces signed_by=request.user. Any member can currently write arbitrary skill rows that drive upgrade eligibility. 2 Fix wrong-arity Huey call on trip cancellation notifications api/views/viewstrip.py:436-439 + api/services/tripregistration_service.py:49,58 critical narrow none Create a TripRegistrationCancellationReason row and pass that single object instead of (user, trip). Cancel/remove notifications currently throw TypeError inside the worker, retry twice, then drop silently. 3 Upgrade Django to 6.0.4 + bundled CVE bumps requirements.txt critical wide none Patch Django 6.0.1 → 6.0.4, cryptography 46.0.7, PyJWT 2.12.0, Pillow 12.2.0 in one PR. Closes 13 Django CVEs (two SQL-injection) plus image-upload buffer overflow and PyJWT crit header bypass. 4 Wrap every Huey enqueue in transaction.on_commit api/views/*, api/signals.py, api/services/tripregistrationservice.py critical medium none Zero matches for on_commit in the whole repo. Enqueues fire before the surrounding transaction commits, so Huey tasks race the writer and read rolled-back state. One-line fix per call site. 5 Make upgrade approve/decline atomic + re-check eligibility api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:106-127 critical medium medium Wrap in transaction.atomic + select_for_update(['level']); guard against downgrade (applicant.level.numeric_level >= target_level.numeric_level); use update_fields=['level']. Currently partial failures leave the member half-promoted or downgrade an already-higher-level member. 6 Cut ClubNews double-send + immutability trap on partial failure api/services/notification_service.py:125-134 critical narrow medium Flip to SENT only after every channel succeeds; record per-channel delivery. Right now a partial failure sets the row immutable-but-undelivered, and retries fan-out again producing duplicate emails. 7 Fix set_primary vehicle endpoint wiring + schema gen api/views/views_vehicle.py + ad4x4/urls.py:205 high narrow high Convert to @action(detail=True, methods=['post']); remove the manual as_view() in urls.py. The schema warning and Flutter path may need to change once the router re-mounts it. 8 Close the capacity race on trip registration api/views/viewstrip.py:300-301 + api/services/tripregistration_service.py:14-26 high narrow low with transaction.atomic(): Trip.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=trip.pk); re-check capacity. Two simultaneous registers can both slip through. 9 Gate MemberViewSet.list + /api/members/ list endpoints behind SEARCH_MEMBERS api/views/views_member.py:116-154 high narrow medium list returns the full member directory with PII to any authenticated user. Add HasSearchMembersPermission to list/retrieve, or split into a scoped serializer. May 403 previously-allowed clients. 10 Fix HERE Maps cache TTL unit inconsistency api/services/heremapsservice.py:115 vs :169 vs :150 high narrow none Resolved in the working tree: both memory-cache paths now use *60, and DB expiry uses timedelta(minutes=...), matching the model field's minutes unit.

docs.title: F-01: Gate LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet behind a permission matrix check
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-logbook.md (F5)
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:26-29
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: permission_classes = (permissions.IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly,). Any authenticated member can POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE LogbookSkillReference rows setting member, trip, signed_by, entered_by to arbitrary values — bypassing CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES/SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS.
  • Blast radius: medium — affects a ViewSet, requires migration if constraints are tightened, Graphify rebuild, schema regen. Logbook signatures are the evidence layer for level upgrades.
  • Frontend impact: low — if the client never used write methods on this ViewSet (expected), nothing changes. If it did, previously-allowed calls start returning 403.
  • Recommendation: Switch to ReadOnlyModelViewSet (preferred — the writes happen via LogbookEntryViewSet._manage_logbook_skill_references). Alternatively add a permission class that verifies SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS against the trip's level and forces signed_by = request.user server-side.

docs.title: F-02: CancelTripRegistration and service callers pass (user, trip) to Huey tasks expecting a single TripRegistrationCancellationReason
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-trip-flow.md + raw/08-async-tasks.md
  • File:line: api/views/viewstrip.py:436,439; api/services/tripregistration_service.py:49,58
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification(user, trip) — signature in api/background.py:32,37 declares one positional cancellation argument; downstream NotificationManager reads cancellation.member, .trip, .id. Every other caller (RemoveMemberFromTripRegistration) builds the cancellation row correctly.
  • Blast radius: narrow — fix in two call sites + write a test that executes the task. No migration, no schema change.
  • Frontend impact: none — the HTTP response already returns success; only the background notification is missing.
  • Recommendation: Build a TripRegistrationCancellationReason in each path (SELF_CANCELLED reason for self-cancel) and pass it. Add a pytest case that invokes the task synchronously in immediate mode to catch regressions.

docs.title: F-03: Django 6.0.1 exposes the backend to 13 CVEs including SQL-injection in QuerySet.order_by() and FilteredRelation
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/11-dependencies.md
  • File:line: requirements.txt (Django==6.0.1)
  • Category: cve-dep
  • Evidence: pip-audit flags CVE-2026-1312 (order_by alias SQLi), CVE-2026-1287 (FilteredRelation SQLi), CVE-2026-4292/4277 (admin forgery), CVE-2026-33033 (multipart perf), CVE-2026-25674 (file storage race), plus 7 more. The mobile app and web portal both hit /api/trips/search/ and /api/members/search/ with query params that can reach order_by.
  • Blast radius: wide — patch release, but surface-area is the whole framework. Requires regression-test run; django-oidc-provider 0.9.0 compatibility to verify (per §15).
  • Frontend impact: none — patch-level Django release.
  • Recommendation: Single PR bumping Django==6.0.4 + cryptography==46.0.7 + PyJWT==2.12.0 + Pillow==12.2.0 + requests==2.33.0 + pyasn1==0.6.3 + pygments==2.20.0 + pytest==9.0.3 + python-dotenv==1.2.2. Run pytest, manage.py check --deploy, regenerate schema.yml, smoke-test /openid/. Also grep order_by( call sites consuming request.query_params and add a whitelist.

docs.title: F-04: Zero transaction.on_commit usage in the whole repo — every Huey enqueue races the writer
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/08-async-tasks.md + raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-02) + raw/06-code-review-upgrade-flow.md (F20) + raw/06-code-review-trip-flow.md
  • File:line: api/signals.py:66,92,161,178,184,189,195; api/views/viewstrip.py:107,516,517,541; api/views/viewsupgraderequest.py:126; api/views/viewsfeedback.py:34; api/services/tripregistration_service.py:39,49,58
  • Category: on-commit
  • Evidence: Grep for on_commit across the repo returns zero matches. Enqueues fire from inside post_save signals and DRF views wrapped by ATOMIC_REQUESTS. On rollback the worker picks up the job and either reads rolled-back state (e.g., Trip.DoesNotExist) or sends a notification about something that didn't happen (member notified they were registered for a trip that was rolled back).
  • Blast radius: medium — touches many files, but each change is one line. Needs a §15 gotcha entry.
  • Frontend impact: none — the HTTP response shape is unchanged; only downstream behaviour becomes correct.
  • Recommendation: Wrap every enqueue in transaction.on_commit(lambda: my_task(pk)). Highest priority sites: signals, trip-registration service, feedback create. Add a §15 gotcha. Consider a lint/grep CI check to prevent regressions.

docs.title: F-05: handle_upgrade_request_verdict is non-atomic, doesn't re-check eligibility, and writes full-row on Member — can downgrade an already-promoted user
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-upgrade-flow.md (F1, F10, F11)
  • File:line: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:106-127
  • Category: tx + data-integrity + race
  • Evidence: Four sequential writes (status/verdict_date save, applicant.level=, applicant.groups.add, applicant.save()) with no atomic(). Eligibility is checked only at creation; between create and approve, auto_upgrade_service may have promoted the member to a higher level. Approve blindly overwrites level = target_level, which can downgrade. The full-row applicant.save() also clobbers concurrent writes from LastVisitedMiddleware and trip_count signals.
  • Blast radius: medium — service-layer refactor + view change + pytest case. No migration. Touches the UpgradeRequest lifecycle which is central to member progression.
  • Frontend impact: medium — approving an upgrade that would downgrade the member now returns 409 (not 200). Clients should surface that message.
  • Recommendation: python with transaction.atomic(): upgrade_request = UpgradeRequest.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=pk) applicant = Member.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=upgrade_request.applicant_id) if applicant.level.numeric_level >= upgrade_request.target_level.numeric_level: return Response({"success": False, "message": "already_at_or_above_level"}, status=409) applicant.level = upgrade_request.target_level applicant.save(update_fields=['level']) applicant.groups.add(upgrade_request.target_level.auto_group) upgrade_request.status = ApprovalStatus.APPROVED upgrade_request.save(update_fields=['status','verdict_date','final_approver']) transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_upgrade_request_handled_notification(upgrade_request.id))

docs.title: F-06: send_club_wide_news flips status to SENT even when channels fail — immutability trap + double-send on retry
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-01) + raw/08-async-tasks.md (medium idempotency)
  • File:line: api/services/notification_service.py:125-134
  • Category: idempotency + data-integrity
  • Evidence: The per-channel fan-out wraps each dispatch in try/except Exception, swallows, continues, then unconditionally data.status = ClubNewsStatus.SENT; data.save(). If email sends to 500 of 1000 members and FCM then raises, the row is SENT (immutable per §15) and cannot be resent or corrected. On retry of the outer send_club_news task (retries=2), every channel re-fans-out to every member — duplicate emails.
  • Blast radius: narrow — single service file; no migration.
  • Frontend impact: medium — members receive duplicate club news emails/push. Admin has no retry path short of DB surgery.
  • Recommendation: Track per-channel delivery (e.g., ClubNewsDelivery row per (news_id, channel) or a set field on ClubNews). Flip SENT only when all channels report success. Skip already-delivered channels on retry. Let the outer task re-raise on real failures so Huey's retry policy actually fires.

docs.title: F-07: set_primary vehicle endpoint wired as manual as_view(), not as @action
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/01-system-check.md + raw/02-endpoint-drift.md + raw/06-code-review-member-flow.md
  • File:line: api/views/views_vehicle.py:104-116 + ad4x4/urls.py:205
  • Category: routing + doc-drift
  • Evidence: VehicleViewSet.set_primary lacks @action(detail=True, methods=['post']). It's registered as VehicleViewSet.as_view({'post': 'set_primary'}) in urls.py:205. Consequences: @extend_schema at line 99 is dead, self.action is only right by accident, drf-spectacular can't introspect the queryset (schema warning W001), permissions/throttles may not fire as expected.
  • Blast radius: narrow — one decorator + one URL entry change.
  • Frontend impact: high — if the router decides a different URL path, the Flutter client must update. Today's URL api/vehicles/<int:pk>/set_primary/ should be kept as url_path='set_primary'. Coordinate with mobile team.
  • Recommendation: Decorate with @action(detail=True, methods=['post'], url_path='set_primary'), remove the manual entry from ad4x4/urls.py, and verify the generated path matches the old one.

docs.title: F-08: trip.cut_off < datetime.datetime.now() violates USE_TZ=False convention
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-trip-flow.md
  • File:line: api/views/views_trip.py:294,370
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: CLAUDE.md §15 says "Never use datetime.datetime.now() — use django.utils.timezone.now()." Works today but is one timezone-aware migration away from silently breaking cutoff checks. Sibling offense in api/models/models_upgraderequest.py:50 (UpgradeRequest.save() sets verdict_date with datetime.datetime.now() imported from django.db.models.functions.datetime, which is the database function namespace, not Python's datetime — likely works only because it re-exports the module). And api/views/views_member.py:668 uses datetime.today().
  • Blast radius: narrow — four edits + grep for any other occurrences.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Replace with from django.utils import timezone and timezone.now() in all three files. Add a lint rule (ruff custom, or flake8-djangoisms) to fail new occurrences.

docs.title: F-09: RegisterForTrip permission branch skips every validation for permission holders
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-trip-flow.md
  • File:line: api/views/views_trip.py:273-281
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: Users with EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS bypass approval status, level requirement, cutoff, capacity, and duplicate-registration checks. Admin force-registration has a dedicated endpoint (ForceRegisterForTrip) so the bypass here is undocumented.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: medium — admin clients may have relied on the silent bypass. Keep the bypass only for bypass_capacity=True flag if it's intentional, or route admin-initiated registration through the dedicated endpoint.
  • Recommendation: Remove the early branch or keep only bypass_capacity. At minimum keep trip_already_registered check above the branch.

docs.title: F-10: Capacity race on concurrent trip registrations
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: medium
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-trip-flow.md
  • File:line: api/views/viewstrip.py:300-301 + api/services/tripregistration_service.py:14-26
  • Category: tx
  • Evidence: if trip.registered.count() >= trip.capacity followed by non-atomic add_to_registered. Two concurrent requests both see count == capacity - 1 and both succeed. add_users_from_waitlist has the same loop-without-lock pattern.
  • Blast radius: narrow — service change + pytest case with threading.
  • Frontend impact: low — over-capacity events today return 200; post-fix one of them returns 409.
  • Recommendation: Lock the trip row with select_for_update inside atomic(), re-check capacity under lock, or add a CheckConstraint/UniqueConstraint for registration count.

docs.title: F-11: add_users_from_waitlist drops the waitlist entry's vehicle
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-trip-flow.md
  • File:line: api/services/tripregistrationservice.py:39
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: trip.registered.add(user, through_defaults={'trip': trip}) doesn't forward TripWaitlist.vehicle. AcceptMemberFromWaitlist.post (manual path) correctly reads waitlist_entry.vehicle. Automatic promotion from waitlist silently loses the member's chosen vehicle.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: low — Flutter shows the wrong vehicle (no vehicle) for auto-promoted members until the member re-selects.
  • Recommendation: Forward entry.vehicle via through_defaults — diff sketch already in the raw finding.

docs.title: F-12: MemberViewSet.list/retrieve exposes full member directory with PII to any authenticated user
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-member-flow.md
  • File:line: api/views/views_member.py:116-154
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: get_permissions returns IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly for list/retrieve, so any logged-in user (and potentially anonymous, though throttles will catch them) can GET /api/members/ and receive BasicMemberSerializer output. ActionChoice.SEARCH_MEMBERS exists and gates MemberSearch — inconsistency.
  • Blast radius: medium — ViewSet change + pytest + possibly a new matrix row.
  • Frontend impact: medium — clients without SEARCH_MEMBERS will see 403 on list. Verify Flutter does not call the raw list endpoint (expected: yes, for dropdowns — add a CHOICES_MEMBERS scope or expose a narrow-directory endpoint).
  • Recommendation: Gate list/retrieve with HasSearchMembersPermission or equivalent. Consider a scoped serializer that drops phone/email.

docs.title: F-13: Vehicle limit TOCTOU on concurrent POST /api/vehicles/
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-member-flow.md
  • File:line: api/serializers/serializersvehicle.py:47-57 (invoked from api/views/viewsvehicle.py:63-66)
  • Category: tx
  • Evidence: Count + create not transactional, no select_for_update, no unique constraint. Two simultaneous POSTs race past vehicle_limit_per_member.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none — additional requests today succeed; post-fix they 400.
  • Recommendation: Wrap perform_create in transaction.atomic() + lock the member row; or push the check into a DB constraint.

docs.title: F-14: Member-level list endpoints N+1 on level FK and groups M2M
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-member-flow.md + raw/07-performance-probes.md
  • File:line: api/views/views_member.py:123, 555; also LeadSearch/ActiveTripLeads
  • Category: n+1
  • Evidence: Member.objects.all() without .select_related('level').prefetch_related('groups'). BasicMemberSerializer renders level per-row; page_size up to 500 means 500+ extra queries on one page.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none — response shape unchanged, latency improves.
  • Recommendation: Override get_queryset on MemberViewSet, MemberSearch, LeadSearch, ActiveTripLeads to prefetch level + groups. Add assertNumQueries regression tests.

docs.title: F-15: HasCreateUpgradeRequestForOtherPermission and upgrade-request comment permissions raise on unknown IDs → 500
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-auth-perms.md (F-08, F-09)
  • File:line: api/permissions.py:245-251, 261-275
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: Level.objects.get(id=level_id) with no DoesNotExist handler — a client posting {"target_level": 99999} crashes the permission check into a 500. Sibling HasCreateUpgradeRequestForSelfPermission catches the same exception. HasViewUpgradeRequestCommentPermission (line 264) has the same bug on UpgradeRequest.objects.get.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: low — today 500, post-fix 403. Flutter error surface becomes more predictable.
  • Recommendation: try/except DoesNotExist: return False to mirror the sibling. Replace == None with is None.

docs.title: F-16: LogbookEntryViewSet / LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet classic N+1 on list
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-logbook.md (F1) + raw/07-performance-probes.md
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:27, 33
  • Category: n+1
  • Evidence: LogbookEntry.objects.all().order_by('id') + serializer with fields = '__all__'. Three FKs + one M2M fire per-row queries; at page_size 500 the list endpoint balloons to ~2000 queries.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none — latency improvement only.
  • Recommendation: .select_related('trip', 'member', 'signed_by').prefetch_related('skills_verified'); same pattern for LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet.

docs.title: F-17: _manage_logbook_skill_references deletes across all entries for (member, trip) and preserves no history
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-logbook.md (F3, F4) + raw/03-model-schema.md
  • File:line: api/views/viewslogbook.py:139-158; api/models/modelslogbook.py
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: Filter is LogbookSkillReference.objects.filter(member=member, trip=trip).delete() — not scoped by logbook_entry. If two marshals each write entries for the same (member, trip), saving the second wipes the first's skill references. Also: no UniqueConstraint on (member, trip, logbook_skill), so duplicates are possible if any code path bypasses the delete-then-insert pattern.
  • Blast radius: medium — needs migration for unique constraint + refactor to update_or_create.
  • Frontend impact: low.
  • Recommendation: Add UniqueConstraint(fields=['member','trip','logbook_skill'], name='uniq_skillref_per_trip_member') in a migration. Replace the delete-then-insert with update_or_create so marshal timestamps are preserved. Enforce one LogbookEntry per (member, trip) at the model layer.

docs.title: F-18: _manage_logbook_skill_references is itself N+1 in the skill loop and silently ignores unknown skill IDs
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-logbook.md (F2)
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:136-158
  • Category: n+1 + data-integrity
  • Evidence: LogbookSkill.objects.get(id=skill_id) inside a for loop — 2N queries per N skills. Unknown skill IDs log a warning and return 201 — client thinks the skill was recorded.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: low — unknown skill IDs start returning 400.
  • Recommendation: LogbookSkill.objects.in_bulk(skill_ids); raise ValidationError('one_or_more_skills_not_found') on mismatch; bulk_create the references.

docs.title: F-19: LogbookEntryViewSet.perform_update doesn't force signed_by
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-logbook.md (F6)
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:199-216
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: perform_create sets serializer.validated_data['signed_by'] = self.request.user; perform_update doesn't. Serializer uses fields='__all__', so a PATCH can set signed_by to anyone.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Set signed_by = self.request.user in perform_update too, or mark read-only in a dedicated serializer (recommended).

docs.title: F-20: TripLogbookEntryCreateView creates LogbookEntry without LogbookSkillReference rows
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-logbook.md (F10)
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:264-326
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: Creates LogbookEntry with entry.skills_verified.set(...) but never creates LogbookSkillReference rows. Every LogbookSkillReference-based report (upgrade eligibility, auto-upgrade) misses entries created via this endpoint.
  • Blast radius: narrow — call the same _manage_logbook_skill_references used by the other viewset, or delete the duplicate view.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Invoke _manage_logbook_skill_references(entry, request.user) after skills_verified.set(...), or delete the duplicate view and use the main ViewSet.

docs.title: F-21: Voting endpoint TOCTOU on status + non-atomic three-M2M mutation
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-upgrade-flow.md (F2, F3)
  • File:line: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:232-257
  • Category: race
  • Evidence: Reads upgrade_request.status, mutates three M2Ms, then unconditionally sets status back to IN_PROGRESS. A concurrent approval can be overwritten. Mid-request failure can count a voter in two buckets.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: low.
  • Recommendation: select_for_update inside atomic, re-check status under lock, .save(update_fields=['status']). Longer term: single-vote through-model with UniqueConstraint(fields=['upgrade_request','member']).

docs.title: F-22: Auto-upgrade + auto-downgrade race with manual approval
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-upgrade-flow.md (F4, F5)
  • File:line: api/services/autoupgradeservice.py:30-49, 77-94
  • Category: race
  • Evidence: handle_logbook_entry_created reads member.level_id, writes member.level, no lock or atomic block — can race with manual approval. handle_logbook_entry_deleted counts remaining entries after delete; two concurrent deletes of the last two entries can both see count==0 and both downgrade.
  • Blast radius: medium.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: atomic() + select_for_update on Member, re-count inside lock, save(update_fields=['level']).

docs.title: F-23: FCM devices fetched without batching and duplicate audience queries
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-09)
  • File:line: api/services/push_notifications.py (multiple)
  • Category: n+1 + style
  • Evidence: devices.count() then devices.send_message(...) — two full scans. data.levels.count() == 0 and data.levels.count() == 0 duplicated condition (copy-paste) in three files. Email and push audience resolution differs from store notification audience (store filters by last_user_activity, others don't).
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Consolidate audience resolution into a helper shared across channels; cache count; drop the duplicated condition.

docs.title: F-24: Per-channel Huey tasks have no idempotency — retries duplicate sends
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-03)
  • File:line: api/services/*notifications.py + api/services/storenotifications.py:30
  • Category: idempotency
  • Evidence: Per-channel delivery now goes through deliver_notification_once_for_channel(...), which keys retries by the channel identity plus notification payload. Already-sent channels are skipped on retry while the failing channel is retried.
  • Blast radius: medium — touches the notification manager and delivery cache keying.
  • Frontend impact: low — fewer duplicate notifications.
  • Recommendation: Keep the per-channel delivery wrapper in sync with any new notification channels; if channel identity ever becomes dynamic, add an explicit channel-key property.

docs.title: F-25: ClubNewsNotificationAPIView.post enqueues raw dict instead of persisted ClubNews
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-04) + raw/08-async-tasks.md
  • File:line: api/views/views_pushnotification.py:26-30
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: send_club_news(serializer.validated_data) — a plain dict. send_club_wide_news ends with data.save() which AttributeErrors on a dict. The serializer is serializers.Serializer, not ModelSerializer, so validated_data is a naive dict without matching ClubNews fields.
  • Blast radius: narrow — verify whether this endpoint is reachable in production (may be dead code) and either remove or fix.
  • Frontend impact: depends on whether admin UI uses it — verify.
  • Recommendation: If live: replace with ClubNews.objects.create(**validated_data); transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_club_news(news.id)). If dead: remove.

docs.title: F-26: NotificationManager swallows every channel exception → Huey's retry policy never fires
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-05) + raw/08-async-tasks.md
  • File:line: api/services/notification_service.py:71-192
  • Category: error-handling
  • Evidence: Every send_* wraps dispatch in try/except Exception + logger.error + logger.exception + continue. Huey's @task(retries=2, retry_delay=300) never sees failures. Double-logging (.error + .exception) inflates Sentry noise.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Let exceptions propagate to Huey; log once with logger.exception(...). Fix typo notificiation across several files while here.

docs.title: F-27: Dry-run logs leak PII (full email body, phone, address) at INFO level
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-06, F-07)
  • File:line: api/services/emailnotifications.py:37,169,206,239; api/services/telegramnotifications.py:171
  • Category: info-leak
  • Evidence: logger.info(f'Dry run: Email sent to {msg.to} with subject {msg.subject} and content {html_content}'). Default notification_dry_run=True in dev means every CI/dev log has full PII for every notification. Telegram feedback formatter logs email + phone + first 200 chars of user message even outside dry-run.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Dry-run logs: subject + recipient count only. Telegram: log feedback.id + feedback.user.username at INFO; keep formatted message local to bot.send_message.

docs.title: F-28: EmailMultiAlternatives reused across iterations appends HTML alternatives and time.sleep blocks Huey worker
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: medium
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-notifications.md (F-10)
  • File:line: api/services/email_notifications.py:19-40
  • Category: data-integrity + perf
  • Evidence: msg.attach_alternative(html_content, "text/html") inside the per-user loop keeps appending alternatives — by the Nth user the message has N identical HTML blobs. time.sleep(email_sleep_period_ms/1000) blocks the Huey worker thread; 1000 users × 100ms = 100s of blocked worker.
  • Blast radius: narrow — service refactor.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Instantiate EmailMultiAlternatives per-user inside the loop; replace time.sleep with Huey's delay= scheduling or SMTP-level rate limiter.

docs.title: F-29: Gallery webhook: settings local shadows django.conf.settings
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-misc-services.md (finding 1)
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:51,119,195,249 (every method)
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: Module imports from django.conf import settings, then each method rebinds settings = get_global_settings(). A maintainer adding settings.DEBUG or settings.GALLERY_API_TOKEN in the body silently reads ConfigurableSettings — AttributeError or wrong value.
  • Blast radius: narrow — rename-only change.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Rename the local to config; keep the Django settings name intact.

docs.title: F-30: Gallery webhook raise Exception(response) causes retry storms and leaks auth headers
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-misc-services.md (findings 2, 3)
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:98,166,228,282
  • Category: retry + info-leak
  • Evidence: Non-200 responses raise Exception(response). (a) Exception is too broad — Huey retries 4xx for 6 hours. (b) The raised object is a Response — when Huey repr/pickles it for the retry queue, body and Authorization: Bearer header may be serialised. response.text is also logged verbatim.
  • Blast radius: narrow — service refactor.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Define GalleryAPIError(Exception) with status_code + sanitised message. Classify 4xx (except 408/429) as permanent (don't retry); 5xx/408/429/timeout/connection as transient. Never include response.text in logs without scrubbing Bearer <token>.

docs.title: F-31: Gallery webhook lacks idempotency — retries can create duplicate galleries
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: medium
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-misc-services.md (finding 11) + raw/08-async-tasks.md
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:33-108; api/background.py:96-103
  • Category: idempotency
  • Evidence: create_gallery_for_trip_task retries 6 times. If the remote POST succeeds but the local trip.save(update_fields=['gallery_id']) fails, next retry creates a second gallery; the local gallery_id ends up referencing only the latest. Task has no if trip.gallery_id: return guard at the top.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Add if trip.gallery_id: return guard. Mirror in delete_/restore_gallery_for_trip_task. Longer-term: pass an idempotency key derived from trip_id + created_at; have the Gallery API return existing gallery on duplicate.

docs.title: F-32: HERE Maps cache TTL unit inconsistency → effectively 4-year cache
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/06-code-review-misc-services.md (finding 6) + raw/07-performance-probes.md
  • File:line: api/services/heremapsservice.py:115 vs :169 vs :150
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: Field here_maps_cache_duration is documented as minutes (default 1440). The working tree now uses *60 for both memory-cache writes and timedelta(minutes=...) for DB expiry, so the default is 1 day rather than 1440 days.
  • Blast radius: narrow.
  • Frontend impact: none.
  • Recommendation: Keep here_maps_cache_duration as a minutes field and preserve the regression coverage in tests/test_here_maps_service_unit.py.

docs.title: F-33: Gallery tasks swallow Trip.DoesNotExist and Exception — permanent failures, no retry
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Source step: raw/08-async-tasks.md
  • File:line: api/background.py:107-110,122-126,138-142,154-158
  • Category: error-handling
  • Evidence: create_gallery_for_trip_task logs-and-returns on both Trip.DoesNotExist and Exception — Huey never retries even when the write hasn't committed yet (exact symptom of missing on_commit). Other gallery tasks do raise Exception(str(e)) which strips the traceback.

docs.title: Positives verified (short bullet list)
docs.text:
• JWT rotation + blacklist semantics match §7 exactly. Password-change-blacklists-all, logout-all, logout-single, session list + selective revocation all behave as documented.
  • Middleware order matches §4 and handles CamelCase in/out correctly.
  • Production security block (if not DEV: SSL/HSTS/secure-cookies/etc.) is complete and correct.
  • No SQL injection vectors in auth or login lookups — all ORM-parameterized.
  • CORS/CSRF match §11. Asia/Dubai + USE_TZ=False + HUEY.utc=False are consistent.
  • Layering invariants hold: models ← services ← views. No import cycles. (One soft services → background upward dependency — noted in raw/09.)
  • PermissionMatrix.has_permission empty-levels semantics match the §15 gotcha (confirmed in raw/06-auth-perms F-12).
  • NotificationLog.save() immutability + ClubNews.save() immutability on SENT are enforced at the model level as documented.
  • No merge migrations (clean rebase history).
  • VehicleViewSet.get_queryset correctly scopes by request.user — no cross-tenant reads.
  • Member anonymize_data is only ever called from the nightly deletion task (confirmed in raw/06-member-flow).

docs.title: F-05 — Upgrade verdict atomicity + downgrade guard
docs.text:
• Status: RESOLVED

  • Evidence: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:114, 133-137: python upgrade_request = UpgradeRequest.objects.filter(id=pk).select_for_update()... applicant = Member.objects.filter(pk=applicant_id).select_for_update().first() if applicant.level and applicant.level.numeric_level >= upgrade_request.target_level.numeric_level: return Response({'success': False, 'message': 'applicant_already_at_or_above_target_level'}, status=409) Row-level lock on both upgrade request and applicant; explicit 409 CONFLICT if the request would downgrade.

docs.title: F-06 — ClubNews SENT/ERROR status
docs.text:
• Status: RESOLVED
  • Commit: 12b4999
  • Evidence: api/services/notification_service.py:135-148: python first_exception = None for channel in self._channels: try: channel.send_club_wide_news(data) except Exception as e: if first_exception is None: first_exception = e logger.exception(e) data.status = ClubNewsStatus.ERROR if first_exception else ClubNewsStatus.SENT data.save() if first_exception: raise first_exception The news record only flips to SENT if every channel succeeds; partial failures mark it ERROR. Re-raising the first exception means Huey's retry policy fires.
  • Caveat: Per-channel delivery state is still not tracked — if a retry runs, all channels re-fan-out, so users who received the first attempt may get a duplicate. The Codex review flagged this; Mikkel's self-report lists it as still outstanding.

docs.title: F-04 — transaction.on_commit coverage
docs.text:
• Status: PARTIAL — ~10 of ~14 enqueue sites now use on_commit
  • What's done: All enqueues in api/views/views_trip.py (8 sites), api/views/views_upgraderequest.py (1 site), and api/services/trip_registration_service.py (1 site) are wrapped. See lines 109, 413, 420, 456, 467, 550, 551, 576.
  • What's missing: api/signals.py still has 6 direct task calls:
  • Line 66: send_upgrade_request_created_notification(instance) on UpgradeRequest post_save
  • Lines 161, 168, 178, 184, 189: 5 gallery task calls on Trip post_save
  • Line 195: send_new_trip_comment_notification_task(instance) on TripComment post_save
  • Risk: Signal handlers fire inside the transaction that created the row. If the transaction rolls back (validation error, integrity error, etc.), the task already fired — producing notifications for events that didn't happen or trying to create galleries for trips that don't exist.
  • Recommendation: Wrap each signal task enqueue in transaction.on_commit(...). One-line fix per site.

docs.title: F-12 — Member directory PII exposure
docs.text:
• Status: PARTIAL — field-level redaction added; view-level gate still broad
  • What's done: api/serializers/serializers_member_base.py — ContactInfoMemberSerializer.to_representation hides phone, email, dob, ice_name, ice_phone unless the viewer has VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission or is viewing their own profile. Trip leads/deputies get contact info shown.
  • What's missing: MemberViewSet.list and retrieve still use IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly — any authenticated member can still enumerate all member IDs, usernames, first/last names, levels, trip counts. Codex review explicitly flagged this.
  • Risk: Primary impact is enumeration / directory scraping, not PII leak. But it does expose paid_member and last_visited timestamps.
  • Recommendation: Add a SEARCH_MEMBERS permission class to the ViewSet's get_permissions() for list+retrieve. Clients that need dropdowns should switch to /api/members/search/ or /leadsearch/ which are already permissioned.

docs.title: F-17 — Logbook skill reference delete-reinsert loses history
docs.text:
• Status: STILL PRESENT (now atomic, but underlying pattern unchanged)
  • What's done: The _manage_logbook_skill_references helper (line 136-158) is now called inside transaction.atomic(), so half-deleted state cannot leak. TripLogbookEntryCreateView also deletes and re-inserts inside a transaction.
  • What's missing: The delete-reinsert pattern itself is still destructive — if two marshals sign the same trip for the same member, the second one's save wipes the first's signatures. A unique constraint on (member, trip, logbook_skill) + update_or_create would preserve history.
  • Recommendation: Add the unique constraint in a migration, then switch to update_or_create. Low priority since both signers would be marshals writing the same set, but still a data-integrity concern.

docs.title: F-03 — Django + dependency CVEs — STILL COMPLETELY UNADDRESSED
docs.text:
• Severity: CRITICAL
  • Evidence: requirements.txt unchanged:
  • Django==6.0.1 (should be 6.0.4 — 13 CVEs including SQL injection)
  • cryptography==46.0.4 (should be 46.0.7 — buffer overflow)
  • PyJWT==2.11.0 (should be 2.12.0 — crit header bypass)
  • pillow==12.1.0 (should be 12.2.0 — PSD out-of-bounds write)
  • requests==2.32.5, pyasn1==0.6.2, Pygments==2.19.2, python-dotenv==1.2.1 — all unchanged
  • Why this matters: QuerySet.order_by() SQL injection is directly exploitable via /api/trips/search/ or any endpoint that reads order_by from query params. Recommend landing this before anything else — it's the lowest-risk, highest-impact fix (patch-level bumps, no API change).
  • Blast radius: medium-wide — requires a full regression test run.
  • Recommendation: Single PR bumping all 8 packages; run pytest; verify /openid/ endpoints (django-oidc-provider compat); regenerate schema.yml.

docs.title: Recommended next steps
docs.text:
1. First priority — land F-03 in a standalone PR. Single dep-bump PR. Test suite + manage.py check --deploy + regenerate schema.yml. Close 13 Django CVEs (including SQL injection) and 11 more across 7 other packages.
  2. Close out F-04 by wrapping the 6 remaining signal enqueues in transaction.on_commit. Ten-line change, no behaviour risk.
  3. Close F-12 view-level gate — add SEARCH_MEMBERS to MemberViewSet. Coordinate with Flutter/web before shipping (they may need to switch to /search/).
  4. Run the full pytest suite and verify. Mikkel's self-report says 101 passed on affected suites; a full run would catch any collateral damage.
  5. Update CLAUDE.md §15 with the new gotchas:
  6. "Trip cancellations must pass a TripRegistrationCancellationReason to the notification task"
  7. "Upgrade approval must re-check applicant level under lock"
  8. "notification_service channels now re-raise — exception-eats-exceptions is gone"
  9. Mark resolved findings in audit-report.md Status tracking table. Convert the 13 verified open rows to resolved <sha>.
  10. Tackle the next batch: F-07 (vehicle set_primary), F-13 (Vehicle TOCTOU), F-15 (permission 500s), F-21 (vote race), F-22 (auto-upgrade race). These are the remaining high findings with concrete exploit paths.

docs.title: Frontend Impact Analysis
docs.text:
Companion document to audit-report.md. Breaks down which audit findings require coordination with the Flutter mobile app, the web portal, the admin panel, the gallery service, or any other external integration.

Generated by filtering every finding in audit-report.md by its **Frontend impact:** tag.

docs.title: Numbers at a glance
docs.text:
Of 119 distinct findings in the full audit:

Frontend impact Count % none (pure server-side) 92 77% low (edge-case validation, transparent 400s) 18 15% medium (stricter permissions, tighter error semantics) 7 6% high (potential endpoint change) 1 1% depends (conditional on client usage) 1 1%

Headline: 77% of fixes are pure backend work. The remaining 23% need varying degrees of client awareness, and only one finding could require an endpoint rename.

docs.title: Must coordinate — Flutter PR should ship alongside the backend
docs.text: Finding Severity What changes for Flutter F-07 high vehicles/<pk>/set_primary/ is currently wired via manual as_view(). Refactor to a proper @action should keep the URL the same, but verify after the fix lands. If the router reassigns a different path, mobile needs a release. F-12 high GET /api/members/ stops returning the full member directory to non-privileged users. If Flutter uses this for dropdowns (trip lead picker, deputy selection), switch to /api/members/search/ or /api/members/leadsearch/ — both are already permissioned. F-09 high Permission holders no longer silently bypass trip registration validation. If admin-initiated registrations rely on the skip, add an explicit force=true flag server-side and update Flutter admin UI accordingly. F-05 critical Upgrade approve/decline may return 409 Conflict (not 200) when approval would downgrade an already-higher-level member. Surface the error message. F-06 critical Users may temporarily see duplicate club-news notifications during rollout while idempotency guard lands. No Flutter code change — support talking point only. F-37 medium Login error messages unified — "invalid credentials" regardless of whether the account exists or is disabled. If Flutter currently shows different UI per error, it becomes one error. F-56 medium ClubNews feed may hide items from lower-level users that were previously visible (fix closes a per-level gate bypass). App behavior is correct but feed gets shorter for some members — customer-support talking point.

docs.title: Nice-to-handle — low impact, app should already handle 400s
docs.text: Finding What changes F-50 Avatars over 2.5 MB now return 400 at the API instead of silent truncation. F-52 /api/members/<id>/payments stops crashing on JSON true/false. F-65 HERE Maps reverse-geocode returns cleaner error responses (was leaking raw exception strings, potentially including the API key). F-80 /api/notifications/ now paginates properly (was hard-sliced to 20). F-01 LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet writes now require SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS. Expected: Flutter only reads this ViewSet, so no change. If it writes, previously-allowed calls return 403. F-10 Capacity race fixed — concurrent registrations may now see a stricter 409/400 more often. Rare. F-11 Waitlist → registration now preserves the waitlist entry's vehicle. Response shape unchanged. F-15 Unknown upgrade-request ID no longer produces 500 — returns 404. F-17, F-18 Logbook skill references now preserve history across marshals — response shape unchanged, but reads may show more rows. F-21 Vote endpoint becomes atomic — behavior more consistent but shape unchanged. F-24 Notification delivery deduplicated on retry. Users may see fewer duplicate pushes. F-36 SessionsView.delete correctly rejects blacklisted keep_refresh tokens. Client should already treat this as "session invalid, re-login". F-49 Upgrade status transition guards prevent double-approval. Previously-allowed illegal transitions now return 400. F-51 LeadSearch missing level param now returns 400 cleanly instead of 500. F-53 /api/members/leadsearch and /api/members/activetripleads may return 403 for users without SEARCH_MEMBERS. F-55 ClubNewsNotificationAPIView now returns 403 instead of 200 for non-admins. F-63 ForceRegisterForTrip now returns 403 on permission denial instead of a silent 200. F-67 PATCH /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings semantics tightened — partial updates only modify specified fields.

Finding Severity Gallery-side requirement F-31 high If the fix adds an idempotency key (UUID in request header) to the create_gallery_for_trip webhook so retries don't create duplicate galleries, the gallery service must accept and honor that header. 1. Week 1 — server-only fixes (F-02, F-04, F-03 CVE bumps, all the N+1s, transaction boundaries, logging cleanup). Zero client impact. Easy to ship incrementally.
  2. Week 2 — permission tightenings (F-01, F-12, F-53, F-55, F-56). Announce to Flutter/web teams 2 weeks ahead. Ship backend with feature flag if the SEARCH_MEMBERS gate is scary.
  3. Week 3 — coordinated client release. Flutter + web ship their PRs referencing the new API contract. Submit to stores. Monitor crash reports and 403 rates.
  4. Week 4 — remaining mediums + lows. Gallery idempotency conversation fits here if it's happening.

docs.text:
• Lowest risk: CVE dep bumps (F-03, F-68). Drop-in patch releases.
  • Medium risk: Permission tightenings (F-01, F-12) — may surface clients we don't know about.
  • Highest risk: F-07 if the set_primary path changes under the feet of the Flutter client. Verify path is preserved during the refactor.

docs.title: Appendix: how to regenerate this table
docs.text:
# From the repo root:
import re
content = open('docs/Audit/audit-report.md', 'r', encoding='utf-8').read()
blocks = re.split(r'^### (F-\d+|D-\d+):\s*', content, flags=re.MULTILINE)[1:]
findings = []
for i in range(0, len(blocks), 2):
    fid = blocks[i]
    body = blocks[i+1] if i+1 < len(blocks) else ''
    m_impact = re.search(r'\*\*Frontend impact:\*\*\s*(\w+)\s*[—-]?\s*(.*?)(?:\n|$)', body)
    if m_impact:
        findings.append((fid, m_impact.group(1).lower(), m_impact.group(2).strip()))

# Group by impact
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(f[1] for f in findings))
for impact in ('high', 'medium', 'low'):
    print(f'\n=== {impact} ===')
    for fid, i, note in findings:
        if i == impact:
            print(f'{fid}: {note[:120]}')

Re-run this after every fix to see the frontend-impact distribution shrink.

docs.title: Frontend Team Messages — Post-Audit Coordination
docs.text:
Three ready-to-send messages for the Gallery, Web Portal, and Flutter teams covering everything that changed in the claude/magical-liskov-06b29d audit branch (PR #72).

Each message below is self-contained — copy the section into an email / Slack / ticket for the respective team. The detailed finding IDs (F-NN) reference audit-report.md for anyone who wants to dig deeper.

docs.title: 1. Gallery Service Team (media.ad4x4.com)
docs.text:
Subject: AD4x4 backend audit — gallery webhook changes, no action required on your side

Hi gallery team,

The AD4x4 backend just completed a large quality/security audit. Several findings touched the gallery webhook integration, but none of our fixes require changes on your side. Sharing for visibility.

docs.title: What changed on our side
docs.text: What Before After Retry behavior on 4xx responses We raised RuntimeError on any non-200 from your webhooks. Huey retried up to 6 times (create) or 3 times (update/delete/restore) with 1-hour backoff, wasting your 4xx responses. We now differentiate: 4xx → log as permanent failure and stop retrying. 5xx / network errors / timeouts → raise and retry as before. You'll see fewer retry storms for bad-request-class failures. Idempotency guard If create_gallery_for_trip succeeded remotely but our local save failed, the retry would create a second gallery for the same trip. We now check if trip.gallery_id: return gallery_id before calling you. No duplicate galleries on retry. Error logging Our error paths sometimes logged the full response body, which could include Bearer tokens if your API echoed headers in error responses. We now log status codes and sanitized message bodies only — no more potential auth-header leakage in our logs. Timeout floor We trusted ConfigurableSettings.gallery_api_timeout blindly; a mis-set 0 would hang the worker forever. We enforce max(1, gallery_api_timeout) — minimum 1-second timeout regardless of config. Cancel trip cascade TripEditView.destroy only flipped approval_status to CANCELED; your webhook was called via signal but members weren't notified. destroy now also notifies every registered + waitlisted member. The gallery soft-delete webhook you already receive continues to fire via the same signal path — no traffic pattern change for you.

docs.title: What you'll see
docs.text:
• Lower 4xx webhook retry volume from our side. If you were seeing repeated calls for rejected requests, those stop.
  • No duplicate trip/published calls for the same trip_id under retry conditions.
  • Everything else (payload shape, endpoints, auth, timing) is unchanged.

docs.title: What we'd like to discuss later (not urgent)
docs.text:
Finding F-31 in our audit recommended adding an explicit Idempotency-Key request header on the webhook calls, so you can reject obvious duplicates even if our local trip.gallery_id guard fails. This is optional and would require a spec conversation — can we:

  1. Sync on whether your webhook endpoints support an Idempotency-Key: <uuid> header today (accept + dedupe / accept + ignore / reject unknown headers)?
  2. Agree on a semantic if we add one: reject duplicate keys as 409, or return the original response?

If it's a non-trivial lift on your side, we're happy to stick with the current guard. No timeline pressure.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Your webhooks weren't exercised in our audit's pytest run (we can't hit a live gallery from CI). Once the audit branch merges to main, standard smoke tests on staging should confirm:

  • POST /api/webhooks/trip/published still works
  • POST /api/webhooks/trip/updated still works
  • POST /api/webhooks/trip/deleted still works (will see increased traffic when trip destroy cascade ships — every cancellation now triggers this + member notifications)

docs.text:

  • Gallery-specific findings: F-29 (settings shadowing), F-30 (exception leakage), F-31 (idempotency), F-33 (retry taxonomy), F-82 (timeout floor) — all in docs/Audit/audit-report.md

Thanks — AD4x4 backend team

docs.title: 2. Web Portal Team (ap.ad4x4.com / ad4x4.com)
docs.text:
Subject: AD4x4 backend audit — web client changes required

Hi web team,

The AD4x4 backend audit branch is ready for merge and includes several changes the web portal needs to be aware of. Below is a triaged list of everything that could affect a web client, ordered from "must fix before merge lands" to "informational."

docs.title: TL;DR coordination
docs.text:
• One coordinated release: please ship client changes for F-12 and F-56 in the same window the backend merges.
  • ~2–3 days of work total, most of it testing across member directory, trip registration, and ClubNews surfaces.
  • No endpoint-path changes — only behavior / error-shape / permission tightenings. Your existing API client can keep its structure; you'll adjust error handling and a couple of endpoint choices.
  • Regenerate your OpenAPI client from the updated schema.yml (45 lines added, 28 removed — all backward-compatible refinements, no breaking types).

docs.title: Must coordinate before merge lands
docs.text: ID What changed What web needs to do F-12 GET /api/members/ now requires SEARCH_MEMBERS permission. Non-privileged authenticated users get 403. The endpoint was previously wide-open to any logged-in user. If the web portal uses the raw member list for dropdowns (e.g. trip lead picker, admin member browsing), switch to /api/members/search/ or /api/members/leadsearch/ which are already permissioned and return a scoped/searchable response. Verify no hidden reliance on GET /api/members/ for enumeration. F-56 ClubNewsViewSet read list/detail now filters by the viewer's level. Lower-level users see fewer items than before (only level-agnostic news + news gated to their level). Product impact: if the web portal has a public-facing news block or a "latest news" widget that expected the full list, it will now return a filtered set for authenticated users. Verify the widget's messaging makes sense ("news for your level" rather than "all news"). No code change if your current filter logic already assumes the backend will filter. F-09 /api/trips/<pk>/register no longer bypasses validation for permission holders. Admin-initiated overrides must use /api/trips/<pk>/forceregister. If the web portal has an admin trip-registration UI that relied on the silent bypass, switch those calls to /forceregister. Member-facing registration UI is unaffected. F-05 /api/upgraderequests/<pk>/approve may now return 409 Conflict with {"message": "applicant_already_at_or_above_target_level"} when approving would downgrade someone. Add error handling for 409 on the approve action — surface the message in the admin UI.

docs.title: Should handle (low-risk 400s, likely already covered)
docs.text: ID What changed F-50 Avatar uploads over 2.5 MB now return 400 at the API (previously silently truncated). If your upload UI already handles 400s with a file-size message, no change. F-52 /api/members/<id>/payments endpoint no longer crashes on JSON true/false — now properly validated. F-65 HERE Maps reverse-geocode errors return cleaner messages (no more raw exception strings or API key leakage in error responses). If you display the error text directly, nothing breaks — just gets cleaner. F-80 /api/notifications/ now paginates properly (was hard-sliced at 20). If your notification list UI expected exactly 20 items, it will now page via standard ?page=N params — uses the standard paginator shape you get elsewhere. F-37 Login now returns a single unified error message for bad credentials vs disabled accounts. If your login UI distinguished the two via error text, it becomes one error. F-63 /api/trips/<pk>/forceregister now returns 403 on permission denial (was silently returning 200 with success: false). Admin UIs should surface 403s rather than inspecting the response body.

docs.title: Web-portal-specific
docs.text: ID What changed F-88 *.sandbox.novita.ai removed from CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_REGEXES in production — restricted to dev mode only. If the web portal uses any tooling hosted on Novita (Figma plugins, Storybook previews, design-review environments), that tooling will no longer reach the production API from those origins. Move to a dev/staging domain instead. F-35 SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER is now only set in production. If the web portal runs behind a local dev TLS proxy that forwarded X-Forwarded-Proto: https, request.is_secure() may now return False in local dev (as intended). Verify dev environment still works.

docs.title: Informational — notification-delivery improvements
docs.text:
Users may notice small behavior changes that do not require web-portal code updates:

  • F-06, F-24, F-26 — ClubNews and per-channel notifications now retry correctly on transient failures without duplicating delivery on success. Users should see fewer duplicate emails / push notifications.
  • F-75 — When an admin cancels a trip, registered and waitlisted members now receive the standard removed_from_trip_* notifications. Previously they got nothing. Customer support talking point: members may ask why they suddenly see cancellation notifications. Messaging is: "This is now working as intended."
  • F-04 — Huey tasks are now wrapped in transaction.on_commit universally. Some edge cases where notifications went out for rolled-back operations are now fixed. No code change for web.

docs.title: 3. Flutter Mobile App Team
docs.text:
Subject: AD4x4 backend audit — Flutter client changes required, one coordinated release

Hi mobile team,

The backend audit is closing out. There are real changes Flutter needs to handle, but the overall surface is small — most of the audit was server-side hardening. Below is triaged from "must fix before backend merge" to "informational."

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
• ~2–3 days of Flutter work + one App Store / Play Store review cycle.
  • No endpoint paths changed. Your existing service layer can stay structurally.
  • One new 409 to handle (upgrade approve conflict).
  • One endpoint migration if the app uses raw /api/members/ for dropdowns — switch to /search/ or /leadsearch/.
  • Regenerate the OpenAPI client from the new schema.yml — all backward-compatible refinements.

docs.title: Must coordinate before merge lands
docs.text: ID What changed What Flutter needs to do F-12 GET /api/members/ now gates on SEARCH_MEMBERS permission. Non-privileged users get 403. If the app uses the member list for trip-lead pickers, deputy-lead selection, or similar dropdowns, switch to /api/members/search/ or /api/members/leadsearch/. Both are already permissioned and take a q param for fuzzy-search. The raw list endpoint is now locked down. F-09 Member-facing /api/trips/<pk>/register no longer silently bypasses validation for permission holders. Admin-registration flows must use /api/trips/<pk>/forceregister. If the marshal / admin UI has a "register member for trip" flow that relied on the silent bypass, point it at /forceregister. Plain member registration is unaffected. F-05 /api/upgraderequests/<pk>/approve may now return 409 with {"message": "applicant_already_at_or_above_target_level"} when approval would downgrade an already-promoted member. Add handling for 409 on the approve action — show the error message, don't retry. Typical scenario: a stale upgrade request sitting in the queue for a member who was already manually promoted. F-50 Avatar uploads over 2.5 MB now return 400 at the API. Previously the image was silently truncated. If the app compresses avatars client-side, no change. If it uploads originals, the user needs a clear message. The backend returns {"success": false, "message": "avatar must be smaller than 2.5MB"}.

docs.title: Should handle (likely already covered by generic 400/403 handlers)
docs.text: ID What changed F-01 /api/logbookskillreferences/ is now read-only via API (was accidentally writable). If the app only reads it, no change. If it writes, those calls now return 405/403. F-52 /api/members/<id>/payments no longer crashes on JSON true/false — properly validated. If the app was serializing booleans correctly, no change. F-63 /api/trips/<pk>/forceregister now returns 403 on permission denial (previously 200 with success: false). If error handling treats non-2xx as failure, no change. If it only checks success: false, it'll work but won't flag the 403 distinctly. F-65 HERE Maps reverse-geocode errors no longer leak raw exception strings or API keys. Error messages are cleaner. F-80 /api/notifications/ now paginates properly (was hard-sliced at 20). If the app already handles paginated responses, no change. If it expected exactly 20, switch to paginated fetching. F-37 Login returns a single unified error for "bad credentials" vs "disabled account." If the login UI distinguished them via error text, it's now one error. F-15 /api/upgraderequests/<pk>/... endpoints and /api/upgraderequestcomments/... now return 404 (was 500) on unknown IDs. Nothing to do — error handling just gets cleaner.

docs.title: Informational — notification behavior improvements
docs.text:
• F-75 — trip cancellations now notify registered + waitlisted members. Previously, canceling a trip silently left members on the roster. Now they receive the standard removed_from_trip_registered or removed_from_trip_waitlist push/email/in-app notification payload — payload shape unchanged, so no Flutter code change. Just more of them. Support talking point: members may ask why they're suddenly seeing cancellation notifications; this is the intended new behavior.
  • F-06, F-24, F-26 — per-channel notification idempotency. Users should see fewer duplicate pushes on retries.
  • F-04 — transaction.on_commit is now universal. Edge cases where a rolled-back operation triggered a notification are gone.

docs.title: Regenerate the OpenAPI client
docs.text:
schema.yml diff: +45 / −28 lines. Worth regenerating for:

  • VehicleViewSet path params correctly typed as integer (was inferred as string)
  • send_club_news added to the PermissionMatrixAction enum — if the app lets admins configure permissions, the new choice appears
  • MarkNotificationLogAsReadView returns 200 (was 201) — update expected status code if asserted
  • LogbookMigrationRequestSerializer response fields (member, target_level, skill_entries) now have proper object schemas — your generated models will be more precise

None are breaking — regeneration produces a cleaner, better-typed client.

docs.title: Test checklist suggestion
docs.text:
• Trip lead picker still populates with appropriate members (F-12 endpoint swap)
  • Admin registration flow routes through force-register (F-09)
  • Upgrade approve shows the 409 message correctly (F-05)
  • Avatar upload shows the size limit message on oversize files (F-50)
  • Notification list pagination works beyond 20 items (F-80)
  • Vehicle set-primary button still works (F-07 internal refactor — path preserved)

docs.title: Release coordination
docs.text:
• Backend targets merge when Mikkel gives the final CI sign-off (expected soon)
  • Recommend: Flutter ships the coordinated release after the backend merge lands on production, not simultaneously — gives time for any backend rollback if needed
  • App Store / Play Store review lag means ~2–5 days from your submission to live; factor that into your release planning
  • No feature-flag coordination needed — all changes are backward-compatible for an older Flutter client (users on old app versions will keep working; the 403s they may now hit on /api/members/ are better than silent PII exposure)

docs.title: Step 1 — Django System Checks
docs.text: Ran run_check (regular) and run_check --deploy via MCP.

docs.title: Regular check (dev mode)
docs.text:
• Total issues: 1 warning, 0 errors
  • staticfiles.W004 — STATICFILES_DIRS references staticfiles/ directory that doesn't exist.

docs.title: Deploy check (also in dev mode — see caveat)
docs.text:
• Total issues: 16 warnings (0 errors, 0 critical)
  • Expected dev-mode artifacts:
  • security.W018 — DEBUG=True
  • security.W004 — SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS not set
  • security.W008 — SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT not True
  • security.W012 — SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE not True
  • security.W016 — CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE not True
  • security.W009 — SECRET_KEY is the insecure dev default

Caveat: These are all correctly handled in ad4x4/settings.py lines 84–92, which sets the production-safe values inside if not DEV:. The deploy check sees the dev state because the MCP server runs in dev mode. No action needed on these six for production (verified in source).

docs.title: [low / confidence high] staticfiles directory missing
docs.text:
• File: ad4x4/settings.py — STATICFILES_DIRS referenced but staticfiles/ folder absent
  • Category: config
  • Evidence: Reported by both regular and deploy check
  • Recommendation: Either create an empty staticfiles/ at project root with a .gitkeep, or remove the entry from STATICFILES_DIRS. The Docker image probably populates it at build — verify by inspecting Dockerapp.

docs.title: [low / confidence high] Dev SECRET_KEY hardcoded in source
docs.text:
• File: ad4x4/settings.py:74
  • Evidence: SECRET_KEY = 'dev-secret-key-123463sdf12349erwh2837h'
  • Category: security (dev-only)
  • Recommendation: Not exploitable (dev mode only) but publishing the string in public source is bad hygiene — move to os.getenv('DJANGO_DEV_SECRET_KEY', '<random default generated each boot>') so anyone cloning the repo doesn't get the same key.

docs.title: [low / confidence high] Stale from django.conf.global_settings import SECRET_KEY
docs.text:
• File: ad4x4/settings.py:19
  • Evidence: Line 19 imports SECRET_KEY from Django globals; lines 70/74 immediately shadow it.
  • Recommendation: Remove line 19 — dead import. Linter would flag it.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] Schema generation warnings for LogbookMigrationRequest serializers
docs.text:
• File: api/serializers/serializers_migration.py
  • Evidence: 6 drf_spectacular.W001 warnings — get_member, get_target_level, get_skill_entries return types not annotated on both LogbookMigrationRequestListSerializer and LogbookMigrationRequestSerializer
  • Category: openapi-drift
  • Recommendation: Add @extend_schema_field(MemberBaseSerializer) (or equivalent) decorators, or type hint -> dict on each get_* method. Otherwise Swagger clients see these fields as plain strings.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] VehicleViewSet queryset resolution fails in schema gen
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_vehicle.py
  • Evidence: drf_spectacular.W001 — failed to obtain model through view's queryset (AnonymousUser passed to Field('id')). Path parameter id also untyped.
  • Category: openapi-drift
  • Recommendation: Two fixes needed:
  • Add queryset = Vehicle.objects.none() on the ViewSet or guard get_queryset() with if getattr(self, 'swagger_fake_view', False): return Vehicle.objects.none()
  • In urls.py or via lookup_value_regex, type the path parameter as int so Swagger stops guessing.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] StatusBc4Enum collision in OpenAPI schema
docs.text:
• Evidence: Warning: enum naming encountered a non-optimally resolvable collision for fields named "status"
  • Category: openapi-drift
  • Recommendation: Add entries in SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS['ENUM_NAME_OVERRIDES'] for the specific status fields (e.g., TripApprovalStatusEnum, UpgradeRequestStatusEnum, ClubNewsStatusEnum, LogbookMigrationStatusEnum, WebsitePaymentStatusEnum) to give each a distinct name. Clients currently see a StatusBc4Enum which is meaningless.

docs.title: [low / confidence medium] ALLOWED_HOSTS includes a hardcoded IP and a port-qualified host
docs.text:
• File: ad4x4/settings.py:81
  • Evidence: ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['0.0.0.0', 'localhost', '127.0.0.1', 'ap.ad4x4.com', '78.47.162.184', 'localhost:50891']
  • Category: config-smell
  • Recommendation: 78.47.162.184 is the Hetzner IP — acceptable but brittle if IP changes. Move to env var. localhost:50891 is very suspicious — ports aren't allowed in ALLOWED_HOSTS (Django strips them anyway), so this entry does nothing. Remove it or convert to comment.

docs.title: [low / confidence high] Settings import ordering / Firebase init at module load
docs.text:
• File: ad4x4/settings.py:16–36
  • Evidence: Firebase Admin SDK is initialized at settings.py import time. This means every manage.py command (including check, makemigrations, tests) runs a network-capable SDK init.
  • Recommendation: Move Firebase init into an AppConfig.ready() method, or lazy-init on first use. Side benefit: tests and check run faster and don't need FCM creds.

docs.title: Production-branch verification (settings.py:84–92)
docs.text:
Manually confirmed the production branch sets all six security headers correctly:

if not DEV:
    SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
    SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000
    SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS = True
    SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD = True
    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
    CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
    SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF = True
    SECURE_BROWSER_XSS_FILTER = True

This is correct. The deploy-check warnings for those six are dev-mode noise.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• 0 critical / 0 error
  • 2 medium findings (schema generation — user-facing impact on Swagger consumers)
  • 3 low findings (dev hygiene)
  • 2 informational (prod-branch correct; Firebase init placement)

docs.title: Step 2 — Endpoint Drift
docs.text: Cross-reference of mcp__django-ai-boost__list_urls output vs CLAUDE.md §6 vs schema.yml.

docs.title: Raw counts
docs.text:
Source Count Notes Total URL patterns 467 Includes admin + DRF format variants Admin patterns 257 Auto-generated, not audited /api/ patterns 181 After filtering admin and OIDC Distinct /api/ paths (no format variants) ~90 Format variants are duplicates schema.yml paths 123 schema.yml operations 174

Note on path counts: schema.yml reports 123 "paths" because drf-spectacular treats each URL with different methods as one path. Our 90 distinct URL patterns × ~2 methods avg ≈ 174 operations matches.

docs.title: [high / confidence high] Duplicate URL registrations for three auth endpoints
docs.text:
• Files: ad4x4/urls.py
  • Evidence: list_urls reports each of these URLs twice with different view handlers:
  • api/auth/login/ → api.views.views_auth.LoginView AND rest_registration.api.views.login.LoginView
  • api/auth/logout/ → api.views.views_auth.LogoutView AND rest_registration.api.views.login.LogoutView
  • api/auth/change-password/ → api.views.views_auth.CustomChangePasswordView AND rest_registration.api.views.change_password.ChangePasswordView
  • Category: routing fragility
  • Why this matters: Django uses the first matching URL pattern. CLAUDE.md §7 explicitly says the custom LoginView is mounted before rest_registration's include so it "shadows" them. That works today, but a future refactor that reorders includes silently changes behavior — the rest_registration views don't honor the login/username/email case-insensitive lookup or the password-change-blacklists-all-tokens rule (§15). A regression here is silent.
  • Recommendation: Either (a) exclude those three routes from the rest_registration include using its include_urls config, or (b) add a test_urls.py assertion that resolve('/api/auth/login/') returns views_auth.LoginView. Prefer (a).

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] Undocumented register-email / verify-email endpoints
docs.text:
• Evidence: list_urls shows:
  • api/auth/register-email/ → rest_registration.api.views.register_email.RegisterEmailView
  • api/auth/verify-email/ → rest_registration.api.views.register_email.VerifyEmailView
  • CLAUDE.md §6 documents only register/, verify-registration/, reset-password/, send-reset-password-link/, change-password/.
  • Category: doc-drift
  • Why this matters: Email change flow is exposed to clients but undocumented. If these are intentional, doc them. If unintentional (e.g. from default rest_registration URL include), disable them.
  • Recommendation: Decide: either remove from URL conf or add to CLAUDE.md §6 with semantics (what body shape, what effect). Ask Mikkel (ADMINS) whether change-email flow is a supported product feature.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] api/vehicles/<int:pk>/set_primary/ is wired manually, not as ViewSet @action
docs.text:
• File: ad4x4/urls.py:205 (per member-flow review agent finding)
  • Evidence: list_urls shows api/vehicles/<int:pk>/set_primary/ routed to VehicleViewSet but NOT through the router — it's a manual as_view() call in urls.py.
  • Category: framework-smell
  • Consequence: DRF @action decorators on the method are dead; @extend_schema on the method doesn't attach to the Swagger spec; permissions/throttles from the ViewSet may not apply correctly. The schema generation warning drf_spectacular.W001 about VehicleViewSet (see raw/01-system-check.md) is a downstream symptom.
  • Recommendation: Convert to a proper @action(detail=True, methods=['post']) method and let the router wire it. Alternatively turn it into a standalone APIView.

docs.title: [low / confidence high] Separate TripCreateView / TripEditView outside the TripViewSet router
docs.text:
• File: ad4x4/urls.py + api/views/views_trip.py
  • Evidence:
  • api/trips → TripCreateView (note: no trailing slash)
  • api/trips/<int:pk> → TripEditView (also no trailing slash)
  • api/trips/ → TripViewSet list/retrieve/destroy (from router, with trailing slash)
  • Category: convention-drift
  • Why this matters: CLAUDE.md §6 lists Trips (/api/trips/) as "Standard CRUD" via ViewSet. In reality create and update go to dedicated views (hence the slashless variant). Trailing-slash sensitivity means a client that hits POST /api/trips/ might not reach TripCreateView — depends on APPEND_SLASH middleware behavior.
  • Recommendation: Either merge TripCreateView / TripEditView logic back into TripViewSet.create / update (DRY and consistent), OR document this split in CLAUDE.md §6 with a clear rationale. Also audit client calls — does the Flutter app hit /api/trips (no slash) or /api/trips/?

docs.title: [low / confidence high] Router regex patterns leak into URL conf (^clubnews/$ etc.)
docs.text:
• Evidence: All router-generated URLs are prefixed with ^ (regex start anchor) because the routers are presumably being include()d with re_path instead of path. Visually obvious in every list_urls entry starting with ^.
  • Category: style / hygiene
  • Why this matters: Works fine functionally but is unusual — Django 6 prefers path + include. Router's ^ prefix appearing in user-visible URL names is a smell.
  • Recommendation: In ad4x4/urls.py, ensure router includes use path('api/', include(router.urls)), not re_path(r'^api/', include(router.urls)). Cosmetic but aligns with the rest of the codebase.

docs.title: [low / confidence medium] NotificationLogViewSet only exposes list, not detail
docs.text:
• Evidence: Only api/^notifications/$ pattern, no (?P<pk>...) variant.
  • Category: rest-surface
  • Why this matters: If the client ever wants to retrieve a specific NotificationLog by ID (e.g. for deep-linking), it can't. mark-as-read handles one ID at a time but it's a write endpoint.
  • Recommendation: Either confirm the product decision (list-only is intentional) and document in CLAUDE.md §6, or expose retrieve.

docs.title: [info / confidence high] 90-ish distinct API paths total; heaviest areas:
docs.text:
• trips/ — 21 operations (16 in §6, rest are format variants)
  • members/ — 17 operations (matches §6)
  • auth/ — 11 operations (8 in §6 + 3 from rest_registration extras noted above)
  • choices/ — 10 operations (9 listed in §6, one possibly new — permissionmatrixaction, confirmed present in §6)
  • upgraderequests/ — 9 operations (matches §6)

docs.title: Undocumented or under-documented endpoints (summary)
docs.text: URL Status Recommendation api/auth/register-email/ Undocumented Decide: document or disable api/auth/verify-email/ Undocumented Decide: document or disable api/trips (no slash) → TripCreateView Under-documented Note split in §6 api/trips/<pk> (no slash) → TripEditView Under-documented Note split in §6 api/vehicles/<pk>/set_primary/ Documented but wired wrong Convert to @action

docs.text:

  • All api/trips/<pk>/* action subroutes match CLAUDE.md §6

docs.title: Recommended action for doc
docs.text:
Regenerate schema and commit:

python manage.py spectacular --file schema.yml

And update CLAUDE.md §6 with: - New row for register-email + verify-email - Note on Trip create/update being separate views - Note on set_primary being a manual as_view() (once fixed, remove that note)

docs.text: Cross-reference of mcp__django-ai-boost__list_models output vs CLAUDE.md §5 vs api/models/*.py source.

docs.title: Caveat
docs.text: mcp__django-ai-boost__database_schema failed (dev DB dev doesn't exist). Recommended follow-up: create a throwaway DB, run migrations, re-run database_schema to catch any migration-level schema that bypasses ORM declaration.

docs.text:
• Total models in api + website: 33
  • Models documented in CLAUDE.md §5: 19

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] 11+ models missing from CLAUDE.md §5
docs.text:
These models exist in source (and most are exposed via endpoints documented in §6) but are absent from §5's model catalog:
