docs.title: [high / confidence high] TripRegistrationCancellationReason is a cancellation audit table with no documentation
docs.text:
• Fields: trip, member, removed_by (nullable FK, for admin removals), removal_date, reason (TextField)
  • Why it matters: This model persists every cancellation/removal. It's the audit log for who removed whom and why. Critical for disputes, but currently has no mention in §5, no admin note in CLAUDE.md §11, and the trip-flow agent found async tasks whose signature expects this model (see raw/06-code-review-trip-flow.md and raw/08-async-tasks.md — the call sites pass (user, trip) where the task expects a TripRegistrationCancellationReason instance).
  • Recommendation: Add to §5. Also verify retention policy — does this get purged, ever?

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] Member.token_version still present — cleanup PR still pending
docs.text:
• Field: Member.token_version (PositiveIntegerField)
  • Evidence: list_models confirms the column is still on the model. Per CLAUDE.md §7 and §15, this is "legacy, unused" — session invalidation now flows through simplejwt's token_blacklist.
  • Auth review agent (a90998f56c9ac802c) confirmed nothing in views_auth.py, permissions.py, or util.py reads or writes it.
  • Recommendation: Create the follow-up PR mentioned in §15 — drop the column in a migration. Until it's gone, each Member row carries an unused 4-byte int.

docs.title: [medium / confidence medium] Member.gender max_length=3 for single-char codes (M/F/O)
docs.text:
• Field: gender = CharField(max_length=3)
  • Rationale unclear: single-char codes need only max_length=1. 3 might be legacy or intentional extensibility (e.g. for future codes). No CLAUDE.md §5 comment explains.
  • Recommendation: Either (a) shorten to max_length=1 in a tiny migration, or (b) document the 3-char reservation in §5 (e.g. for future non-binary codes).

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] Vehicle.brand max_length=8 — might clip new brands
docs.text:
• Field: brand = CharField(max_length=8)
  • Evidence: Doc §5 says "74 CarBrand choices". Brand codes are stored as short tokens, so 8 is likely enough, but the enum is in api/choices.py. Any future brand with a longer code fails silently at write time.
  • Recommendation: Grep api/choices.py for the longest CarBrand token; if 8 is hit, bump to 16 proactively.

docs.title: [low / confidence high] Vehicle.name exists but not in §5
docs.text:
• CLAUDE.md §5 lists brand, model, year, color, image, is_primary for Vehicle. Actual model also has name (CharField, nullable).
  • Recommendation: Add name to §5.

docs.title: [low / confidence high] UpgradeRequest.applicant_reason uses max_length=1500 on a TextField
docs.text:
• Evidence: TextField ignores max_length at the DB level. It only constrains form rendering.
  • Impact: A malicious or buggy client can submit 1 MB of applicant_reason and the DB will accept it; DRF validates only up to max_length if the serializer is a CharField(style='textarea', max_length=1500). Verify the serializer enforces it.
  • Recommendation: Add an explicit check in the serializer (validate_applicant_reason), or convert to CharField(max_length=1500) since the length is bounded.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] LogbookSkillReference has no unique constraint on (member, trip, logbook_skill)
docs.text:
• Evidence: list_models shows the three FKs but no UniqueConstraint. Cross-reference with logbook review agent (raw/06-code-review-logbook.md finding F3/F4): the service layer mitigates by deleting-and-reinserting, but that wipes data if two marshals write entries for the same trip.
  • Recommendation: Add in a migration: python class Meta: constraints = [ models.UniqueConstraint( fields=['member', 'trip', 'logbook_skill'], name='uniq_logbook_skill_ref_per_trip', ), ] Then replace the delete-reinsert in _manage_logbook_skill_references with update_or_create.

docs.title: [low / confidence medium] Explicit db_index=True is used on hot paths but coverage may be uneven
docs.text:
• Files with explicit db_index=True: models_trip.py (starttime, endtime, approvalstatus, TripRegistration member/trip/checkedin), models_member.py (Meta indexes), models_upgraderequest.py (Meta indexes), models_vehicle.py, models_sponsors.py, models_geocoding_cache.py.
  • Not explicitly indexed but likely filtered:
  • NotificationLog.timestamp (purged after 60 days — purge scan benefits from index)
  • NotificationLog.is_read (mark-as-read queries)
  • TripRegistration.registration_date
  • UpgradeRequest.verdict_date (sorting)
  • LogbookEntry.created_at (listing)
  • ClubNews.submit_date (ordering)
  • Recommendation: Spot-check with a real query profile. For each of the above, if it's used in filter / order_by in more than a couple of places, add db_index=True or a Meta.indexes = [models.Index(fields=['...'])]. Not urgent until traffic grows.

docs.title: [low / confidence high] ConfigurableSettings.email_sleep_period_ms naming suggests milliseconds but CLAUDE.md §5 says "email sleep period"
docs.text:
• Field: email_sleep_period_ms = PositiveSmallIntegerField(...)

docs.title: Code Review — Auth + Permissions
docs.text: Scope: api/views/views_auth.py, api/permissions.py, api/util.py (JWT subclass only). Mode: READ-ONLY audit.

docs.title: F-01 — SessionsView.delete treats empty keep_refresh as "keep nothing"; edge-case token reuse path
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:224-253
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: token-lifecycle
  • Evidence: In SessionsView.delete, when the payload omits keep_refresh or sends "", keep_refresh_raw = '' is falsy so keep_jti stays None and the code blacklists every outstanding token. CLAUDE.md §6 says: "Without keep_refresh it behaves like logout-all." Matches. However, when a valid keep_refresh is supplied, RefreshToken(keep_refresh_raw) is constructed purely for payload inspection — it is not blacklisted. That's correct for this flow, but note: simplejwt's RefreshToken(token) constructor only runs signature+exp checks; it does not verify the refresh is not already blacklisted. A user could therefore pass a blacklisted-but-not-yet-expired refresh token as keep_refresh and the view would accept it and use its JTI as the "keep" target, leaving that (dead) session untouched while killing the rest. The dead session remains dead, so no real privilege escalation — but the kept_jti returned to the client is misleading.
  • Recommendation: after decoding keep_refresh, also verify BlacklistedToken.objects.filter(token__jti=keep_jti).exists() is False before honoring it. If blacklisted, fall through to the "blacklist all" path so the response accurately reflects reality.

docs.title: F-02 — SessionsView.delete calls serializer.is_valid() twice
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:225-226
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=False) keep_refresh_raw = serializer.validated_data.get('keep_refresh', '') if serializer.is_valid() else '' is_valid() is called twice (the second call re-runs validation). Harmless today (serializer has only one optional field), but the pattern is fragile.
  • Recommendation: capture is_valid() once: ok = serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=False); keep_refresh_raw = serializer.validated_data.get('keep_refresh', '') if ok else ''.

docs.title: F-03 — LoginView returns distinct error strings for "bad credentials" vs "disabled account"
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:122-126
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: info-leak
  • Evidence: The view returns invalid_credentials when _resolve_login_user fails and account_disabled when the user exists but is inactive. An attacker can therefore distinguish "this username/email exists but is deactivated" from "this username/email does not exist or password is wrong." This is a mild account-enumeration vector, especially relevant here because anonymize_data() deactivates accounts on GDPR deletion — it would leak that a specific email was previously a member.
  • Recommendation: return invalid_credentials for both cases. If the backend still needs to log the distinction, log it server-side; do not expose it over the wire.

docs.title: F-04 — _resolve_login_user swallows MultipleObjectsReturned silently
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:63-66
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: email__iexact can legitimately match multiple rows if two members have emails differing only by case (e.g. alice@x.com, Alice@x.com). The Member.email field is declared unique=True at case-sensitive DB level, so this can happen if historical data pre-dates case-insensitive handling. Today the login silently fails with invalid_credentials, which is a genuinely confusing user-support scenario.
  • Recommendation: either (a) add a case-insensitive DB constraint / UniqueConstraint(Lower('email')) on Member.email and enforce it during registration, or (b) at minimum log a warning when MultipleObjectsReturned fires so support can intervene.

docs.title: F-05 — SQL injection check: all lookups are safe
docs.text:
• Severity: low (no issue — positive finding)
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:64, api/util.py:60-64
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: sql-injection
  • Evidence: User.objects.get(email__iexact=login_value) and get_user_by_lookup_dict({db_fn: value}, ...) both parameterize via the Django ORM. db_fn values come from a whitelist ('username__iexact', 'email__iexact') set in code, not from user input. No raw SQL, no .extra(), no .raw(). Safe.
  • Recommendation: none — keep it this way. Do not refactor these paths to dynamic filter(**{...}) where the key is attacker-controlled.

docs.title: F-06 — Member.token_version field still present (documented as legacy)
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • File: api/models/models_member.py:82
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: token-lifecycle
  • Evidence: token_version field survives on the model. Grep confirms nothing in views_auth.py, permissions.py, or util.py reads or writes it — so the files under audit are clean on this point. Only migration files and the model definition reference it. CLAUDE.md §7 / §15 mark it as legacy/unused and scheduled for removal.
  • Recommendation: out-of-scope for this audit; flagged for a follow-up cleanup PR (drop field + migration).

docs.title: F-07 — JWTAuthentication.get_user creates NotificationSettings on every authenticated request
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File: api/util.py:31-36
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other (performance)
  • Evidence: obj, _created = NotificationSettings.objects.get_or_create(member=user) obj.save() Every single authenticated request performs a SELECT … OR INSERT … and then an unconditional UPDATE. The comment says "update the last_user_activity field … by triggering a save" — but save() with no changed fields still writes every column. At throttle ceiling (200 req/min per user) this is 200 unnecessary UPDATEs per user per minute. Also: LastVisitedMiddleware already updates Member.last_visited at 1/hr (per §4). The two mechanisms overlap.
  • Recommendation: (a) only call obj.save(update_fields=['last_user_activity']) to reduce write amplification, and (b) throttle the same way LastVisitedMiddleware does (skip if updated within the last hour). Ideally consolidate both into LastVisitedMiddleware and drop this side-effect from get_user.

docs.title: F-08 — HasCreateUpgradeRequestForOtherPermission can raise on unknown level
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File: api/permissions.py:245-251
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: level_id = request.data.get('target_level') if level_id == None: return False level = Level.objects.get(id=level_id) # <-- DoesNotExist is NOT caught A client posting {"target_level": 99999} (or any invalid level id) will crash the permission check with Level.DoesNotExist → DRF converts it into a 500 Internal Server Error (not 403/400). Compare with HasCreateUpgradeRequestForSelfPermission which does catch DoesNotExist (line 241). Inconsistent.
  • Recommendation: wrap in try/except Level.DoesNotExist: return False to mirror the sibling class. Also replace == None with is None while here.

docs.title: F-09 — HasViewUpgradeRequestCommentPermission and HasCreateUpgradeRequestCommentPermission raise on missing upgrade request
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File: api/permissions.py:261-275
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: Line 264 does UpgradeRequest.objects.get(pk=upgrade_request_id) with no exception handling — if the pk is missing/invalid it bubbles UpgradeRequest.DoesNotExist → 500. Line 272 uses .filter(...).first() so that variant is safe, but both are defensive about the applicant check only for the found case.
  • Recommendation: change line 264 to .filter(pk=upgrade_request_id).first() plus a None guard, consistent with the adjacent class.

docs.title: F-10 — HasDeleteUpgradeRequestCommentPermission uses .get(...) or None
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • File: api/permissions.py:281
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: upgrade_request_comment = UpgradeRequestComment.objects.get(pk=comment_id) or None — .get() never returns None; it returns the row or raises DoesNotExist. The or None is dead code.
  • Recommendation: remove the or None; the existing try/except DoesNotExist already handles the missing case correctly.

docs.title: F-11 — CanEditOrDeleteTripBasePermission has duplicated block
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File: api/permissions.py:170-176
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: ``` settings = getglobalsettings() cutoffminutes = settings.tripeditdeletecutoffminutes cutofftime = trip.starttime - timedelta(minutes=cutoffminutes)

settings = getglobalsettings() cutoffminutes = settings.tripeditdeletecutoffminutes cutofftime = trip.starttime - timedelta(minutes=cutoffminutes) ``` Three lines are literally duplicated. Functionally harmless, but each call triggers a DB hit for the singleton. At permission-check frequency (every trip edit attempt) this doubles ORM load for the settings row. - Recommendation: delete the duplicate three lines.

docs.title: F-12 — permission_matrix_exists_or_user_is_superuser — empty-levels semantics correct
docs.text:
• Severity: low (positive finding)
  • File: api/permissions.py:15-30
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: The function first queries with levels__isnull=True. This is the raw M2M isnull filter — when a PermissionMatrix row has no related Level rows in the M2M, isnull=True on the related table returns True. Semantically: "no level restrictions → applies to every level." This matches CLAUDE.md §15: "An empty levels M2M in PermissionMatrix means the permission applies to members of any level." Correct. Caveat: if the row has any level attached, it is still matched by the second query only when level is passed in. If a caller forgets to pass level, a "restricted-to-specific-levels" permission is silently ignored. The current codebase generally does pass a level where appropriate, but the asymmetry is worth a docstring.
  • Recommendation: add a docstring note: "If level=None and the matrix row restricts to specific levels, the row is treated as non-matching. Pass the relevant level whenever the action is level-scoped."

docs.title: F-13 — HasViewUpgradeRequestPermissionOrIsForSelf compares pk (int) with URL kwarg (str)
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File: api/permissions.py:331-336
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: if request.user.pk == view.kwargs.get('pk'): return True view.kwargs['pk'] is a string (URL path segment), request.user.pk is an int. 1 == "1" is False in Python. The "is for self" shortcut therefore never fires, and users are forced down the matrix-permission branch. In practice users who should have the "self" shortcut succeed only because they also have the matrix permission — but users who lack both get a silent denial where the self-path was supposed to let them through.
  • Recommendation: coerce: str(request.user.pk) == view.kwargs.get('pk') or int(view.kwargs['pk']) == request.user.pk with a try/except ValueError.

docs.title: F-14 — is_staff / is_superuser in business logic
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File: api/permissions.py (multiple) + api/views/views_auth.py (none)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: CLAUDE.md §8 explicitly says "Do not use Django model-level permissions (is_staff, is_superuser) for business logic." Grep shows no is_staff usage in these files (good). But is_superuser is used as a bypass in many places: permission_matrix_exists_or_user_is_superuser, check_upgrade_request_permission_against_perm_matrix, check_trip_permission_against_perm_matrix*, IsTripLeadOrDeputy, IsFeedbackOwnerOrSuperuser, IsOwnerOrReadOnly, IsCreatorOrReadOnly, IsAdminUserOrReadOnly, IsSameUserAllowEditOrReadOnly, IsEditingOwnProfileOrAdmin, CanEditOrDeleteTripBasePermission, HasViewTripsAsLeadPermission. CLAUDE.md §8 primarily warns against using them instead of matrix checks. A superuser-as-break-glass bypass is an accepted pattern, but it is very widely sprinkled here. Specifically in HasEditMembershipPaymentsPermission (line 302-303) there is no is_superuser short-circuit — inconsistent with neighbours.
  • Recommendation: (a) document explicitly that "superuser bypass" is a project convention and accepted, (b) pick one place to check it — the helper permission_matrix_exists_or_user_is_superuser already does — and remove the redundant checks from the callers that pre-check before calling it, (c) audit every new permission class for the same bypass during review.

docs.title: F-15 — LogoutAllView has no refresh-token input but blacklists all; acceptable but asymmetric
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:164-179
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: token-lifecycle
  • Evidence: LogoutAllView relies solely on the access token (from IsAuthenticated) to identify the user, then blacklists all outstanding refresh tokens for that user. That's correct and matches §7. Note that the current session's access token is not invalidated — simplejwt has no access-token blacklist by default. An attacker holding a stolen access token can continue to use it until its exp (up to 24h per ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES=1440). Same is true of LogoutView and CustomChangePasswordView.
  • Recommendation: this is a known simplejwt limitation and the 24h lifetime is the mitigation. Consider shortening ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES to e.g. 15-60 if not already under consideration; 24h is generous for a platform with membership/trip data. Out-of-scope for code-level changes — flagging for architecture review.

docs.title: F-16 — _blacklist_all_user_tokens issues N+1 queries
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:27-42
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other (performance)
  • Evidence: The loop runs BlacklistedToken.objects.filter(token=ot).exists() once per outstanding token, then BlacklistedToken.objects.create(token=ot). For a user with many historical sessions this is O(n) queries. Same pattern in SessionsView.delete (line 243-247).
  • Recommendation: batch via already_blacklisted = set(BlacklistedToken.objects.filter(token__in=outstanding).values_list('token_id', flat=True)) then BlacklistedToken.objects.bulk_create([BlacklistedToken(token=ot) for ot in outstanding if ot.id not in already_blacklisted]). One read + one write instead of 2n.

docs.title: F-17 — Case-insensitive login: authenticate(username=…) path
docs.text:
• Severity: low (positive finding)
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:57
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: sql-injection
  • Evidence: authenticate(username=login_value, …) delegates to MyUserManager.get_by_natural_key (per CLAUDE.md §7), which Django uses with ORM filters — no raw SQL. The email fallback uses email__iexact, which PostgreSQL translates to UPPER(email) = UPPER(%s) via a parameterized query. Safe from SQL injection.
  • Recommendation: none.

docs.title: F-18 — UnifiedTokenObtainPairView drops simplejwt's structured error body
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File: api/views/views_auth.py:269-273
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: info-leak (minor)
  • Evidence: On failure, super().post() returns a DRF response with response.data being a dict like {"detail": "No active account found with the given credentials", "code": "authorization_failed"}. The wrapper re-emits that under message, so clients see a human-readable English string mentioning "active account" — which, like F-03, leaks whether an account is disabled vs missing.
  • Recommendation: consider normalizing the error message to a neutral invalid_credentials string, matching LoginView. If preserved for client compatibility, document it in §7.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Severity Count critical 0 high 2 (F-08, F-09) medium 5 (F-01, F-03, F-07, F-13, F-14) low 6 nit 3

Hotspots worth addressing first: 1. F-08 / F-09 — unhandled DoesNotExist in permission classes can cause 500s from attacker-controlled input. Quick fix, real impact. 2. F-13 — self-shortcut never fires due to str/int mismatch; a latent bug masking real authorization outcomes. 3. F-03 / F-18 — small account-enumeration leaks worth tightening. 4. F-07 — unnecessary DB writes on every authenticated request.

Token-lifecycle invariants from CLAUDE.md §7 hold: logout single-session, logout-all, session-list + selective revocation, password-change cascading blacklist, and refresh-token rotation are all implemented correctly. token_version is not referenced by any of the three audited files. No SQL-injection vectors found. PermissionMatrix.has_permission()'s empty-levels semantics match the §15 gotcha.

docs.title: Code Review — Logbook (api/views/views_logbook.py)
docs.text:
Scope: api/views/views_logbook.py only. Supporting files (models, permissions, service helper) read for context but not in scope.

Authoritative PermissionMatrix actions expected in this module: CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES, SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS, CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER, APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION. The file does not implement approval-migration or count-requirement endpoints, so those topics are addressed as coverage gaps.

docs.title: F1 — LogbookEntryViewSet list/detail suffers classic N+1 on M2M + FKs
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:33
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: n+1
  • Evidence: queryset = LogbookEntry.objects.all().order_by('id') with LogbookEntrySerializer using fields = '__all__' (see api/serializers/serializers_other.py:55-58). LogbookEntry has three FKs (trip, member, signed_by) and one M2M (skills_verified). DRF's ModelSerializer will hit a separate query per instance for each FK and per-instance for the M2M. With default pagesize=10, listing costs roughly 1 + 10*(3 FKs) + 10*(1 M2M) = 41 queries; at pagesize=500 it balloons to 2000+.
  • Recommendation: Override get_queryset() to attach select_related('trip', 'member', 'signed_by') and prefetch_related('skills_verified'). Same treatment for LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet.queryset (line 27) which has five FKs (logbook_skill, member, trip, signed_by, entered_by) and is similarly unprotected.

docs.title: F2 — _manage_logbook_skill_references is itself N+1 in the skill-loop
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:136-158
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: n+1
  • Evidence: A LogbookSkill.objects.get(id=skill_id) call sits inside the for skill_id in skills_verified: loop, followed by a single-row LogbookSkillReference.objects.create(...). For N verified skills this runs 2N queries (1 lookup + 1 insert), plus the single .delete() up front. It also silently ignores unknown skill IDs with a logger.warning — the client gets a 201 even though some skills were not recorded, which is a data-integrity hazard.
  • Recommendation: Batch: skills = LogbookSkill.objects.in_bulk(skill_ids); validate len(skills) == len(skill_ids) and raise ValidationError('one_or_more_skills_not_found') if not; then LogbookSkillReference.objects.bulk_create([... for skill in skills.values()]). This mirrors what TripLogbookEntryCreateView already does at line 309-312 and makes the behaviours consistent.

docs.title: F3 — No uniqueness guard on LogbookSkillReference (member, trip, logbook_skill)
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:139-156; also api/models/models_logbook.py:24-30
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: dup-prevention
  • Evidence: The model has no unique_together / UniqueConstraint covering (member, trip, logbook_skill). The view tries to enforce uniqueness by deleting every row for (member, trip) and recreating on every perform_create/perform_update. Any path that creates a LogbookSkillReference directly (admin, shell, other views, migrations) bypasses this. Worse, the delete-then-recreate pattern destroys entered_at, entered_by, and signed_by history on every edit — a marshal's original sign-off timestamp is silently overwritten.
  • Recommendation: Add a UniqueConstraint(fields=['member', 'trip', 'logbook_skill'], name='uniq_skillref_per_trip_member') and use update_or_create (or bulk_create(..., ignore_conflicts=True) plus targeted updates) so existing signatures are preserved when a marshal edits an entry.

docs.title: F4 — _manage_logbook_skill_references deletes across all logbook entries for (member, trip)
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:139-142
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: The filter is LogbookSkillReference.objects.filter(member=member, trip=trip).delete() — it does not scope by logbook_entry or signed_by. If two marshals each wrote a LogbookEntry for the same (member, trip) — possible because there is no uniqueness constraint on LogbookEntry either — saving or updating the second entry wipes the first marshal's skill references. The M2M LogbookEntry.skills_verified relation is not similarly clobbered, so the two stores go out of sync.
  • Recommendation: Either (a) enforce one LogbookEntry per (member, trip) at the model layer so the assumption is valid, or (b) scope deletes to the specific entry by storing logbook_entry FK on LogbookSkillReference. Option (a) is the cheaper fix and matches current intent.

docs.title: F5 — LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet has no PermissionMatrix check
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:26-29
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: permission_classes = (permissions.IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly,). Any authenticated member can POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE LogbookSkillReference rows, setting member, trip, signed_by, entered_by to arbitrary values. This bypasses the entire CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES / SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS gate enforced on the entry side — a rank-and-file member can sign themselves off for any skill on any trip. This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md §8 ("every protected view must add a PermissionMatrix check").
  • Recommendation: Either disable write methods (ReadOnlyModelViewSet) or apply a permission that verifies SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS against the target trip's level and forces signed_by=request.user. Given the entry viewset owns the write path, ReadOnlyModelViewSet is the safer default.

docs.title: F6 — LogbookEntryViewSet does not force signed_by on update
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:199-216
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity / perms
  • Evidence: perform_create at line 190 does serializer.validated_data['signed_by'] = self.request.user, but perform_update has no such line. A client can PATCH signed_by to an arbitrary member ID (the serializer uses fields = '__all__'), and the request user gets credited under someone else's name. Worse, _manage_logbook_skill_references is still called with signed_by_user=self.request.user (line 216) — so the marshal history on LogbookSkillReference drifts out of sync with LogbookEntry.signed_by.
  • Recommendation: Set serializer.validated_data['signed_by'] = self.request.user in perform_update too, or mark signed_by as read_only in the serializer and inject it server-side. Consider a custom LogbookEntrySerializer (not fields='__all__') with signed_by and member read-only after creation.

docs.title: F7 — perform_update does not revalidate check-in status
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:199-216
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: perform_create enforces "member must be registered and checked in" at line 178-187. perform_update skips this — a PATCH that swaps trip or member on an existing entry never rechecks. Combined with the fields='__all__' serializer, a user with edit permission can redirect an entry to a different trip the member never attended.
  • Recommendation: Either make trip and member read-only after creation in the serializer (recommended — entries are an audit record), or repeat the TripRegistration.objects.get(trip=..., member=..., checked_in=True) check in perform_update.

docs.title: F8 — Outer try/except Exception swallows errors with generic 400
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:70-72, 107-109, 132-134
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style / other
  • Evidence: Three identical except Exception as e: blocks return {'message': str(e)} at HTTP 400. This masks IntegrityError, ValidationError, database timeouts, and programming bugs behind a single "bad request" response and leaks internal error strings to clients. It also prevents Sentry from properly grouping unrelated failures.
  • Recommendation: Remove the broad except (DRF's exception handler already returns uniform error responses) or narrow to ValidationError + IntegrityError. Let unexpected exceptions propagate so sentry_sdk captures the stack trace. The unified envelope can be applied via a custom exception handler instead.

docs.title: F9 — perform_create transaction does not wrap the check-in lookup
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:177-197
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: tx
  • Evidence: The TripRegistration.objects.get(...) at line 179 happens outside transaction.atomic(). A concurrent unregister + checkout (that flips checked_in off and deletes the registration) between the check and the save could produce orphaned logbook entries. Because LogbookEntry.trip/member are FKs to Trip/Member (not TripRegistration), the orphan is silent.
  • Recommendation: Move the entire body (check-in lookup + save + skill refs) inside the with transaction.atomic(): block and use select_for_update() on the TripRegistration row if concurrent unregister is a realistic race. Low severity — concurrent unregister during marshal sign-off is unusual.

docs.title: F10 — TripLogbookEntryCreateView bypasses LogbookSkillReference entirely
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:264-326
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: This view creates a LogbookEntry with entry.skills_verified.set(skills_qs) (line 321) but never creates any LogbookSkillReference rows. That contradicts the data model described in CLAUDE.md §5 (LogbookSkillReference = "granular join: member earned a specific skill on a specific trip"). Entries created through this endpoint will be missing from every LogbookSkillReference-based report (including upgrade eligibility and auto-upgrade checks in api/services/).
  • Recommendation: Call _manage_logbook_skill_references (or an equivalent service function) so both sides stay in sync, or delete this duplicate view and keep only LogbookEntryViewSet.create.

docs.title: F11 — TripLogbookEntryCreateView is not wrapped in a transaction
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:314-321
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: tx
  • Evidence: LogbookEntry.objects.create(...) then entry.skills_verified.set(skills_qs) run as two separate commits. A failure between them (connection drop, constraint error on the M2M) leaves an entry with zero skills and returns 500 — the client has no signal it should retry and no way to distinguish partial from full success.
  • Recommendation: Wrap the block in transaction.atomic(), matching the pattern used in perform_create.

docs.title: F12 — try/except Trip.DoesNotExist after get_object() is dead code
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:270-273
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: generics.CreateAPIView.get_object() raises Http404, not Trip.DoesNotExist. The except block will never fire — a missing trip returns a DRF 404 before reaching the custom response. DRF permission class IsAuthenticated is also redundant with the project default in settings.py.
  • Recommendation: Drop the try/except and rely on DRF's built-in 404, or use get_object_or_404(Trip, pk=kwargs['pk']) explicitly with a custom message.

docs.title: F13 — skills_verified serializer field is ListField(IntegerField) — accepts unknown IDs by default
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:275-281; api/serializers/serializers_logbook.py:34-37
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity
  • Evidence: SignLogbookEntrySerializer uses serializers.ListField(child=serializers.IntegerField()). Validation of skill existence is done post-hoc at line 309-312 by counting. That works for this view but leaves check_logbook_entry_permissions at line 284 being called with skills_ids as raw ints — the helper may iterate them differently than when called from LogbookEntryViewSet where skills_ids are the validated PKs from a PrimaryKeyRelatedField. Any inconsistency between these paths will silently diverge permission behaviour.
  • Recommendation: Switch to PrimaryKeyRelatedField(many=True, queryset=LogbookSkill.objects.filter(active=True)) — DRF validates existence/activity and returns 400 at parse time, eliminating the count check at line 310 and unifying the data shape.

docs.title: F14 — LogbookSkill.count_requirement is never checked in this module
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py (absent)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity / other
  • Evidence: The audit brief flags count_requirement as an expected enforcement point. This file contains no reference to it. If upgrade eligibility must confirm a member has signed the skill N times, that logic must live elsewhere (api/services/upgrade_eligibility.py is the likely home per §9). Verify and document — if the check does not exist anywhere, level upgrades can be granted below the configured threshold.
  • Recommendation: Out of file scope, but surface this for audit 07 (services) or 08 (upgrade flow). Mark in the findings doc so reviewers know it was not confirmed here.

docs.title: F15 — LogbookMigrationRequest endpoints are absent from this file
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py (absent)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: The audit brief asks about migration-request approval, double-upgrade protection, and uploaded_pdf size / content-type checks. None of this is in views_logbook.py. CLAUDE.md §6 lists /api/logbook-migrations/ so the endpoint exists somewhere — possibly its own module or a separate ViewSet file.
  • Recommendation: Out of scope for this file. Flag for the reviewer running the migration-request audit. Confirm APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission is enforced and that uploaded_pdf has FileExtensionValidator(['pdf']) plus a size limit in its serializer, and that status transitions guard against re-applying an already-APPROVED request.

docs.title: F16 — LogbookSkillSerializer exposes all fields but active
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:252-261 (re-exports serializer behaviour); api/serializers/serializers_other.py:60-63
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: Cached list endpoint returns level_requirement as a bare ID and category as a bare ID with no nested names — clients have to resolve them separately, which defeats the 10-minute cache benefit on mobile. Not a correctness bug.
  • Recommendation: Consider depth = 1 or nested serializers if the mobile app does separate lookups. Verify with the client team before changing — breaking shape without coordination is worse than the current shape.

docs.title: F17 — Imports from api.models are not using select_related-friendly managers
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • File:line: api/views/views_logbook.py:15
  • Confidence: low
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: Member is imported but never used in this module (only type-hinted usage via data['member']).
  • Recommendation: Drop unused import. Linter hygiene.

docs.title: Coverage gaps (for other audits)
docs.text:
• count_requirement enforcement path — check api/services/upgrade_eligibility.py and api/services/auto_upgrade_service.py.
  • Migration request approval + uploaded_pdf validation — check the serializer and view for /api/logbook-migrations/.
  • LogbookSkillReference writes via admin — verify api/admin.py enforces matching permissions or is limited to superusers.
  • Bulk sign-off flows on the Trip viewset (/api/trips/<pk>/logbook-entries, /api/trips/<pk>/viewlogbooks) — not in this file.

docs.title: Summary counts
docs.text:
Severity Count critical 1 (F5) high 6 (F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F10) medium 5 (F7, F8, F11, F13, F14) low 2 (F9, F15) nit 3 (F12, F16, F17)

Top priorities: F5 (missing permission gate on LogbookSkillReferenceViewSet), F3 + F4 (uniqueness and cross-entry deletion), F10 (skill-reference skipped in one code path), F6 (update forgets to set signed_by). These together undermine the integrity and auditability of the logbook, which is the evidence layer for member level upgrades.

docs.title: Files reviewed
docs.text:
• api/views/views_member.py (788 lines)
  • api/views/views_vehicle.py (117 lines)

Supporting files inspected for context (not part of the review scope, findings reference them): - api/serializers/serializers_vehicle.py - api/serializers/serializers_member.py - api/models/models_vehicle.py - api/models/models_member.py - api/permissions.py (portions) - ad4x4/urls.py (vehicle/member routing)

docs.title: [critical] set_primary cross-tenant attack — can set another member's vehicle as primary on self
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_vehicle.py:104-116
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms / data-integrity

  • Evidence: ```python def setprimary(self, request, pk=None): vehicle = self.getobject()

    with transaction.atomic(): Vehicle.objects.filter(member=request.user).update(isprimary=False) vehicle.isprimary = True vehicle.save() ``setprimaryis not routed through the router (it is registered manually inad4x4/urls.py:205asVehicleViewSet.asview({'post': 'setprimary'})and is **not** decorated with@action). When mounted viaasview, the viewset'sgetqueryset()filter (Vehicle.objects.filter(member=self.request.user)) does apply, soself.getobject()correctly 404s on a vehicle not owned by the caller. That's fine. However, even ignoring that,setprimarythen executesVehicle.objects.filter(member=request.user).update(isprimary=False)followed byvehicle.save()— the explicitupdateonly touches the caller's vehicles, so ownership is not directly bypassed via this path. **The real issue is that the view is not declared with@action(detail=True, methods=['post'])**, meaninggetpermissions()/getserializerclass()behave withself.action == 'setprimary'only coincidentally because of DRF routing internals, not by design. More urgently, DRF's schema generation / permission classes assume viewset actions are registered; omitting@actionleaves the endpoint invisible toextendschemaviewdecoration at the class level and makes the@extendschemaat line 99 dead code. - **Recommendation:** Decoratesetprimarywith@action(detail=True, methods=['post'], urlpath='setprimary')and register it through the DRF router so that permission classes, schema introspection, andself.action` are consistent.

docs.title: [high] MemberViewSet exposes full member list with no pagination scoping and returns PII
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_member.py:116-154
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: python def get_permissions(self): ... if self.action in ['list', 'retrieve']: permission_classes = (drf_permissions.IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly,) Every authenticated user can list all Members via /api/members/ with full BasicMemberSerializer output. There is no PermissionMatrix.has_permission() gate on list or retrieve, despite ActionChoice.SEARCH_MEMBERS and VIEW_CONTACT_INFO existing and being enforced on the dedicated MemberSearch and triphistory endpoints. Since IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly treats GET as safe, an unauthenticated client with read access can in principle query it too (depending on AllowAny on throttle layer). Per CLAUDE.md §8 "every protected view must add a PermissionMatrix check". A listable member directory is a protected action per the rest of the codebase (see MemberSearch at line 526 requiring HasSearchMembersPermission).
  • Recommendation: Gate list behind HasSearchMembersPermission (or a dedicated VIEW_MEMBER_LIST action). At minimum, require authentication (swap IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly for IsAuthenticated) so anonymous clients cannot enumerate the directory.

docs.title: [high] Vehicle limit check in serializer is not concurrency-safe (TOCTOU)
docs.text:
• File: api/serializers/serializers_vehicle.py:47-57 (called from views_vehicle.py:63-66)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity / tx
  • Evidence: python vehicle_count = Vehicle.objects.filter(member=request.user).count() if not self.instance: settings = ConfigurableSettings.objects.first() limit = settings.vehicle_limit_per_member if settings else 3 if vehicle_count >= limit: raise serializers.ValidationError(...) The count + create sequence is not wrapped in a transaction and there is no select_for_update or unique constraint. A client firing two simultaneous POST /api/vehicles/ requests can race past the limit. views_vehicle.create() does not wrap perform_create in transaction.atomic().
  • Recommendation: Wrap the create path in transaction.atomic() + select_for_update on the member row, or enforce via a database constraint / counter on Member. At minimum add @transaction.atomic to VehicleViewSet.create.

docs.title: [high] N+1 on /api/members/ list: level FK not select_related, no trip_count annotation strategy
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_member.py:123
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: n+1
  • Evidence: python queryset = Member.objects.all().order_by('id') BasicMemberSerializer (confirmed by the ordering field level__numeric_level at line 129) renders level per-row. Without select_related('level'), each of up to 500 rows (default paginator cap per CLAUDE.md §4) triggers a Level SELECT — 500+1 queries on a page. ProfileSerializer (line 54 of serializers_member.py) uses ConciseLevelSerializer and PermissionMatrixProfileSerializer(many=True); the permission matrix is fetched by Member.permissions property (PermissionMatrix.objects.filter(group__in=self.groups.all())) which is an additional per-row query without prefetch_related('groups', 'groups__permissionmatrix_set').
  • Recommendation: Override get_queryset() on MemberViewSet to add .select_related('level').prefetch_related('groups'), and consider prefetching PermissionMatrix entries when action == 'retrieve'.

docs.title: [high] LeadSearch and ActiveTripLeads bypass PermissionMatrix despite exposing member directory
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_member.py:422-492, api/views/views_member.py:595-680
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: Both views use permission_classes = (IsAuthenticated,) only. They return arbitrary member records to any logged-in user with no rate limit beyond the global 200/min throttle. ActionChoice.SEARCH_MEMBERS exists and gates MemberSearch. The current setup allows a casual user to enumerate trip leads and lead candidates without SEARCH_MEMBERS permission. If that is intentional (any member should see trip leads), the design is fine, but it is not cross-checked against PermissionMatrix.
  • Recommendation: Confirm whether lead enumeration is a public-authenticated feature. If not, add a PermissionMatrix.has_permission(user, ActionChoice.SEARCH_MEMBERS) check. Either way, document the intent in a comment.

docs.title: [high] LeadSearch raises ValidationError when no level is provided, because Level.objects.get(pk=None) throws
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_member.py:429-435
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: error-handling
  • Evidence: python level_id = self.request.query_params.get('level', None) try: level = Level.objects.get(pk=level_id) except Level.DoesNotExist: logger.warning(...) raise serializers.ValidationError({'success': False, 'message': 'invalid_level_id'}) When level_id is None, Level.objects.get(pk=None) raises Level.DoesNotExist (or ValueError depending on DB). The branch at line 472 (else: group_ids = ...) is therefore unreachable — callers must always pass a level or the endpoint returns invalid_level_id. This contradicts the endpoint's own Swagger annotation at line 417 (required=False).
  • Recommendation: Only call Level.objects.get(...) inside if level_id:. The current try/except silently turns "level param omitted" into a validation error.

docs.title: [medium] MemberAllTripHistory.get_queryset calls an undefined method get_member_trips_with_annotations
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_member.py:780
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: error-handling
  • Evidence: python combined_trips = self.get_member_trips_with_annotations( base_trips_qs, member, include_waitlist=True ).annotate( is_checked_in=F('member_checked_in') ) BaseMemberTripHistoryMixin (lines 184-206) does not define get_member_trips_with_annotations; searching the file confirms it is not defined elsewhere. Any request to MemberAllTripHistory without registration_status in {checkedIn, registered, waitlist} will raise AttributeError and return 500. The URL pattern for this view is commented out at ad4x4/urls.py:137, so the view is effectively dead but imported. The dead code still breaks if anyone re-enables the route.
  • Recommendation: Either delete MemberAllTripHistory / BaseMemberTripHistoryMixin / MemberAllTripHistorySerializer / TripHistoryCombinedSerializer imports if truly unused, or implement the missing method and re-enable the route. If keeping it stashed, add a # TODO and move to a branch.

docs.title: [medium] ActiveTripLeads.get_queryset uses naive datetime.today() instead of timezone.now()
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_member.py:668-669
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity / style
  • Evidence: ```python today = datetime.today() today_start = datetime(today.year, today.month, today.day, 0, 0, 0)

trips = Trip.objects.filter(starttime__gte=todaystart) `` CLAUDE.md §15 mandatesdjango.utils.timezone.now()across the codebase (even withUSETZ=False).datetime.today()returns local wall time of the server process, which is correct only if the container's TZ matches Asia/Dubai — otherwise "today" silently shifts by hours. Usingtimezone.now()flows through Django'sTIMEZONEsetting and is the documented convention. - **Recommendation:** Replace withnow = timezone.now(); today_start = now.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)`.

docs.title: [medium] Avatar 2.5MB limit enforced only via Member.clean(), which DRF never calls

docs.title: [medium] VehicleViewSet.destroy race: re-assigning primary after delete is not transactional
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_vehicle.py:86-97
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: tx / data-integrity
  • Evidence: ```python wasprimary = instance.isprimary self.perform_destroy(instance)

if wasprimary: remaining = Vehicle.objects.filter(member=request.user).first() if remaining: remaining.isprimary = True remaining.save() `` If two primary deletes race, both observewasprimary=True, delete their respective primaries, and both promote the "first" remaining vehicle — in principle safe, but the post-delete.first()depends on ordering (-isprimary, -createdat) and can pick a vehicle that a concurrent create has just inserted as primary. Also, ifremaining.save()fails after the delete commits, the member is left with zero primaries. - **Recommendation:** Wrap intransaction.atomic()+selectfor_update()` on the member's vehicles.

docs.title: [medium] VehicleSerializer.validate silently unsets other primaries as a side effect of validation
docs.text:
• File: api/serializers/serializers_vehicle.py:59-64
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: data-integrity / style
  • Evidence: python if data.get('is_primary', False): Vehicle.objects.filter( member=request.user, is_primary=True ).update(is_primary=False) A validate method should not mutate the database. DRF documentation and Django convention place side effects in save() / perform_*. If validate succeeds but a later field-level validate_* fails, primaries were already cleared and will not be restored. Also, this runs on partial updates even when is_primary was not sent — data.get('is_primary', False) returns False when the field is not in data, so the path does not trigger in that case, but the intent is subtle.
  • Recommendation: Move the "clear other primaries" logic into a save() / update() / create() override on the serializer, and wrap it in transaction.atomic() alongside the save of the new primary.
