docs.title: Code Review — Misc Services
docs.text: Scope: api/services/gallery_webhook.py, api/services/global_settings.py, api/services/here_maps_service.py, api/services/permission_service.py. Read-only audit.

docs.title: 1. Local settings variable shadows django.conf.settings
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:51, :119, :195, :249 (every method body)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: Module imports from django.conf import settings at line 9, then each method rebinds the name: settings = get_global_settings(). A future maintainer adding settings.DEBUG or settings.GALLERY_API_TOKEN inside these methods will silently read the ConfigurableSettings row and either raise AttributeError or — worse — read an unrelated attribute. This is exactly the class of bug that causes production incidents.
  • Recommendation: rename the local to config (or conf) everywhere in the file; keep the imported django.conf.settings name untouched.

docs.title: 2. raise Exception(response) wraps a requests.Response object as an exception
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:98, :166, :228, :282
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: retry
  • Evidence: Non-200 responses raise Exception(response). This has two problems: (a) Exception is too broad and forces callers/Huey to treat every failure as a transient retry — a 400/404 from the gallery API will be retried 6 times over 6 hours before giving up (§10 lists 6 retries, 1-hour delay for create_gallery_for_trip_task, etc.); (b) the raised object is a Response, not an Exception subclass, but Python accepts arbitrary objects in Exception(...) — when Huey tries to repr/pickle this for the retry queue the response body and Authorization header (see finding 3) may be serialised into task metadata.
  • Recommendation: define a custom GalleryAPIError(Exception) that stores status_code and a sanitised message. Classify: 4xx (except 408/429) → permanent, don't retry; 5xx, 408, 429, Timeout, ConnectionError → transient, retry. Use response.raise_for_status() or an explicit status check, never raise Exception(response).

docs.title: 3. Potential secret leak in error logs
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:96, :164, :226, :280; api/services/here_maps_service.py:187
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: secret-leak
  • Evidence: Gallery error paths log response.text verbatim. If the Gallery API ever echoes back the Authorization: Bearer <GALLERY_API_TOKEN> header in an error payload (many frameworks do in 401/403/500 responses), the bearer token lands in ad4x4-web logs. Similarly, here_maps_service.py:187 returns f'HERE Maps API error: {str(e)}' as part of the API response body; requests.RequestException messages from requests can contain the full URL including apiKey query param if the exception is raised from inside a redirect or SSL handshake.
  • Recommendation: log response.status_code and a truncated body (first 200 chars) with any Bearer / apiKey= tokens scrubbed via a helper. Never include the raw exception string in a client-facing response; log internally, return a generic message.

docs.title: 4. HERE Maps API key passed as query-string parameter is logged by upstream proxies
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/here_maps_service.py:131-138
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: secret-leak
  • Evidence: apiKey is sent as a GET query parameter. This is how HERE Maps authenticates, so not a code bug per se, but nginx access logs, Sentry breadcrumbs, and any intermediate proxy will record the full URL with the key. If request.Request is logged in Sentry via the default requests integration, the key ends up in error reports.
  • Recommendation: confirm SENTRY_DSN integration is configured with send_default_pii=False (it is by default) and that the requests integration is not adding the URL with secrets to breadcrumbs. Consider placing the key in a custom header Authorization: apiKey <key> if HERE supports it; at minimum, document this in §15 gotchas.

docs.title: 5. Cache key precision / collision risk in HERE Maps
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/here_maps_service.py:78-82
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: cache
  • Evidence: Cache key built as f'geocode_{lat_rounded}_{lon_rounded}'. Values like lat=1.2, lon=34.56789 and lat=1.23456, lon=789 produce different keys here, but floats without leading zeros and with variable precision can collide under edge cases (e.g. -0.0 vs 0.0, trailing zero stripping). Round-tripping float(latitude) accepts strings that GeocodingCache.objects.get(...) may not accept with the same Decimal precision if the DB column is DecimalField. A mismatched round between memory cache write and DB lookup means the DB row is never hit and the API is called every time for certain coords.
  • Recommendation: normalise to a fixed-width string with explicit sign, e.g. f'geocode_{lat_rounded:+.6f}_{lon_rounded:+.6f}', and use the same normalised value when constructing the GeocodingCache query. Verify GeocodingCache.latitude/longitude column type and match its precision.

docs.title: 6. Inconsistent cache TTL units between memory and DB cache
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/here_maps_service.py:115 vs :169
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: cache
  • Evidence: Two different TTLs for the same cache key:
  • Line 115 (DB-cache hit path): cache.set(cache_key, result, config.here_maps_cache_duration * 60) — treating here_maps_cache_duration as minutes.
  • Line 169 (API fetch path): cache.set(cache_key, result, config.here_maps_cache_duration * 86400) — treating it as days.
  • Line 150-152: timedelta(days=config.here_maps_cache_duration) — also treats it as days for DB expiry.

The field's verbose_name in ConfigurableSettings (models_util.py:82) says "HERE Maps Cache duration in minutes" (default 1440). So the DB-cache-hit path is correct (*60 = minutes to seconds), and both the API-fetch path and expires_at are wrong: 1440 days is 4 years of memory caching and DB expiry, not 1 day. - Recommendation: decide on a unit (minutes is stated), then apply consistently: cache.set(..., config.here_maps_cache_duration * 60) in both paths, and timedelta(minutes=config.here_maps_cache_duration) for the DB expires_at. This is a real behavioural bug in production once HERE Maps is enabled.

docs.title: 7. get_global_settings creates a singleton during a GET-style call
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/global_settings.py:17-23
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: null-ref
  • Evidence: When the cache misses and the DB row is missing, get_global_settings writes a new ConfigurableSettings with whatever Group.objects.first() and the lowest-numeric Level happen to be. This is nominally what §15 warns about ("service handles this") but:
  • Group.objects.first() and Level.objects.order_by('numeric_level').first() can themselves be None on a truly empty DB. ConfigurableSettings.default_user_group and default_user_level fields are FKs; the model allows them to be null? Verify. If they're non-null, creation crashes mid-request with IntegrityError.
  • Any read-only request (e.g. GET /api/auth/profile/ during middleware) will spontaneously write to the DB on a cold cache, producing surprising behaviour and write load during read traffic surges after a Redis flush.
  • The settings.save() on line 22 is redundant — objects.create already saved the row.
  • Recommendation: fail loud when the singleton row is absent in production (raise ImproperlyConfigured); provide a management command seed_global_settings or a data migration. If keeping the auto-create path, wrap in transaction.atomic() and handle IntegrityError/None FKs gracefully.

docs.title: 8. cache.get('global_settings') falsy check is wrong for cached model instance
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/services/global_settings.py:16
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: cache
  • Evidence: if not settings: — for a Django model instance this evaluates __bool__ which is True for any model; a cached None (Django's cache backend will store None if explicitly set) would retrigger the fetch. This happens to work but is subtly wrong.
  • Recommendation: use a sentinel. settings = cache.get('global_settings', SENTINEL); if settings is SENTINEL: .... Minor but idiomatic.

docs.title: 9. Caching a live model instance across requests
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/global_settings.py:23
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: cache
  • Evidence: A pickled ConfigurableSettings instance goes into Redis for 5 minutes. Stale instances may retain stale relations (default_user_group), and the invalidation signal at line 28 is registered on post_save. That misses: direct UPDATE SQL, admin bulk actions that bypass save(), signals disconnected during tests, and cache eviction unreliability. Worse, the cached instance carries old M2M/FK caches, so settings.default_user_level.name may point at stale data. In production with USE_TZ=False, staleness bugs tend to manifest as "why did that email just get sent from the old address".
  • Recommendation: cache a plain dict of the handful of fields the callers actually use, not the full model. Or cache by field with cache.get_or_set per field. Alternatively, accept the staleness and document it in §15.

docs.title: 10. requests.get/requests.post timeout defaults from DB — no fallback
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/services/here_maps_service.py:137; api/services/gallery_webhook.py:78, :146, :216, :270
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: timeout
  • Evidence: Timeouts come from config.here_maps_request_timeout / settings.gallery_api_timeout. If an admin accidentally sets 0 in Django admin, requests interprets timeout=0 as "no timeout" on some platforms, hanging Gunicorn worker indefinitely and blocking Huey tasks for the full retry window (1 hour × 6 = 6 hours per stuck trip). No lower bound validation on the model field.
  • Recommendation: add validators=[MinValueValidator(1), MaxValueValidator(120)] on the IntegerField definitions, and clamp at read time: timeout = max(1, min(120, config.gallery_api_timeout)). Also set a hard ceiling in code regardless of config.

docs.title: 11. Gallery webhook: no idempotency, retries may create duplicate galleries
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:33-108
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: idempotency
  • Evidence: create_gallery_for_trip is called from a Huey task that retries 6 times. The payload contains trip_id, but if the request succeeds remotely and the response times out or is lost on the way back, the retry creates a second gallery. The caller stores the returned gallery_id on the Trip; if the first-call response was lost, the second call's id overwrites the first, leaving an orphan gallery on the remote. Nothing in the payload is an idempotency key.
  • Recommendation: add an idempotency_key (UUID deterministic from trip_id + created_at) to every webhook payload; have the Gallery API return the existing gallery when the key matches. Alternatively, have the Gallery API treat trip_id as a unique constraint and return the existing record on duplicate POST.

docs.title: 12. update_gallery_for_trip runs even when trip.gallery_id is missing
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:111-176
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: idempotency
  • Evidence: delete_gallery_for_trip early-returns when trip.gallery_id is falsy (line 200). update_gallery_for_trip has no such guard: if a trip never had a gallery created (e.g. auto_create_trip_gallery=False), every edit still POSTs to /trip/updated. Either the remote errors (wastes 6 retries) or silently no-ops (creates an orphan expectation).
  • Recommendation: mirror the delete guard — early return when not trip.gallery_id.

docs.title: 13. Error log message says "creating gallery" in the update / delete / restore paths
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:163, :169, :172, :175 (update_gallery_for_trip)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: Copy-paste from create_gallery_for_trip: every error log in update_gallery_for_trip says "creating gallery" — "Failed to create gallery for trip …" on an update path, "Gallery API timeout when creating gallery" on update timeout, "Network error creating gallery" on update network error. Hard to debug production incidents when the operation is mislabelled.
  • Recommendation: replace "creating" with the correct verb per method.

docs.title: 14. creator_avatar attribute access will crash if profile has no avatar_url
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:68, :136
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: null-ref
  • Evidence: trip.lead.profile.avatar_url if trip.lead and hasattr(trip.lead, 'profile') else None. hasattr checks that trip.lead has a profile attribute, but accessing .profile.avatar_url will raise AttributeError if the profile object doesn't have avatar_url, which hasattr didn't guard. Also, Member in this codebase is itself AUTH_USER_MODEL with an avatar field on it — the profile relation is worth re-examining (may be a legacy attribute).
  • Recommendation: getattr(getattr(trip.lead, 'profile', None), 'avatar_url', None). Or just pull from trip.lead.avatar (Member.avatar ImageField exists per §5) and skip the intermediate model.

docs.title: 15. permission_service.superuser_or_has_permission duplicates permission_matrix_exists_or_user_is_superuser
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/permission_service.py:5-14 vs api/permissions.py:15-30
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms-drift
  • Evidence: Two near-identical functions exist with different signatures:
  • permissions.permission_matrix_exists_or_user_is_superuser(user, action, level=None) — the canonical, widely-used helper (40+ call sites per grep above).
  • services.permission_service.superuser_or_has_permission(level, request_user, action) — same logic, different argument order, used in three spots in views_trip.py.

The semantic mismatch with PermissionMatrix.has_permission is worse: the model method (api/models/models.py:77) takes (user, action, member=None, trip=None, require_trip_lead=False) and has special-case handling for CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER and member-level resolution. None of the service-layer helpers honour that. §8 of CLAUDE.md says: "PermissionMatrix.has_permission(user, action, member, trip, require_trip_lead) is the single authoritative check". These helpers violate that rule. - Recommendation: delete superuser_or_has_permission; migrate the three views_trip.py call sites to permission_matrix_exists_or_user_is_superuser (already imported elsewhere). Over the medium term, consolidate that function into PermissionMatrix.has_permission so drift is impossible.

docs.title: 16. check_logbook_entry_permissions returns stale decisions
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/permission_service.py:17-64
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: perms-drift
  • Evidence: The function has five code paths and returns (False, False) early on line 52 only after computing can_create_logbook_entry. If the user is editing their own logbook (user == member) and is NOT a superuser, the function returns (False, False) even when the user IS lead/deputy for the trip. It's unclear whether self-editing is forbidden for leads (I'd expect leads to be able to sign their own skills), but the flow suggests yes. The logic is hard to follow and the check at line 51 runs after the expensive DB lookups on lines 42-49, wasting queries when the answer is predetermined.
  • Recommendation: restructure with early returns. Add a docstring with a decision table (user role × self vs other × skills present). Consider a unit test that enumerates the 8 combinations explicitly.

docs.title: 17. PermissionMatrix queries inside loops (N+1)
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/services/permission_service.py:7-12, api/services/permission_service.py:43-49
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: superuser_or_has_permission does up to two sequential PermissionMatrix.objects.filter(...).exists() queries per call. check_logbook_entry_permissions calls it multiple times per request (CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER, CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES, SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS), plus a TripRegistration.objects.get(...) per logbook entry. In bulk logbook-entry endpoints this is 4-5 queries per member. The permission matrix is small and near-static — it should be cached.
  • Recommendation: cache a per-user (or per-group) permission summary in memory/Redis for 60 seconds; invalidate on PermissionMatrix / Group.user_set change via signals.

docs.title: 18. HERE Maps service returns raw exception strings in API response
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • File:line: api/services/here_maps_service.py:185-195
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: secret-leak
  • Evidence: return {'success': False, 'error': f'HERE Maps API error: {str(e)}', ...} and f'Internal error: {str(e)}' return internal exception messages to the API client. requests.RequestException can include the full URL with apiKey=... query string. Also leaks internal stack trace hints. The generic except Exception on line 190 is a catch-all that will mask bugs.
  • Recommendation: log internally with logger.exception(...), return a generic 'Reverse geocoding failed' to the client. Drop the broad except Exception or narrow it to specific anticipated failure modes.

docs.title: 19. _extract_fields swallows exceptions silently
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/services/here_maps_service.py:233-235
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: except Exception as e: logger.error(f'Error extracting fields: {e}'); return {}. An empty dict is then written to the DB cache as a valid geocoding result, meaning any malformed HERE Maps response poisons the cache with empties for that lat/lon for here_maps_cache_duration minutes (which, per finding 6, could be 4 years).
  • Recommendation: on parse failure, re-raise so the outer handler treats it as a transient error; do NOT cache the empty result.

docs.title: 20. Module-level getattr(settings, 'GALLERY_API_TOKEN', '') is evaluated once at import
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • File:line: api/services/gallery_webhook.py:19
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • Evidence: Captured at import time. If the token is rotated and settings are reloaded (e.g. via django-constance or env refresh), the service keeps the old value until process restart.
  • Recommendation: read inside _get_headers() via settings.GALLERY_API_TOKEN, and keep from django.conf import settings (note the collision with finding 1 — rename the local settings first).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highest-impact fixes, in priority order: 1. Rename the settings local in gallery_webhook.py (finding 1) — trivial, prevents a whole class of bugs. 2. Fix the HERE Maps cache TTL unit inconsistency (finding 6) — behavioural bug. 3. Replace raise Exception(response) + classify transient vs permanent errors (finding 2) — cuts retry storms. 4. Sanitise error logs and response bodies (findings 3, 4, 18) — secret-leak surface. 5. Unify permission helpers around PermissionMatrix.has_permission (finding 15) — per CLAUDE.md §8 this is a documented architectural rule.

None of the findings require schema changes beyond minor model validators (finding 10). All are in-service refactors.

docs.title: Code Review — Notifications Stack
docs.text:
Audit date: 2026-04-22. Mode: READ-ONLY.

Scope: api/views/views_clubnews.py, api/views/views_notificationsettings.py, api/views/views_pushnotification.py, api/services/notification_service.py, api/services/email_notifications.py, api/services/push_notifications.py, api/services/telegram_notifications.py, api/services/store_notifications.py.

Referenced collaborators (read for context, not in audit scope): api/background.py, api/signals.py, api/models/models.py (ClubNews), api/services/trip_registration_service.py, api/views/views_trip.py, templates/emails/*.

docs.title: F-01 [critical] [immutability] send_club_wide_news flips status to SENT inside the channel fan-out loop, so partial failures leave the record immutable-but-undelivered
docs.text:
File: api/services/notification_service.py lines 125–134.

def send_club_wide_news(self, data: ClubNews):
    logger.info(...)
    for channel in self.channels:
        try:
            channel.send_club_wide_news(data)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(...)
            logger.exception(e)
    data.status = ClubNewsStatus.SENT
    data.save()

Two concrete problems flow from this block.

  1. Double-send on Huey retry. send_club_news is declared @task(retries=2, retry_delay=300) in api/background.py:80. Channel implementations (send_club_wide_news in each channel) are also @task()-decorated — they enqueue nested Huey tasks. If any channel raises synchronously (e.g., the queryset blows up before enqueuing), the manager swallows it, flips status to SENT, saves. But on transient errors before the final data.save(), the outer send_club_news task will retry — and because ClubNewsStatus.SENT is set only on the final pass, the retry fans out to every channel again, enqueuing a second batch of per-channel tasks. Members receive duplicate emails/pushes.
  2. Immutability trap on partial failure. The try/except inside the loop silently eats every exception from every channel, yet the manager still sets status=SENT unconditionally. If push succeeds but email fails, or vice-versa, the record is now immutable (ClubNews.save() raises ValidationError once status==SENT, §15) and cannot be resent or corrected. Admin has no way to retry just the failed channel short of DB surgery.

Recommendation: move the data.status = SENT; data.save() into the successful branch of an all-channels-succeeded check, or drive status off an audit trail of per-channel delivery. At minimum, log a warning and skip the SENT flip if any channel raised.

docs.title: F-02 [critical] [on-commit] Notifications fire during add_users_from_waitlist inside an implicit transaction — rollback still pings users
docs.text:
File: api/services/trip_registration_service.py lines 29–41.

while trip.registered.count() < trip.capacity and len(waitlist_registrations) > 0:
    user = waitlist_registrations.pop(0).member
    trip.registered.add(user, through_defaults={'trip': trip})
    trip.waitlist.remove(user)
    send_registration_from_waitlist_notification(user, trip)

send_registration_from_waitlist_notification is a Huey @task — in production it pushes a message to Redis immediately. If the request is wrapped in a transaction.atomic() block further up (DRF's ATOMIC_REQUESTS may or may not be on, but individual service flows like trip_registration_service.remove_from_registered can be called mid-transaction by upstream handlers) and that transaction rolls back, the waitlist moves are undone but the notification has already been enqueued — members get "you're registered" emails for trips they're no longer registered for.

Same pattern in remove_from_registered (line 49) and remove_from_waitlist. Same pattern in views_trip.py:107,516,517,541 where send_trip_notification and send_trip_approval_notification are fired right after trip.save() without on_commit.

Recommendation: wrap every send_* enqueue in transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_x(...)). This is a one-line fix per call site and is the standard Django idiom for Celery/Huey-adjacent code.

Signal club_news_post_save at api/signals.py:89 has the same issue — post_save fires before the outer transaction commits, so on rollback the enqueued task runs against a row that no longer exists or still has the pre-save status.

docs.title: F-03 [high] [idempotency] Per-channel Huey tasks retry independently but have no delivery receipt — retries duplicate sends
docs.text:
Every channel method (EmailNotificationChannel.send_new_trip_notification, PushNotificationChannel.send_new_trip_notification, etc.) is itself @task(). None of them is idempotent: there is no "already sent" marker, no dedup key, no NotificationLog.objects.get_or_create. Combined with the outer send_trip_notification task (retries=2), a transient SMTP timeout that Huey treats as a failed task will re-enqueue the email task, which will re-run the full DB query and email every matching user again.

The StoreNotificationChannel.send_new_trip_notification task creates NotificationLog rows with no uniqueness constraint (store_notifications.py:30). A retry produces duplicate rows.

Recommendation: Either (a) introduce a compound unique constraint on NotificationLog (member, type, related_object_id, related_object_type) with get_or_create semantics, or (b) gate each channel task on a per-task idempotency key (e.g., trip_id + channel_name) stored in a NotificationDispatch audit table.

docs.title: F-04 [high] [on-commit] ClubNewsNotificationAPIView.post enqueues send_club_news(validated_data) with raw dict, not persisted ClubNews
docs.text:
File: api/views/views_pushnotification.py lines 26–30.

def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    serializer = self.get_serializer(data=request.data)
    serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
    send_club_news(serializer.validated_data)
    return Response(...)

send_club_news(data) in background.py:81 expects a ClubNews model instance (it calls notification_manager.send_club_wide_news(data), which ends with data.status = ClubNewsStatus.SENT; data.save()). Here it is handed serializer.validated_data, which is a plain dict. The .save() call on a dict will raise AttributeError inside Huey — which will then retry the task twice (retries=2). Two retries of something that can never succeed, three failures logged per admin push.

Additionally, CustomPushNotificationSerializer is a plain serializers.Serializer, not a ModelSerializer — validated_data will not contain the correct ClubNews fields (title, content, levels, status) in a shape the downstream consumer expects. The fan-out in email/push channels reads data.levels.count(), data.title, data.content — those only work on a model instance.

This endpoint looks broken as shipped, or it is dead code. Either way, it warrants verification.

docs.title: F-05 [high] [error-handling] Swallowed exceptions in NotificationManager hide channel failures from Huey's retry logic
docs.text:
File: api/services/notification_service.py lines 71–192.

Every send_* method on NotificationManager wraps its per-channel dispatch in try/except Exception + logger.error + logger.exception, and then continues. Outcomes:

  • A real failure never propagates, so Huey's @task(retries=2, retry_delay=300) wrappers in background.py never see it and never retry.
  • logger.exception(e) called twice per failure (once as error, once as exception) produces two tracebacks in Sentry/logs per event, inflating noise.
  • Operators cannot distinguish "one channel down, rest delivered" from "all channels down" via alerting.

Recommendation: drop the try/except or re-raise after logging the first one. Let Huey retries handle transient failures. Use logger.exception(...) once — it already prints the message plus traceback; the extra logger.error(...) line before it is redundant.

The per-method logging also has the typo notificiation (lines 77, 86 at minimum) — minor, but search-unfriendly.

docs.title: F-06 [high] [pii] Dry-run logs dump full HTML bodies, addresses, and Telegram payloads at INFO level
docs.text:
File: api/services/email_notifications.py lines 37, 169, 206, 239; api/services/telegram_notifications.py line 171.

logger.info(f'Dry run: Email sent to {msg.to} with subject {msg.subject} and content {html_content}')

In dry-run mode, the full rendered HTML (including recipient name, phone, email, feedback body, trip details) is written to logs at INFO. Similarly telegram_notifications.py:171 logs the formatted feedback message — which contains email, phone, and the first 200 chars of the user's feedback. These logs stream to Sentry breadcrumbs and any aggregation backend.

Given dry-run is the default in dev (NotificationSettings default notification_dry_run=True, models_util.py:69) and the same logging path is hit every test run, this is GDPR-relevant PII in every dev/CI log stream.

Recommendation: log subject + recipient count in dry-run mode, not the full body. If full-body dry-run is required for template debugging, gate it behind DEBUG=True or a separate flag and redact email addresses/phone numbers.

docs.title: F-07 [high] [pii] Phone number and email always logged by TelegramNotificationChannel._format_feedback_message when sent for real
docs.text:
File: api/services/telegram_notifications.py lines 148–156, 171.

The formatted feedback message includes user.email and user.phone, and line 171 logs the entire formatted message before sending. Even outside dry-run, every feedback produces an INFO log containing email + phone + first 200 chars of message. This is production PII in logs.

Recommendation: log only feedback.id and feedback.user.username at INFO; keep the full formatted message local to the bot.send_message call.

docs.title: F-08 [high] [template-injection] Feedback email template renders user-supplied message without escaping, and uses raw HTML body
docs.text:
File: templates/emails/feedback_received.html + api/services/email_notifications.py:149–172.

<p>{{ context.message }}</p>

Django templates autoescape by default, so < becomes < in HTML context — that's safe. However: the EmailMultiAlternatives object in send_feedback_notification is constructed with html_content as the plaintext body (positional arg 2 of EmailMultiAlternatives, which is body). Then msg.attach_alternative(html_content, "text/html") attaches the same HTML as the HTML alternative. Result: the plaintext part of the email is literal HTML markup (not user-readable), and the HTML part relies entirely on the template engine's autoescape.

feedback_received.html does not use |safe, so Django's autoescape saves the day here. But this same pattern is used by _send_email (line 20) for every template. If anyone ever adds {{ context.message|safe }} or a custom admin-controlled template with HTML, feedback messages, trip titles, and trip lead display names become an HTML-injection vector that lands in an admin or member's inbox.

Recommendation: (a) render a real plain-text body via a .txt template and pass it as the positional body arg, with the HTML going into attach_alternative. (b) document in CLAUDE.md §14 that notification templates must never use |safe on user-controlled fields.

Related: trip.title is rendered into push notification body and Telegram markdown. Push body is plain text and safe. Telegram uses escape_markdown(..., version=2) consistently except _format_trip_message line 49 — which does escape — so Telegram is OK. Email/HTML remains the risk surface.

docs.title: F-09 [high] [batching] FCM devices fetched without .only() / .select_related() and iterated instead of batched where possible
docs.text:
File: api/services/push_notifications.py.

  • _send_msg_to_devices calls devices.send_message(...) on a QuerySet — that is fcm_django's batched bulk API. Good. But before sending it calls devices.count() (a separate SQL COUNT), then send_message re-evaluates the queryset — at minimum one redundant round trip. For larger sends this is two full queryset scans.
  • send_new_trip_notification (line 85) uses len(users) on a values_list queryset, which forces evaluation into a Python list; then subscribed_user_devices = FCMDevice.objects.filter(user__in=users, active=True) re-queries. Given users is already evaluated, passing it as a list is fine, but the pattern differs from .exists() / .count() elsewhere.
  • send_club_wide_news line 182: if data.levels.count() == 0 and data.levels.count() == 0: — duplicated condition; the second clause is a copy-paste bug. data.levels.count() is also called three times in a row — one cached call would suffice. Same duplication in store_notifications.py:134 and email_notifications.py:115.
  • send_club_wide_news queries NotificationSettings without checking last_user_activity filtering that store_notifications.py does apply (60-day activity threshold) — inconsistent audience between channels. Email and push go to everyone who opted in; store goes to active users only. Dormant users get emails/push but no in-app notification entry.

Recommendation: consolidate audience resolution into a helper so all three channels share the same query. Collapse the duplicated .count() check. Decide whether inactive users should receive any channel.

docs.title: F-10 [medium] [error-handling] _send_email sleeps inside the send loop with no bulk send, no chunking, no async
docs.text:
File: api/services/email_notifications.py lines 19–40.

for user in users:
    msg.to = [user.email]
    msg.attach_alternative(html_content, "text/html")
    ...
    time.sleep(conf_settings.email_sleep_period_ms/1000)

Two issues.

  1. Reusing the same EmailMultiAlternatives object across iterations: msg.attach_alternative(html_content, "text/html") appends a new alternative each iteration. By the Nth user, the message has N identical HTML alternatives attached. SMTP servers may reject or most clients render only the first, but the outgoing payload grows linearly — wasted bandwidth.
  2. time.sleep(...) blocks the Huey worker thread. For a 1000-user club-wide news send at 100ms sleep, that's 100 seconds of blocked worker. Huey workers are a finite pool; other tasks back up. Use @task() per email with the sleep replaced by Huey's delay= scheduling, or batch via an SMTP-level rate limiter.

Recommendation: instantiate EmailMultiAlternatives per-user inside the loop, or use send_mass_mail / a real transactional email service.

docs.title: F-11 [medium] [perms] ClubNewsNotificationAPIView does not check PermissionMatrix — falls back to Django is_superuser
docs.text:
File: api/views/views_pushnotification.py line 20.

permission_classes = (IsAdminUserOrReadOnly,) which in permissions.py:394 checks request.user.is_superuser. Per CLAUDE.md §8: "Do not use Django model-level permissions (is_staff, is_superuser) for business logic; those are admin-panel shortcuts only. […] every protected view must add a PermissionMatrix check." Sending a club-wide push is a protected action. Add a PermissionMatrix.has_permission(request.user, ActionChoice.<SEND_CLUB_NEWS_OR_SIMILAR>) check.

docs.title: F-12 [medium] [perms] MarkNotificationLogAsReadView uses a CreateAPIView for an update action
docs.text:
File: api/views/views_pushnotification.py lines 33–58.

A mark-as-read operation is not a create — it mutates existing rows. Using CreateAPIView with an unbound queryset = NotificationLog.objects.all() exposes all notification logs via DRF's generic introspection (e.g., OPTIONS), which a non-admin can call. The actual post method correctly filters by member=request.user, so the data path is safe, but the view shape is misleading.

Minor: notifications.count() != len(notification_ids) treats duplicates in the input as errors (count of distinct matches vs count of input IDs). [1, 1, 2] with two existing rows returns 400 because count=2 vs len=3. Deduplicate the input first or use set(notification_ids).

Recommendation: use APIView with PATCH semantics, or at minimum an explicit @action(detail=False, methods=['post']) on NotificationLogViewSet.

docs.title: F-13 [medium] [style] NotificationLogViewSet.get_queryset hard-codes [:20]
docs.text:
File: api/views/views_pushnotification.py lines 65–67.

Returning the latest 20 notifications bypasses DRF pagination (StandardResultsSetPagination) because slicing a queryset prevents it from being paginated by DRF. Clients cannot retrieve older notifications. Given NotificationLog is purged at 60 days, this is a soft-limit of 20 latest in a 60-day window. Prefer real pagination; if a "last 20" view is really wanted, expose it as a distinct action and keep the default listing paginated.

docs.title: F-14 [medium] [immutability] ClubNewsViewSet is read-only but list filters only status='SENT'
docs.text:
File: api/views/views_clubnews.py lines 8–15.

queryset = ClubNews.objects.filter(status='SENT') uses a hard-coded string rather than ClubNewsStatus.SENT. ClubNewsStatus is an enum (used elsewhere). Use the enum constant to avoid drift if the value is renamed.

Also: the ViewSet is ReadOnlyModelViewSet and permissions.AllowAny, so anonymous users can read all SENT club news. Per §6 documented endpoints this appears intentional, but given some news is level-gated (levels M2M), an anonymous client sees news intended only for specific levels — the level filter is only applied at send time, not at read time. If that's the intent, document it; if not, add a queryset filter tied to request.user.level.

docs.title: F-15 [medium] [style] NotificationSettingsApiView.patch delegates to put — partial semantics correct but misleading
docs.text:
File: api/views/views_notificationsettings.py lines 24–34.

Both put and patch use partial=True, which is correct for PATCH but wrong for PUT — PUT should require the full representation. Tests and clients can therefore omit required fields and still get 200 from a PUT. Either enforce partial=False on PUT or collapse into a single PATCH-only view (DRF has UpdateAPIView with GET+PATCH support).

get_or_create(member_id=self.request.user.id) runs on every GET — creating a row on read is a side effect that makes GET /profile/notificationsettings non-idempotent. Prefer get_or_create in a signal on Member creation (or lazy-create on first PATCH only).

docs.title: F-16 [low] [style] ConfigurableSettings.objects.first() called without None guard in multiple places
docs.text:
Files: api/services/push_notifications.py:18,41,58; api/services/email_notifications.py:220.

Per CLAUDE.md §15: "ConfigurableSettings.objects.first() can return None. […] Always guard: check for None before accessing fields, or use the global_settings.py service which handles this." Email code already uses get_global_settings() in _send_email but the two account-deletion paths use the raw .first() (line 220 in email). Push code always uses raw .first(). In test/dev if the settings row is missing, every push enqueue raises AttributeError inside the Huey worker, which then silently retries.

docs.title: F-17 [low] [style] Unused variable and redundant level_name
docs.text:
File: api/services/push_notifications.py lines 87, 20.

Line 87: level_name = trip.level.name is assigned but never used. Line 20: NotificationType imported but also used via store_notifications.py:10 — fine, but the unused local at line 87 is dead code. Same in store_notifications.py:19 (level_name = trip.level.name never read).

docs.title: F-18 [low] [style] send_upgrade_request_created wrapped per-channel reveals applicant rather than using cached username lookup
docs.text:
File: api/services/email_notifications.py lines 94–98.

username = upgrade_request.applicant_str
try:
    username = upgrade_request.applicant.username
except AttributeError:
    pass

Replace with username = upgrade_request.applicant.username if upgrade_request.applicant else upgrade_request.applicant_str — clearer and avoids using exception flow for regular logic.

docs.title: F-19 [nit] [style] Docstrings and logging typos
docs.text:
• notificiation misspelled in notification_service.py lines 77, 86, 95, 104, 113.
  • send_club_wide_news duplicated condition data.levels.count() == 0 and data.levels.count() == 0 in three files.
  • email_notifications.py:153 f-string with no interpolation: f'templates/emails/feedback_received.html'.

docs.title: Non-findings (checked, not an issue)
docs.text:
• Telegram escaping uses escape_markdown(..., version=2) consistently; no Markdown injection via user content.
  • ClubNews.save() does enforce immutability once status=SENT (models.py:155–161), so direct DB writes are safe. The risk in F-01 is the application flow producing a SENT record when the send was partial, not the model check itself.
  • Push notifications already use fcm_django's batched send_message on a QuerySet rather than per-device iteration — batching works correctly.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Severity Count critical 2 high 7 medium 6 low 3 nit 1

Highest-leverage fixes: add transaction.on_commit wrappers at every send_* call site (F-02), and restructure send_club_wide_news so SENT is only set on all-success (F-01). Those two together eliminate the double-send and immutability-on-failure paths. F-04 warrants verification to determine if ClubNewsNotificationAPIView is reachable in production or dead.

docs.title: Files reviewed
docs.text:
• api/views/views_trip.py (1114 loc)
  • api/services/trip_registration_service.py (102 loc)

Context sources: CLAUDE.md §7/§8/§14/§15, api/permissions.py (for permission-class semantics).

docs.title: [critical] CancelTripRegistration calls notification helpers with wrong signature
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_trip.py:436,439
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: error-handling / correctness
  • Evidence: python send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification(user, trip) ... send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification(user, trip) Every other caller (e.g. RemoveMemberFromTripRegistration at line 405/409 and TripRegistrationService.remove_from_registered/remove_from_waitlist) passes a single cancellation/TripRegistrationCancellationReason object. Since send_* are Huey tasks (@db_task), any argument-shape mismatch will only surface when the task executes, producing silent background failures. Users will see trip_registration_cancelled success, but no notification is sent and the task retries 2x then dies.
  • Recommendation: Route through the service: TripRegistrationService.remove_from_registered(user, trip) / remove_from_waitlist(user, trip), and create a TripRegistrationCancellationReason row (even with a default reason like SELF_CANCELLED) so the notification task has a consistent argument. Verify the task signature in api/background.py and align all call sites.

docs.title: [critical] trip.cut_off < datetime.datetime.now() violates USE_TZ=False convention
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_trip.py:294, 370
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other (timezone gotcha, §15)
  • Evidence: python if trip.cut_off < datetime.datetime.now(): CLAUDE.md §15 explicitly warns: "Never use datetime.datetime.now() — use django.utils.timezone.now()." With USE_TZ=False the two happen to coincide in naive Asia/Dubai time today, but any future migration to TZ-aware datetimes will silently break cutoff checks, and the project convention is already violated.
  • Recommendation: from django.utils import timezone and replace with timezone.now(). Remove the bare import datetime at the top of the file if no longer needed.

docs.title: [high] RegisterForTrip has contradictory permission branching — permission holders skip all validation
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_trip.py:273-281
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: perms
  • Evidence: python if permission_matrix_exists_or_user_is_superuser(user, ActionChoice.EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS): ... msg = add_to_registered(user, trip, vehicle=vehicle) return Response(...) Users with EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS skip every sanity check below: trip-approval status, level-requirement, cutoff, capacity, duplicate registration. That may be intentional for admin-driven registration, but this endpoint is /api/trips/<pk>/register (member-initiated). Admin force-registration is supposed to flow through ForceRegisterForTrip. Bypassing trip_already_registered and trip_full silently is a footgun — capacity can be over-run without any audit trail.
  • Recommendation: Either document the bypass explicitly, or remove the early branch and let permissioned users go through the normal flow (with a separate bypass_capacity flag on ForceRegisterForTrip for the admin path). At minimum, keep the trip_already_registered check above the permission branch.

docs.title: [high] Missing transaction boundaries around multi-row mutations
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_trip.py:93-107, 169-178, 400-415, 510-519; api/services/trip_registration_service.py:14-26, 29-41
  • Confidence: high

RemoveMemberFromTripRegistration.post builds an unsaved TripRegistrationCancellationReason, mutates M2M, fires a Huey task, then saves the cancellation and the trip. If any step fails mid-flight you get partial state (member added but not checked in, trip approved but notification never queued, cancellation notified but cancellation row never persisted).
  • Recommendation: Wrap each multi-row endpoint in with transaction.atomic(): and use transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_*) for Huey enqueues so notifications never fire for rolled-back transactions. This matters more once Huey is production-async.

docs.title: Code Review: Upgrade Flow
docs.text:
Audit of api/views/views_upgrade.py, api/views/views_upgraderequest.py, api/services/upgrade_eligibility.py, and api/services/auto_upgrade_service.py.

Focus areas: race conditions in voting, transaction atomicity in approval, N+1 queries, permission-matrix coverage, verdict reason handling, auto-upgrade vs manual-upgrade conflicts, applicant_str backup, idempotency on logbook completion, and timezone.now() vs datetime.datetime.now() under USE_TZ=False.

docs.title: F1 — Approve/Decline path is not atomic (missing transaction.atomic)
docs.text:
• Severity: critical
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: tx
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:106-127
  • Evidence: handle_upgrade_request_verdict() performs four distinct writes — upgrade_request.save() (status/finalapprover/verdictdate), applicant.level = target_level, applicant.groups.add(auto_group), applicant.save() — followed by send_upgrade_request_handled_notification(...). None of this is wrapped in transaction.atomic. A DB error or process crash between steps leaves the system in a corrupt state: request marked APPROVED but member still at old level, or member promoted to new level without the auto_group assignment (which governs PermissionMatrix checks elsewhere). The notification is also fired from inside the view — if the preceding save succeeded but a later save raises, the member is notified of a half-applied upgrade.
  • Recommendation: Wrap the mutation block in transaction.atomic(), then fire send_upgrade_request_handled_notification only after the transaction commits (use transaction.on_commit(...)). The Huey task should be enqueued post-commit to avoid the classic "task runs before row is visible" race.

docs.title: F2 — Voting endpoint has a TOCTOU race on status
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: race
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:232-257
  • Evidence: UpgradeRequestVoteView.post() reads upgrade_request.status at line 234, then does M2M adds/removes (lines 239-250), then unconditionally re-assigns status=IN_PROGRESS and calls .save() (lines 254-256). Two simultaneous requests (one voter, one approver pressing approve/decline) can race: approver transitions status to APPROVED, voter then silently overwrites to IN_PROGRESS because the voter loaded a stale instance. Result: an approved upgrade appears back "in progress" and the applicant has already been upgraded. Also, because .save() writes the whole row, any other field mutated concurrently is clobbered.
  • Recommendation: Use select_for_update() inside transaction.atomic when fetching upgrade_request, re-check the status guard after lock, and .save(update_fields=['status']) to narrow the write. Better yet, do the M2M mutations after the status guard is re-verified.

docs.title: F3 — Vote is not atomic across three M2M operations
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: race
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:239-250
  • Evidence: Each vote branch does add() to one list and remove() from two others as three separate queries. A failure (connection drop, timeout) after add() but before remove() leaves a user counted in two vote buckets simultaneously. The annotated counts on the queryset (yes_voters_count, no_voters_count, defer_voters_count, line 26-30) will then double-count that voter, skewing the verdict view.
  • Recommendation: Wrap the three M2M operations in transaction.atomic. Consider a single vote field on a through-model with a UniqueConstraint(fields=['upgrade_request', 'member']) — this makes vote-change an update/upsert rather than three independent writes.

docs.title: F4 — Auto-upgrade has no lock and can race with manual approval
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: race
  • File: api/services/auto_upgrade_service.py:30-49
  • Evidence: handle_logbook_entry_created reads member.level_id, compares to source_level.id, then writes member.level = target_level and member.save(). No lock, no transaction.atomic, no guard against a concurrent manual approval that is also writing applicant.level. Two simultaneous triggers (e.g., marshal signs a logbook entry while an approver clicks approve) can produce: (a) double-group-add (benign but noisy), (b) partial rollback of the manual upgrade's group change, or (c) member.save() clobbering unrelated fields the other request just wrote. The guard on member.level_id != source_level.id at line 33 is the only idempotency check — it is effective only if both paths see the same "before" state.
  • Recommendation: Wrap the whole routine in transaction.atomic and fetch the member under select_for_update(). Also use .save(update_fields=['level']) instead of a full-row save.

docs.title: F5 — Auto-downgrade race when logbook entry is deleted
docs.text:
• Severity: high
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: race
  • File: api/services/auto_upgrade_service.py:77-94
  • Evidence: handle_logbook_entry_deleted does remaining_entries = LogbookEntry.objects.filter(member=member).count() and only downgrades if remaining_entries == 0. The post_delete signal fires after the deletion, but two concurrent deletes of the last two entries can both see remaining_entries == 0 and both run the downgrade. More subtly, a new logbook entry being created concurrently may not yet be visible to the counting query, and the member will be downgraded despite having a fresh entry.
  • Recommendation: Lock the member row (select_for_update) inside a transaction, re-count inside the lock, only then demote. Again, use update_fields=['level'] to avoid full-row writes.

docs.title: F6 — verdict_date uses datetime.datetime.now() instead of timezone.now()
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other
  • File: api/models/models_upgraderequest.py:50
  • Evidence: self.verdict_date = datetime.datetime.now() in UpgradeRequest.save(). The import is from django.db.models.functions import datetime, which is not Python's datetime module — it is Django's database-function namespace. This is almost certainly broken at runtime and relies on accidentally working because django.db.models.functions.datetime re-exports Python's datetime. CLAUDE.md §15 explicitly calls out: "Never use datetime.datetime.now() — use django.utils.timezone.now()." The view at views_upgraderequest.py:115 correctly uses timezone.now(); the model then overwrites it with datetime.datetime.now() during save(). If the project ever enables USE_TZ=True, this becomes a naive/aware mismatch bug.
  • Recommendation: Import from django.utils import timezone and use timezone.now().

docs.title: F8 — N+1 on logbook skill requirements

docs.title: F12 — verdict_reason applied before permission check (rejected requests)
docs.text:
• Severity: medium

  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:154-162
  • Evidence: UpgradeRequestDeclineView.post sets upgrade_request.verdict_reason = request.data.get('verdict_reason') before handle_upgrade_request_verdict runs the permission check. If the permission check fails, the in-memory object has already been mutated; while .save() is only called inside the handler on the permitted path, returning a 403 here means the field was temporarily set on the instance, which is confusing and fragile. Additionally, the verdict_reason has no sanitisation — the field accepts raw text up to 500 chars (per model), but the serializer here accepts max_length=500 which matches — fine, but no escaping when rendered in emails. Check upgrade_request_voters.html for context injection.
  • Recommendation: Validate via the UpgradeRequestRejectSerializer (serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)) before touching the model. Treat verdict_reason as untrusted when rendering templates (Django templates auto-escape, but confirm no |safe filter is used).

docs.title: F13 — Duplicate-request check only covers applicant=request.user
docs.text:
• Severity: medium
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:73-76
  • Evidence: The "duplicate_request" guard filters applicant=request.user, but the create serializer accepts an arbitrary applicant (line 44: serializer.validated_data['applicant']). A user with CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_OTHERS could open a second upgrade request for another member (the duplicate check misses because request.user is not the applicant).
  • Recommendation: Filter on applicant=applicant_member (the validated applicant), not on request.user.

docs.title: F14 — ActionChoice.VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ / EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ /
docs.text: DELETE_UPGRADE_REQ / CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ not listed in CLAUDE.md §8 - Severity: low - Confidence: high - Category: perms - Evidence: CLAUDE.md §8 enumerates CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_SELF, CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_OTHERS, APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ, VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ only. The code references VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ, EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ, DELETE_UPGRADE_REQ, CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ, DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ in permissions.py. - Recommendation: Trigger the CLAUDE.md self-update protocol to document these actions (this is a documentation gap, not a bug).

docs.title: F15 — Status transition accepts NEW→APPROVED without intermediate votes
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: other
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:113
  • Evidence: handle_upgrade_request_verdict accepts any status in (APPROVED, DECLINED) regardless of the current status. An already APPROVED request can be re-approved (re-firing the notification, re-adding group, resetting verdict_date). A DECLINED request can be flipped to APPROVED without trace, and an APPROVED member's group membership won't be rolled back if it's changed to DECLINED.
  • Recommendation: Guard the transition: only allow status in (NEW, IN_PROGRESS) before applying a verdict. Record the transition in an audit table or log.

docs.title: F16 — .order_by('id') on UpgradeRequestApproveView queryset is misleading
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: style
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:131, 147, 225
  • Evidence: generics.CreateAPIView does not paginate, and get_object fetches by pk; .order_by('id') adds an unused ORDER BY to SELECT ... WHERE id=... queries.
  • Recommendation: Drop .order_by('id').

docs.title: F17 — UpgradeRequestCommentViewSet.get_queryset() uses unqualified select_related()
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: n+1
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:169
  • Evidence: .select_related() with no arguments follows all non-null FKs — future-proof, but opaque. It also does not include the upgrade_request.applicant chain used by get_queryset() filter at line 197 (that filter hits the DB anyway), nor does the list path annotate anything.
  • Recommendation: Make joins explicit: .select_related('author', 'upgrade_request__applicant').

docs.title: F18 — Empty-M2M semantics conflict: "no voters" unclear in verdict math
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: There is no quorum / threshold check anywhere. Approval and decline are pure admin actions; voter counts are displayed but not enforced. If product intent is "approver can verdict any time", this is fine — but worth calling out given the VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ ceremony and per-request voter counts.
  • Recommendation: Confirm with product: is voting advisory or mandatory? If mandatory, add a quorum guard in handle_upgrade_request_verdict.

docs.title: F19 — applicant_str is set in save() but not preserved if applicant is deleted then re-linked
docs.text:
• Severity: nit
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: other
  • File: api/models/models_upgraderequest.py:46-47
  • Evidence: The backup is populated correctly on every save, but applicant = models.ForeignKey(..., on_delete=models.SET_NULL) means that when the applicant is deleted, the FK becomes null and applicant_str retains the old username — good. However, the model never calls save() after the FK is SET_NULL'd by cascade, so applicant_str is in fact preserved by virtue of not being touched, not by defensive code. This is the correct outcome, but fragile: any future migration or data fix that calls .save() on applicant-less rows would need to guard if self.applicant: (which it already does). Confirmed correct.
  • Recommendation: None — noted for documentation.

docs.title: F20 — send_upgrade_request_handled_notification called outside transaction
docs.text:
• Severity: low
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: tx
  • File: api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:126
  • Evidence: Related to F1. Even if F1 is fixed with transaction.atomic, the Huey enqueue must use transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_upgrade_request_handled_notification(ur)) or the worker can pick up the task before the row is visible. Same applies to the post_save signal for upgrade_request_post_save in signals.py:63-66 which fires send_upgrade_request_created_notification.
  • Recommendation: Wrap Huey enqueues in transaction.on_commit.

docs.text: Severity Count critical 1 (F1) high 4 (F2, F3, F4, F5) medium 7 (F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, F11, F12, F13) low 4 (F14, F15, F18, F20) nit 3 (F16, F17, F19)

docs.title: Quick-win recommendations (do these first)
docs.text:
1. Replace datetime.datetime.now() with timezone.now() in models_upgraderequest.py:50 (F6). One-line fix, matches CLAUDE.md §15.
  2. Wrap handle_upgrade_request_verdict and AutoUpgradeService.* in transaction.atomic + select_for_update() on Member and UpgradeRequest (F1, F4, F5). This closes the worst races in one sweep.
  3. Use .save(update_fields=[...]) everywhere on Member and UpgradeRequest in these paths (F11).
  4. Add .select_related('lead', 'level') on the recent-trips queryset and prefetch skill entries (F7, F8).
  5. Guard status transitions: only NEW/IN_PROGRESS can be verdicted (F15).

docs.title: Caveat
docs.text:
mcp__django-ai-boost__query_model requires a DB connection; the dev DB dev doesn't exist in this environment, so no live aggregate probes were run. This step falls back to static analysis: pattern grep + cross-reference with Step 6 code-review findings.

Follow-up for the team: stand up a realistic dev DB or connect the MCP to staging to get actual row-count distributions and query plans. The findings below identify suspects; live probes would confirm hit rates.

docs.title: Static metrics
docs.text:
Metric Count Files in api/views/ 30 Total potentially-expensive query patterns (.all() / .filter().first() / for x in .objects. / related_set.all()) 62 occurrences across 16 files select_related/prefetch_related uses in api/ (views + services + migrations) 18 occurrences across 6 files Views with any query-optimization call 5 of 30 (views_member, views_trip, views_triprequest, views_tripreport, views_upgraderequest)

Interpretation: five views have thought about N+1; the other 25 haven't. Many of those 25 are small resource-level ViewSets where the default DRF generic behaviour is OK (single retrieve), but several — e.g. views_logbook.py, views_clubnews.py, views_upgraderequest.py listings, views_pushnotification.py — serialize FK-heavy data and almost certainly have N+1 on list endpoints.

docs.title: [high / confidence high] TripViewLogbookView — prefetch defeated by .filter(...).first() pattern
docs.text:

docs.title: [high / confidence high] MemberViewSet.list — no select_related('level') or prefetch_related('groups')
docs.text:
• File: api/views/views_member.py

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] Six copy-pasted Vehicle.objects.filter(member=..., id=...).first() calls in views_trip.py
docs.text:

docs.title: Probe plan (for later, once DB is available)
docs.text:
# Row counts per hot model
query_model Member    — total count, count(is_active=True), count(paid_member=True)
query_model Trip       — total, by approval_status, upcoming (start_time > now)

orphan LogbookEntry rows — same
Member rows with level=NULL — should be 0
