docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• No live profiling possible in this environment.
  • Static analysis confirms Step 6 agents' findings — several confirmed N+1s, one defeated prefetch, and widespread inconsistency in query optimization across views.
  • Roughly 5/30 views use query optimization. Remaining 25 are either simple enough not to need it or have latent N+1.
  • Recommend seeding dev DB from staging (anonymized) and re-running this step with live query_model probes.

docs.title: Async Task Audit
docs.text: Scope: api/background.py plus enqueue sites in api/signals.py, api/views/*.py, and api/services/trip_registration_service.py.

docs.title: Tasks reviewed
docs.text:
Task Type Retries Schedule / delay LOC send_trip_notification async 2 300s 17-19 send_trip_approval_notification async 2 300s 21-23 send_registration_from_waitlist_notification async 2 900s 26-28 send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification async 2 900s 31-33 send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification async 2 900s 36-38 send_upgrade_request_handled_notification async 2 300s 41-43 send_upgrade_request_created_notification async 2 300s 46-48 periodic_upgrade_request_reminder periodic – daily 20:00 Asia/Dubai 51-53 periodic_purge_old_notifications periodic – daily 04:00 55-64 periodic_purge_inactive_devices periodic – daily 02:00 66-70 periodic_delete_old_triprequests periodic – daily 03:00 73-77 send_club_news async 2 300s 80-82 send_feedback_notification async 2 300s 85-87 create_gallery_for_trip_task async 6 3600s 90-110 update_gallery_for_trip_task async 6 3600s 113-126 delete_gallery_for_trip_task async 3 3600s 129-142 restore_gallery_for_trip_task async 3 3600s 145-158 send_new_trip_comment_notification_task async 2 300s 162-164 process_account_deletion_requests periodic – daily 00:00 167-174 cleanup_expired_geocoding_cache periodic – daily 01:00 176-180 cleanup_blacklisted_tokens periodic – daily 04:30 183-191 cleanup_expired_outstanding_tokens periodic – daily 04:45 194-203

Huey config (settings.py:119-143): RedisHuey, results=True, immediate=DEV, utc=False. With USE_TZ=False and TIME_ZONE='Asia/Dubai', all crontabs correctly fire at local Dubai time.

docs.title: [CRITICAL] TypeError at runtime — remove_from_registered / remove_from_waitlist pass the wrong arguments
docs.text:
• File: api/services/trip_registration_service.py:49, 58
  • Task: send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification, send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: args
  • Evidence: python # trip_registration_service.py send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification(user, trip) # 2 positional args send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification(user, trip) # 2 positional args But the task signatures in api/background.py:32, 37 declare a single cancellation: TripRegistrationCancellationReason argument, and the downstream NotificationManager.send_removed_from_trip_registered(cancellation) (notification_service.py:136) reads cancellation.member, cancellation.trip, cancellation.id. An identical 2-arg call also exists in api/views/views_trip.py:436, 439 (CancelTripRegistration).
  • Recommendation: Either (a) update callers to build a TripRegistrationCancellationReason and pass it (views/views_trip.py:399-414 already demonstrates the correct pattern), or (b) refactor the task to accept (member_id, trip_id, reason_id_or_none) and resolve DB-side. Option (a) is least invasive; option (b) is more correct for Celery/Huey best practice. In either case, add a test that actually executes the task — it will fail fast.

docs.title: [HIGH] Model instances passed to every task instead of IDs
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:18, 22, 27, 32, 37, 42, 47, 81, 86, 163
  • Task: all notification tasks except the four *_gallery_for_trip_task tasks
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: args
  • Evidence: Signatures like def send_trip_notification(trip: Trip), def send_club_news(data: ClubNews), def send_feedback_notification(data: Feedback) receive Django model instances, which Huey pickles into Redis. Pickled instances are (1) fragile across schema changes, (2) can reference stale data by the time the worker runs, and (3) break send_club_news when the view at views_pushnotification.py:29 calls send_club_news(serializer.validated_data) — that passes a dict, not a ClubNews, yet the task ultimately calls data.status = ClubNewsStatus.SENT; data.save() (notification_service.py:133-134). Second runtime bug.
  • Recommendation: Switch every notification task to accept a primary key (e.g. send_trip_notification(trip_id: int)) and do Trip.objects.get(pk=trip_id) at the top. Apply the gallery-task pattern uniformly. Fix ClubNewsNotificationAPIView to create/save the ClubNews row first, then enqueue send_club_news(news.id).

docs.title: [HIGH] No transaction.on_commit wrapper at any enqueue site
docs.text:
• File: api/signals.py (post_save receivers), api/views/views_trip.py, api/views/views_upgraderequest.py:126, api/views/views_feedback.py:34, api/services/trip_registration_service.py
  • Task: every async task
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: on-commit
  • Evidence: Grepping the whole worktree for on_commit returns zero matches. Yet tasks are enqueued from inside post_save signals (signals.py:66, 92, 161, 178, 184, 189, 195) and from DRF views wrapped by ATOMIC_REQUESTS/serializer saves. If the surrounding transaction rolls back (e.g. an error after perform_create but before response), the worker still picks up the job and either (a) .get() raises DoesNotExist because the row was never committed, or (b) reads partially-committed state. create_gallery_for_trip_task is especially exposed — it calls GalleryWebhookService which hits an external API, so a rollback means the remote gallery still gets created.
  • Recommendation: Wrap every enqueue that depends on committed DB state: python from django.db import transaction transaction.on_commit(lambda: create_gallery_for_trip_task(trip.id)) Highest priority: the signal handlers in signals.py and views_feedback.py:34 (serializer.save() returns before commit finishes when inside ATOMIC_REQUESTS). The NotificationLog.objects.bulk_create side of things is fine because it runs inside the worker, but any fresh read of Trip/UpgradeRequest/ClubNews must be on-commit.

docs.title: [HIGH] Gallery tasks swallow Trip.DoesNotExist — no retry on genuine race
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:107-110, 122-126, 138-142, 154-158
  • Task: create_gallery_for_trip_task, update_gallery_for_trip_task, delete_gallery_for_trip_task, restore_gallery_for_trip_task
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: error-path
  • Evidence: python except Trip.DoesNotExist: logger.error(f"Trip {trip_id} not found when creating gallery") except Exception as e: logger.error(...) # no re-raise in create_gallery_for_trip_task create_gallery_for_trip_task logs-and-returns for both error paths, so Huey never retries even when the write hasn't committed yet (Trip.DoesNotExist is exactly the symptom of missing on_commit). The three other gallery tasks do raise Exception(...) but that wraps and loses the original traceback, and still log-only on DoesNotExist. A "trip not yet committed" race therefore never recovers — you get a permanent log entry, no gallery.
  • Recommendation: Re-raise in create_gallery_for_trip_task so retries kick in. For DoesNotExist, raise a RetryException on the first few attempts and only swallow after a retry budget. Stop wrapping exceptions in raise Exception(str(e)) — that strips the traceback; just raise bare to propagate.

docs.title: [MEDIUM] Idempotency gap — gallery creation can double up
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:96-103
  • Task: create_gallery_for_trip_task
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: idempotency
  • Evidence: The task always calls GalleryWebhookService.create_gallery_for_trip(trip). There is no guard such as if trip.gallery_id: return at the top. If the remote call succeeds but the local trip.save(update_fields=['gallery_id']) fails (e.g. DB hiccup), the next retry creates a second gallery on the remote side.
  • Recommendation: python trip = Trip.objects.get(id=trip_id) if trip.gallery_id: logger.info(f"Trip {trip_id} already has gallery_id={trip.gallery_id}, skipping") return Apply the mirror guard in delete_gallery_for_trip_task (skip if gallery_id is already None) and in restore_gallery_for_trip_task.

docs.title: [MEDIUM] Idempotency gap — club_news marked SENT by side-effect inside a retryable task
docs.text:
• File: api/services/notification_service.py:133-134, called from api/background.py:81 via send_club_wide_news
  • Task: send_club_news
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: idempotency
  • Evidence: send_club_wide_news iterates channels (email + FCM + Telegram), then unconditionally does data.status = ClubNewsStatus.SENT; data.save(). If any channel raises after a partial fan-out (say, 500 of 1000 members got the email and then FCM 5xx'd), Huey retries — but on the next run every channel re-sends to everyone. Combined with ClubNews.save() being immutable once SENT (CLAUDE.md §15), a retry after the status flipped will actually raise a ValidationError from the save side, permanently blocking the retry.
  • Recommendation: Record per-channel success in a set (e.g. on a ClubNewsDelivery row or on NotificationLog) and skip already-delivered channels on retry. Flip the status to SENT only after all channels report success.

docs.title: [MEDIUM] process_account_deletion_requests is not idempotent and not transactional
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:167-174
  • Task: process_account_deletion_requests
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: idempotency + error-path
  • Evidence: python for request in requests: request.member.anonymize_data() request.delete() If anonymize_data() raises mid-loop (one member out of many), the loop aborts, the request row is not deleted, and the next-day run re-anonymizes everyone already processed. anonymize_data() deactivates + wipes PII, which on a re-run is a no-op-ish, but Vehicle deletions would already be gone and the loop will still blow up on the same failing member forever.
  • Recommendation: Per-request try/except with logger.exception, so one bad row doesn't block the rest. Wrap anonymize_data() + request.delete() in an atomic() block so partial anonymization doesn't leave a half-deleted member.

docs.title: [MEDIUM] periodic_purge_old_notifications uses .count() then .delete() — two roundtrips, races
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:59-64
  • Task: periodic_purge_old_notifications
  • Confidence: low
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: The .count() log line runs a separate query from .delete(), and at 04:00 the window is wide enough that a new row can slip in between them. Not a correctness bug (the .delete() re-evaluates the filter) but the logged count is misleading.
  • Recommendation: Use the tuple returned by .delete(): deleted, _ = qs.delete(); logger.info(f'Deleted {deleted} ...'). The cleanup-token tasks at 184-190 and 194-202 already do this correctly — apply the same pattern.

docs.title: [LOW] Two token-cleanup tasks scheduled 15 min apart — race with long tx
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:183-203
  • Task: cleanup_blacklisted_tokens, cleanup_expired_outstanding_tokens
  • Confidence: low
  • Category: tz
  • Evidence: Blacklist (04:30) must complete before outstanding (04:45), otherwise the FK cascade from OutstandingToken.delete() will wipe blacklist rows the first task hadn't touched yet. In practice 15 minutes is generous, but there's no ordering guarantee encoded in code — it's crontab-order only.
  • Recommendation: Make cleanup_expired_outstanding_tokens chain off the end of cleanup_blacklisted_tokens instead of relying on crontab timing. Or merge them into one task since the second subsumes the first (cascade removes blacklist rows anyway).

docs.title: [LOW] create_gallery_for_trip_task calls trip.save(), re-triggering trip_post_save signal
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:101-103
  • Task: create_gallery_for_trip_task
  • Confidence: medium
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: trip.save(update_fields=['gallery_id']) fires pre_save / post_save signals. trip_post_save in signals.py checks _original_approval_status and may re-enqueue update_gallery_for_trip_task(instance.id) at line 189 because the trip is APPROVED and now has a gallery_id. That probably doesn't loop because update_gallery_for_trip_task just PATCHes remote state, but it is an unintended second API call on every fresh gallery create.
  • Recommendation: Use Trip.objects.filter(pk=trip.id).update(gallery_id=gallery_id) to bypass signals, matching the pattern already used in signals.py:158 and 170.

docs.title: [LOW] Huey logger name is ad4x4-worker but some tasks import from code that logs to ad4x4-web
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:14, cross-reference api/signals.py:17, api/services/trip_registration_service.py:9
  • Task: n/a (observability)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: obs
  • Evidence: Tasks log to ad4x4-worker, but they call service functions that log to ad4x4-web (signals) or other contexts. Correlating a task's full log trail requires joining on the task ID, which is never logged.
  • Recommendation: Log task start/end in each task body: logger.info(f'send_trip_notification start trip={trip_id}') + logger.info('...end'). Add the Huey task ID (huey.api.Task.id is available on the task object via execute_ignore_result=False context or a decorator wrapper).

docs.title: [LOW] from ... import AccountDeletionRequest mid-file at line 161
docs.text:
• File: api/background.py:161
  • Task: n/a (code hygiene)
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: other
  • Evidence: The import is wedged between restore_gallery_for_trip_task and send_new_trip_comment_notification_task, suggesting it was added to avoid a top-of-file circular import. No actual circular exists today — AccountDeletionRequest can safely be imported from api.models.models_member at the top.
  • Recommendation: Move to the header. Same for the late from api.models.models_geocoding_cache import GeocodingCache at line 178 — both should sit at the top.

docs.title: CLAUDE.md §10 drift
docs.text:
Tasks in code not in docs: - cleanup_blacklisted_tokens — documented correctly (daily 04:30). OK. - cleanup_expired_outstanding_tokens — documented correctly (daily 04:45). OK. - cleanup_expired_geocoding_cache — documented correctly (daily 01:00). OK.

After cross-reference, every code-side task appears in CLAUDE.md §10 tables.

Tasks in docs not in code: none. All 14 async and 8 periodic tasks listed in §10 match the decorated functions in api/background.py.

Minor drift worth noting: - CLAUDE.md §10 lists send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification and send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification with retry_delay 15 min (= 900s) — matches code. - CLAUDE.md §10 Gallery tasks: create/update 6 retries / 1 hr, delete/restore 3 retries / 1 hr — matches code. - The task-count discrepancy in CLAUDE.md §3 ("14 async tasks") is consistent with the code count (14 @task-decorated functions).

No doc-drift corrections needed in CLAUDE.md §10. Main documentation gap is §15 — the transaction.on_commit gotcha is mentioned in the audit framing but not currently called out as a repo-wide gotcha. If the fixes in this audit are applied, §15 should gain an entry:

Always enqueue Huey tasks from transaction.on_commit. Every enqueue site in views, serializers, and signals that runs inside a DB transaction must wrap the call in transaction.on_commit(lambda: my_task(pk)), otherwise the worker races the writer and reads rolled-back state.

docs.title: Summary of severity
docs.text:
• CRITICAL (1): 2-arg vs 1-arg mismatch in trip_registration_service and views_trip.CancelTripRegistration — runtime TypeError on every real cancel flow that goes through these paths.
  • HIGH (3): Instances instead of IDs, no on_commit anywhere, gallery tasks swallow errors.
  • MEDIUM (3): Gallery double-create, club_news partial retry, account-deletion non-idempotency.
  • LOW (4): Two-query purge, token cleanup ordering, signal re-fire, logger naming / late imports.

No task-scheduling timezone issue — HUEY['utc']=False + TIME_ZONE='Asia/Dubai' is correct and CLAUDE.md §15's USE_TZ gotcha is respected throughout (all periodic tasks use timezone.now()).

docs.title: Architecture Sweep
docs.text: Audit of AD4x4 Django backend based on graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md and source verification. Read-only — no source file modified.

docs.title: Graph at a glance
docs.text:
• Nodes: 2,397 (CLAUDE.md §19 says 2,376 — drift, minor)
  • Edges: 7,596 (CLAUDE.md §19 says 7,488 — drift, minor)
  • Extraction: 33% EXTRACTED / 67% INFERRED (avg confidence 0.5) — per Graphify's own header. Inferred edges must be treated as hypotheses.
  • Communities: 115 (CLAUDE.md §19 says 100 — drift); 26 of them are empty/single-node noise.

docs.title: Top fan-in (god nodes) — verified
docs.text:
Graphify "edges" counts conflate every occurrence (filter class, permission class, serializer, test, admin, migration). Real model-level fan-in is an order of magnitude lower. Verified by grep.

Rank Node Graphify fan-in Source reality Verdict 1 Level 566 9 ForeignKey(Level) + 3 M2M(Level) across 5 model files; 46 files touch the name Real load-bearing node. Used as FK from Member, Trip, LogbookSkill, LogbookMigrationRequest, UpgradeRequest, ConfigurableSettings (3 FKs). M2M from PermissionMatrix, ClubNews, NotificationSettings. 566 is heavily inflated but the "god node" label is correct. 2 ActionChoice 388 TextChoices enum in api/choices.py; 182 occurrences across 21 files, mostly in permissions.py (30) and views Real. Used by every PermissionMatrix check. Anchors the whole authorisation system. 3 PermissionMatrix 364 Model in api/models/models.py:35; 96 occurrences across 19 files Real. PermissionMatrix.has_permission() is the authoritative perm check, called from 30+ permissions.py classes. Actual call sites: 4 direct invocations (confirmed via grep), but the class is referenced in every permissions.py class body via helpers in permission_service.py. 4 ApprovalStatus 357 TextChoices enum in api/choices.py:80; 39 occurrences across 8 files Over-inflated. Only views_trip.py (15), signals.py (11), permissions.py (3), views_member.py (3) materially use it. 357 is >10x reality. Still legitimately central to trip lifecycle. 5 CarBrand 217 TextChoices in api/choices.py:4; narrowly used by Vehicle + Member Over-inflated. Real impact is small — one serializer + one choice endpoint. Appears in the top 10 only because it's a 74-member enum (each member counts). 6 CountryChoice 197 TextChoices (ISO 3166) in api/choices.py:145 Same pattern as CarBrand. Many enum members, very narrow real usage. 7 URL configuration for ad4x4 project… 90 = ad4x4/urls.py docstring node — treated as a node with every registered URL as an edge Artifact of Graphify's node model, not a god node. 8 StandardResultsSetPagination 89 Defined in api/util.py; applied as DRF default pagination Real but shallow. Referenced as a pagination class in almost every ViewSet. Not a "change-at-your-peril" node. 9 UnifiedResponseSerializer 89 Response envelope {success, message} — used by every view returning non-default shape Real. Changing its shape breaks every client. 10 Gender 84 3-member enum, narrow use on Member Inflated. Same "big enum → big fan-in" artefact.

True blast radius of the real god nodes: - Level: changing Level.numeric_level or auto_group affects upgrade, trip-level filtering, permission-matrix scoping, notification targeting. Must-test: member login (defaultuserlevel), trip create (views_trip.py), upgrade voting, auto-upgrade service, permission-matrix filtering. - PermissionMatrix: the has_permission classmethod signature is frozen — it's called from permissions.py and the helpers in api/services/permission_service.py (check_trip_permission_against_perm_matrix_or_trip_lead, etc. — community 14). Changing its kwargs breaks 30+ permission classes. - ActionChoice: adding a value is safe; renaming is not — existing PermissionMatrix rows in the DB reference the old string. - ApprovalStatus: the P/A/R/C state machine is encoded in views_trip.py (1113 LOC) + signals.py trip_post_save / trip_pre_save. Changing a value re-breaks trip count signals.

docs.title: Top fan-out (integrators)
docs.text:
Graphify does not publish a fan-out list, but source grep identifies the integrators:

File Evidence Role api/views/views_trip.py (1,113 LOC) Imports 12 api.* modules; 23 top-level classes; imports from background, 3 services, permissions, serializers, models, choices, filters, util The integrator. Trip CRUD, register/unregister, waitlist, approve/decline, check-in/out, search, history, export, view-logbook — all live here. api/views/views_member.py (787 LOC) 12 api.* imports Member CRUD + logbook/upgrade/trip-history side endpoints. api/services/notification_service.py + friends 5 channel implementations + manager Fans out to email / push / Telegram / store / noop. api/background.py Imports init_notifications + gallery_webhook + models Huey task entrypoints — every background action is dispatched through here. api/admin.py (281 LOC, 29 ModelAdmin classes) Imports 15+ model names Single flat admin file — reasonable for project size. api/permissions.py (525 LOC, 35+ permission classes) Imports ActionChoice, PermissionMatrix, ApprovalStatus, Level Central authorisation surface. api/signals.py Imports from background, services.global_settings, services.auto_upgrade_service, 5+ models Glue between ORM events and async tasks. ad4x4/urls.py Imports from 27 view modules URL integrator.

docs.title: The 5 most tightly-coupled clusters
docs.text:
Graphify's communities are unnamed. Inferred from member nodes:

  • Community 0 (393 nodes, cohesion 0.02) — "Admin & everything-that-references-Level." Hosts every *Admin class plus many models. Low cohesion = Graphify's dumping ground; the Level god node drags half the codebase into this cluster.
  • Community 1 (172 nodes, cohesion 0.05) — "Trip lifecycle." TripsFilter, GalleryWebhookService, CanCreateTripPermission, HasDeleteTripPermission, HasEditTripMediaPermission, HasEditTripPermission, PageNumberPagination. Maps to trip views + permissions + gallery integration.
  • Community 2 (105 nodes, cohesion 0.04) — "Upgrade request + trip request + filters." AreaChoice, TimeOfDayChoice, UpgradeRequestStatus, VoteChoice, LevelsFilter, MeetingPointsFilter, upgrade-request comment filter. Corresponds to member-wish / upgrade-voting domain.
  • Community 3 (81 nodes, cohesion 0.04) — "Payments + profile settings." PayPalConfigurationAdmin, WebsitePaymentAdmin, Emirates, Gender, NotificationSettings, PaymentMethod, PaymentStatus, PayPalConfiguration. Combines website-app payments with member profile side-data.
  • Community 4 (46 nodes, cohesion 0.02) — "Notifications." LoggingContexts, NotificationType, EmailNotificationChannel, every send_*() function (acceptedfromwaitlist, accountdeletioncancelled, accountdeletionrequest, clubwidenews). Corresponds exactly to api/services/notification_service.py + email_notifications.py + friends.
  • Community 5 (67 nodes, cohesion 0.11) — "Member-centric endpoints." ContactInfoMemberSerializer, MembersFilter, AccountDeletionRequest, HasEditMembershipPaymentsPermission, HasSearchMembersPermission, HasViewUpgradeRequestPermissionOrIsForSelf, ListLogbookEntrySerializer. Hosts the member CRUD + personal-logbook seam.

All five have cohesion under 0.12 — these are not tight clusters, they're loose affinity groups.

docs.title: [medium] Services layer imports from the Huey task module
docs.text:
• Node / area: api/services/trip_registration_service.py → api/background.py
  • Confidence: high (source-verified)
  • Category: layering
  • Evidence: trip_registration_service.py lines 3–7 import send_registration_from_waitlist_notification, send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification, send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification from api.background. api.background in turn imports from api.services.init_notifications and api.services.gallery_webhook. No actual import-time cycle (services/init.py does not re-export tripregistrationservice), but this is an upward dependency: services should dispatch via an abstraction, not import task entrypoints directly.
  • Recommendation: Move waitlist-related notification dispatch into notification_service.py (consistent with how notification_manager.send_* is the dispatch seam) and have background.py remain the only file that knows about Huey + service glue. Removes the risk of reintroducing a real cycle.

docs.title: [medium] Graphify's fan-in counts over-inflate by ~10x
docs.text:
• Node / area: all top-10 god nodes
  • Confidence: high (source-verified)
  • Category: drift — CLAUDE.md §19 reports these numbers as-is
  • Evidence: Level 566 vs 12 real model-level references; ApprovalStatus 357 vs 39 real occurrences.
  • Recommendation: Treat Graphify's edge counts as relative-ranking only, not absolute blast-radius. The ranking is directionally right; the magnitude is not. Consider adding a one-line caveat to CLAUDE.md §19's "Key structural facts" subsection so future agents don't quote the raw number.

docs.title: [medium] views_trip.py is a 1,113-line god file
docs.text:
• Node / area: api/views/views_trip.py
  • Confidence: high (source-verified — 23 top-level classes, 12 service imports)
  • Category: god-file
  • Evidence: Hosts TripCreateView, TripEditView, TripViewSet, RegisterForTrip, ForceRegisterForTrip, RegisterForTripWaitlist, RemoveMemberFromTripRegistration, CancelTripRegistration, AcceptMemberFromWaitlist, TripApproveView, TripDeclineView, TripCheckinView, TripCheckoutView, DetailedMemberTripCountView, TripExportRegistrantsView, TripViewLogbookView, TripSearch, LeadTripHistorySearch — plus two inline serializers.
  • Recommendation: Split into views_trip_core.py (CRUD/Viewset), views_trip_registration.py (register / waitlist / force-register), views_trip_lifecycle.py (approve / decline / checkin / checkout), views_trip_reports.py (export, logbook view, search/history). Matches CLAUDE.md §14 "one file per resource" convention.

docs.title: [low] Test directory drift vs CLAUDE.md
docs.text:
• Node / area: tests/ vs api/tests/
  • Confidence: high (source-verified)
  • Category: drift
  • Evidence: CLAUDE.md §3 says api/tests/ contains "~59 test files." Reality: api/tests/ has 3 test files; tests/ at the repo root has 63. Both are discovered by pytest.ini files.
  • Recommendation: Either consolidate into one location or update CLAUDE.md §3 + §13 to describe the split (root tests/ = feature tests, api/tests/ = legacy remnants).

docs.title: [low] Graphify count / community drift vs CLAUDE.md §19
docs.text:
• Node / area: CLAUDE.md §19 "Key structural facts"
  • Confidence: high
  • Category: drift
  • Evidence: CLAUDE.md §19 quotes "2,376 nodes, 7,488 edges, 100 communities." Actual graph: 2,397 / 7,596 / 115. God-node edge counts also drift slightly (Level 564 → 566, ActionChoice 389 → 388, PermissionMatrix 364 (matches), ApprovalStatus 357 (matches)).
  • Recommendation: Per §19's own rebuild note, these numbers go stale on every rebuild — consider rephrasing to "approximate" or dropping exact numbers.

docs.title: [low] 72 isolated nodes flagged as knowledge gaps
docs.text:
• Node / area: Graphify "Knowledge Gaps" section
  • Confidence: medium (Graphify-only)
  • Category: graph-quality
  • Evidence: 72 nodes with ≤1 connection; views_media.py/serve_media(), upgrade_eligibility.py/get_upgrade_eligibility_data() called out. Both are legitimate, production-used code.
  • Recommendation: No source-side action needed. This is a signal that Graphify's extractor missed imports for some utility files, not a codebase defect.

docs.title: [info] No structural cycles, no services→views, no models→services
docs.text:
• Confidence: high (source-verified)
  • Evidence: grep for from api.views in api/services/ and api/models/ returns zero matches; grep for from api.services in api/models/ returns zero matches. Layering invariants hold: models ← services ← views, and services import background for task dispatch (one-way).

docs.title: Graphify false positives
docs.text:
All top-10 god-node edge counts are inflated — these are the worst offenders when interpreted as "change blast radius":

  1. Level claimed 566 edges. True model-level fan-in is 12 (9 FK + 3 M2M). Every file that mentions the word "Level" is scored as an edge.
  2. ApprovalStatus claimed 357 edges. Real usage is concentrated in 8 files, 39 occurrences. Most "edges" are to test functions, serializer fields, and admin displays that merely reference the enum class.
  3. CarBrand claimed 217 edges. Real structural usage is one CharField(choices=CarBrand.choices) on Vehicle + a choices endpoint. The 217 comes from the 74 enum members each generating "edges."
  4. Gender claimed 84 edges — same pattern. 3-member enum, narrow use, artificially boosted by Graphify treating enum members as nodes.
  5. "URL configuration for ad4x4 project…" (the urls.py docstring) claimed 90 edges. This is a node type (docstring-as-node), not a real god class.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Three true god nodes (Level, PermissionMatrix, ActionChoice) and one god file (views_trip.py, 1,113 LOC) are the real blast-radius concerns. The other top-10 entries are Graphify artefacts.
  • Layering is clean: no models→services, no services→views, no import cycles at load time. One soft upward dependency: services/trip_registration_service.py → background.py — worth refactoring but not urgent.
  • CLAUDE.md §3, §13, §19 have drifted from reality (test-dir split and graph counts). Quick doc fix; no code change needed.

docs.title: Step 11 — Dependency Audit (pip-audit)
docs.text: Ran pip-audit against both requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt in the project venv.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• requirements.txt: 104 packages scanned, 24 known vulnerabilities in 9 packages
  • requirements-dev.txt: No known vulnerabilities

docs.title: Critical block — Django 13 CVEs
docs.text:
Current version: django==6.0.1 · Recommended: upgrade to 6.0.4 minimum (drop-in patch release)

The 13 CVEs in Django ordered by exploit potential against AD4x4:

CVE Severity Fix Relevance to AD4x4 CVE-2026-1312 — SQL injection in QuerySet.order_by() via column aliases with periods Critical 6.0.2 Very likely exploitable. AD4x4 has several endpoints that accept an order_by query param (trip search, member search, upgrade request listings). If any reach user-controlled alias values, this is an SQL injection vector. CVE-2026-1287 — SQL injection in FilteredRelation column aliases via control characters Critical 6.0.2 Possibly exploitable if FilteredRelation is used; grep to confirm. CVE-2026-1207 — SQL injection in RasterField (PostGIS only) High 6.0.2 Not applicable — no PostGIS usage. CVE-2026-4292 — Admin list_editable forgery allows instance creation via forged POST High 6.0.4 Admin-only but significant. Staff with admin access can be tricked via CSRF? Needs review of admin pages that use list_editable. CVE-2026-4277 — Add-permission bypass on GenericInlineModelAdmin via forged POST High 6.0.4 Same as above — admin panel risk. CVE-2026-3902 — ASGIRequest header spoofing via ambiguous header mapping High 6.0.4 The AD4x4 backend is WSGI via Gunicorn (per CLAUDE.md §11), so ASGI is not active. Low practical risk; still worth the upgrade. CVE-2026-33034 — ASGI Content-Length bypass of DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE High 6.0.4 Same — WSGI not affected. CVE-2026-33033 — MultiPartParser perf degradation via Content-Transfer-Encoding Medium 6.0.4 Applies to multipart upload paths (avatar, trip image, logbook migration PDF, feedback image). CVE-2026-25674 — Race in file-system storage / file-based cache Medium 6.0.3 AD4x4 uses filesystem MEDIA_ROOT = /app/uploads (prod) and LocMem cache (dev) — low risk for cache side; some risk for uploads if concurrent writes hit identical filenames. Django's default FileSystemStorage.get_available_name handles this but the CVE implies edge cases. CVE-2026-25673 — URLField.to_python() NFKC normalization on Windows Medium 6.0.3 Production runs Linux (Docker) — not affected. Dev on Windows technically affected but dev-only. CVE-2025-14550 — ASGIRequest DoS via multiple headers Medium 6.0.2 WSGI — not affected. CVE-2026-1285 — Truncator.chars/.words XSS via crafted HTML with html=True Low 6.0.2 Grep Truncator and truncatechars_html in codebase; likely unused. CVE-2025-13473 — mod_wsgi check_password() auth via untrusted input Low 6.0.2 Not applicable — AD4x4 uses Gunicorn, not mod_wsgi.

docs.title: cryptography==46.0.4 → 46.0.7 (3 CVEs)
docs.text: CVE Fix Relevance CVE-2026-39892 46.0.7 Buffer overflow in Hash.update() with non-contiguous Python buffers. Relevant to any code that hashes user-supplied bytes (file upload hashing, JWT signing internals via pyjwt). High severity — upgrade. CVE-2026-34073 46.0.6 DNS name constraints only validated against SANs, not peer name. Relevant for any cert-validated outbound TLS: HERE Maps, Gallery API, FCM. Upgrade. CVE-2026-26007 46.0.5 load_der_public_key/load_pem_public_key issue. Not invoked by AD4x4 code directly (JWT uses HS256 = symmetric, not asymmetric key loading). Low practical risk, but free with the upgrade.

docs.title: pyjwt==2.11.0 → 2.12.0 (1 CVE) — JWT-relevant
docs.text: • CVE-2026-32597 — PyJWT does not validate the crit (Critical) Header Parameter (RFC 7515 §4.1.11). A JWS with an unknown crit claim is accepted instead of rejected as required. Directly relevant to AD4x4 auth (SIMPLE_JWT.ALGORITHM=HS256). A crafted token with a crit header listing a spec extension the token fails to satisfy would be wrongly accepted. Exploitability depends on whether any attacker-controlled path produces such tokens — not trivially exploitable since AD4x4 signs with a server-only secret, but the defense-in-depth upgrade is cheap.

docs.title: pillow==12.1.0 → 12.2.0 (2 CVEs) — image upload paths affected
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-25990 (fix 12.1.1) — out-of-bounds write on crafted PSD image. AD4x4 accepts avatar, trip image, logbook migration PDF (PDF not PIL), feedback image, trip report images, sponsor images. If any of these reach Pillow and a user uploads a .psd, the worker process could crash or worse.
  • CVE-2026-40192 (fix 12.2.0) — FITS decompression bomb (scientific image format, extremely unlikely in this codebase).
  • Recommendation: Upgrade to 12.2.0 and add an explicit content-type allow-list in image-upload validators (JPEG/PNG/WebP only — no PSD/FITS/TIFF unless specifically needed).

docs.title: requests==2.32.5 → 2.33.0 (1 CVE)
docs.text: • CVE-2026-25645 — predictable filename in extract_zipped_paths(). AD4x4 does not use that function (grep confirms). Still, upgrade for hygiene.

docs.title: pyasn1==0.6.2 → 0.6.3 (1 CVE, DoS via deep recursion)
docs.text: • CVE-2026-30922. pyasn1 is a transitive dep (likely via cryptography/OIDC). DoS only. DOS is excluded from this audit's severity reporting per policy; upgrade with the batch anyway.

docs.title: pygments==2.19.2 → 2.20.0 (1 CVE)
docs.text: • CVE-2026-4539 — ReDoS in AdlLexer. Transitive (likely via docs or drf-spectacular). DOS-class, low real impact.

docs.title: pytest==9.0.2 → 9.0.3 (1 CVE, dev-only)
docs.text: • CVE-2025-71176 — /tmp/pytest-of-{user} naming allows local user to cause DoS/priv-esc. Dev-only (pytest is in requirements-dev.txt, not requirements.txt). But pip-audit found it in requirements.txt too — verify where pytest is declared. Upgrade.

docs.title: python-dotenv==1.2.1 → 1.2.2 (1 CVE)
docs.text: • CVE-2026-28684 — set_key()/unset_key() follow symlinks. Only relevant if AD4x4 or its tooling calls those write functions on an attacker-writable path. Production doesn't rewrite .env, so this is effectively dev-only. Upgrade with the batch.

docs.title: [critical / confidence high] Django 6.0.1 exposes the backend to multiple SQL-injection CVEs
docs.text:
• Category: cve-dep
  • Evidence: pip-audit output above; CVE-2026-1312 in particular allows SQL injection via QuerySet.order_by() — a query param commonly passed from the mobile app and web portal (trip/member search endpoints).
  • Exploit scenario: Attacker sends GET /api/trips/search/?order_by=<crafted_sql> (or similar). If the view passes that param directly into .order_by(), database contents are exposed or modified.
  • Recommendation: Upgrade Django==6.0.4 in requirements.txt today. Regression-test with pytest. No API breakage expected (patch-level release).

docs.title: [high / confidence high] PyJWT 2.11.0 accepts tokens with unknown crit headers
docs.text:
• Category: auth-lib-cve
  • Evidence: CVE-2026-32597. AD4x4 uses simplejwt which uses PyJWT internally.
  • Recommendation: Upgrade PyJWT>=2.12.0. Low risk of breakage (defensive fix; tokens signed by the server's own secret won't contain hostile crit headers unless the attacker can forge signatures — which they can't).

docs.title: [high / confidence high] Cryptography 46.0.4 has a buffer-overflow in Hash.update()
docs.text:
• Category: mem-cve
  • Evidence: CVE-2026-39892. Buffer overflow on non-contiguous buffers passed to hash functions.
  • Exploit scenario: Any code path hashing user-supplied bytes. Limited surface in AD4x4 but cryptography is a transitive dep of everything TLS.
  • Recommendation: Upgrade cryptography>=46.0.7.

docs.title: [high / confidence high] Pillow 12.1.0 out-of-bounds write on crafted PSD image
docs.text:
• Category: img-cve
  • Evidence: CVE-2026-25990.
  • Exploit scenario: Attacker uploads a .psd as avatar/feedback image/trip image. Worker process memory corruption.
  • Recommendation: Upgrade Pillow>=12.2.0 AND add an image-format allow-list in every file-upload serializer (MemberSerializer.validate_avatar, TripSerializer.validate_image, feedback/trip-report serializers).

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] 5 more Django CVEs fixed in 6.0.4 relevant to admin + multipart
docs.text:
• Category: cve-dep
  • Evidence: CVE-2026-4292, CVE-2026-4277, CVE-2026-33033, CVE-2026-33034, CVE-2026-3902, CVE-2026-25674, CVE-2026-25673, CVE-2026-1285, CVE-2025-14550, CVE-2025-13473.
  • Recommendation: Single upgrade Django==6.0.4 closes all 13 Django CVEs at once.

docs.title: [medium / confidence medium] Minor dep upgrades bundled
docs.text:
• Category: cve-dep
  • Recommendation: Batch upgrade: text Django==6.0.4 cryptography==46.0.7 pyjwt==2.12.0 pillow==12.2.0 requests==2.33.0 pyasn1==0.6.3 pygments==2.20.0 pytest==9.0.3 python-dotenv==1.2.2 Test the full suite before shipping. python manage.py check --deploy should be clean.

docs.title: Positives
docs.text:
• requirements-dev.txt: no vulnerabilities.
  • No end-of-life dependencies.
  • django-oidc-provider 0.9.0 — no known CVEs, but per CLAUDE.md §2/§15, its Django 6 compatibility is worth re-testing after any Django upgrade.

docs.title: Follow-ups
docs.text:
1. Create a single PR that bumps all 9 packages to their fix versions.
  2. Run full test suite and manage.py check --deploy.
  3. Regenerate schema.yml and compare — Django patch releases shouldn't change schema, but verify.
  4. Grep for order_by( call sites that read from request.query_params/request.GET and add an allow-list of column names.
  5. Add explicit image-format validators to every ImageField serializer.
  6. After upgrade, add pip-audit to the CI pipeline (fails the build on new CVEs).

docs.title: Step 12 — Documentation Drift
docs.text: Aggregation of doc-vs-reality drift from Steps 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9. Each finding cites the CLAUDE.md section and the source-of-truth file:line.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] §5 missing 11+ models
docs.text:
• Source of truth: api/models/*.py
  • Drift: NotificationSettings, TripRegistrationCancellationReason, TripComment, UpgradeRequestComment, LogbookMigrationSkillEntry, Feedback, TripReport, TripReportImage, MeetingPoint, UIString, FaqEntry, Sponsorship — all exist and are referenced via endpoints in §6, but none have a §5 stanza.
  • Severity driver: TripRegistrationCancellationReason is especially bad — it's the audit log for cancellations, referenced by multiple async-task signatures, and completely undocumented.
  • Fix: Add stanzas to §5 for each. Template in raw/03-model-schema.md.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] §7 claims token_version is legacy but the column still exists
docs.text:
• Doc: CLAUDE.md §7 "Member.token_version: legacy, unused… scheduled for removal"
  • Source of truth: api/models/models_member.py (the field is still there per list_models)
  • Drift: Doc promises the cleanup PR but it hasn't landed. Either land the PR or update §7 to soften the wording ("intended for removal in a later PR — still present as of YYYY-MM-DD").
  • Fix: Preferably do the cleanup PR; otherwise add a date marker.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] §6 undocumented rest_registration endpoints
docs.text:
• Doc: CLAUDE.md §6 lists register/, verify-registration/, reset-password/, etc.
  • Source of truth: URL list from list_urls
  • Drift: api/auth/register-email/ and api/auth/verify-email/ are routed to rest_registration views but not in §6.
  • Fix: Either document or remove from URL config. See raw/02-endpoint-drift.md.

docs.title: [medium / confidence high] §6 doesn't mention TripCreateView/TripEditView split
docs.text:
• Doc: "Trips (/api/trips/) — Standard CRUD"
  • Source of truth: ad4x4/urls.py + api/views/views_trip.py
  • Drift: POST /api/trips and PUT /api/trips/<pk> (no trailing slash) route to dedicated TripCreateView / TripEditView, not TripViewSet. CRUD is not uniform.
  • Fix: Note the split in §6 with a short rationale.

docs.title: [high / confidence high] §3 + §13 claim "~59 test files in api/tests/" — wrong location
docs.text:
• Source of truth: ls api/tests/ shows 3 files; ls tests/ at repo root shows 63 files (per Step 9 architecture agent).
  • Drift: Both §3 (repo layout) and §13 (testing conventions) point at the wrong directory.

docs.title: Backend Change Requests — AD4x4 Website
docs.text:
Purpose: Running list of backend API changes needed to support the website portal. Accumulated across development sessions for the backend team to address in one coordinated effort.

docs.title: Instructions for the Backend Developer / AI
docs.text:
IMPORTANT — Read this before implementing any item below.

Each item has a "Problem" section (written by the frontend team) and an "Implementation Record" section (to be filled by YOU after implementing the fix).

After you implement a change, you MUST fill in the Implementation Record for that item. This document will be shared back with the frontend AI developer so it can wire up the website to use your changes. If the record is incomplete or missing, the frontend developer will not know the correct parameter names, response format, or behaviour — and will have to reverse-engineer your changes, wasting time.

docs.title: What to write in each Implementation Record:
docs.text:
1. Status — Mark one: ⬜ Not started / 🔄 In progress / ✅ Complete / ❌ Won't fix

  2. What was changed — List every file you modified, every model field you added, every filter/ordering class you configured. Be specific:

  3. "Added OrderingFilter to MemberViewSet in members/views.py"
  4. "Added last_visited = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True) to Member model"

  7. Full URL pattern (e.g., GET /api/members/)
  8. Every query parameter: name, type, accepted values, default, whether optional

  9. Use a table format for clarity

  10. Example request & response — Provide at least one working curl command with a real response (or a realistic mock). Include:

  11. The full URL with query params
  12. Required headers (e.g., Authorization: Bearer <token>)
  13. The JSON response body (abbreviated if long, but show the structure)

  14. The HTTP status code

  15. Breaking changes — If you renamed fields, removed params, changed response structure, or altered default behaviour, list every change explicitly. If nothing breaks, write "None".

  16. Notes for frontend — Anything the frontend dev needs to know:

  17. "The param is ordering not order"
  18. "Returns 400 if query is less than 2 chars"

docs.title: #1 — Add server-side filtering for user's registered/waitlisted trips
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/trips/ Reported: Session #13 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The My Trips portal page needs to show only trips where the logged-in user is registered or waitlisted. The API currently has no server-side filter for this. The frontend is forced to:

  1. Fetch ALL club trips (pageSize=100) — returns trips for every member, not just the requesting user
  2. Filter client-side using the isRegistered / isWaitlisted booleans on each trip object

This causes:

  • ~17-30 second load times on mobile (95 KB payload, 3,305 total trips in the database, only ~17 belong to the user out of the 100 returned)
  • Incomplete data — the Past tab can only show the user's trips that happen to fall within the most recent 100 trips. Older registered trips are invisible.
  • Wasted bandwidth — 80-95% of the downloaded data is discarded

docs.title: Evidence (tested 2026-03-30 with user Elle, ID 21144)
docs.text:
What we fetch Time Payload User's trips in response GET /api/trips/?startTimeBefore=2026-03-30&pageSize=100 ~1.5-17s 87-95 KB 17 out of 100 results GET /api/trips/?startTimeAfter=2026-03-30&pageSize=100 ~0.5s 7 KB 2 out of 5 results GET /api/members/21144/triphistory?pageSize=100 ~0.5s 4.6 KB 7 out of 7 (all user's)

We confirmed that registered=true and isRegistered=true query params are silently ignored — the count does not change.

docs.title: Recommended backend changes
docs.text:
Option A (preferred): Add query filters to GET /api/trips/

Add support for these query parameters:

GET /api/trips/?registered=true        -> only trips where the authenticated user is registered
GET /api/trips/?waitlisted=true        -> only trips where the authenticated user is waitlisted

The data already exists — the API already computes isRegistered and isWaitlisted per-trip in the response. This just needs to be wired up as a queryset filter. This would reduce the Past tab response from 3,305 trips to ~17, and from 95 KB to ~15 KB.

Option B (alternative): Enrich GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory

The triphistory endpoint already returns only the user's trips and is fast (0.5s, 4.6 KB). However, it returns a slim object missing several fields the portal needs:

Currently returned: id, title, description, startTime, endTime, lead, level, checkedIn

Missing fields needed by the portal: - image (trip cover photo URL) - meetingPoint (name, lat/lon, link, area) - registeredCount / capacity (registration count vs capacity) - isRegistered / isWaitlisted (registration status badges) - allowWaitlist (UI logic for full-trip warnings) - approvalStatus (filter cancelled/rejected trips)

Adding these fields to the triphistory response would make it a drop-in replacement.

docs.title: Why not fetch individual trip details?
docs.text: We tested GET /api/trips/{id}/ for each trip ID from triphistory. Each call takes 3-13 seconds. Seven sequential calls = ~90s. Even in parallel = ~21s. This is worse than the current approach.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. Backend docs (trips.md, members.md) confirm: - GET /api/trips/ has NO registered or waitlisted filter parameter. - GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory returns slim objects missing: image, meetingPoint, registeredCount, capacity, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, allowWaitlist, approvalStatus. - New finding from vehicles.md: Trip registration responses now include a vehicle object. The triphistory endpoint is also missing this field. If Option B is chosen, vehicle should be added to the enriched response too. - All assumptions in our Problem section are valid.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete (both options implemented — confirmed by backend team 2026-04-01)

What was changed: Backend team implemented BOTH Option A and Option B: - Option A: Added registered and waitlisted boolean query parameters to GET /api/trips/ - Option B: Enriched GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory with 9 additional fields (image, meetingPoint, registeredCount, capacity, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, allowWaitlist, approvalStatus, plus level as full object)

New/updated endpoint syntax (Option A):

Parameter Type Description registered boolean true = only trips where auth'd user is registered; false = only trips where NOT registered waitlisted boolean true = only trips where auth'd user is on waitlist; false = only trips where NOT waitlisted

These filters combine with all existing filters. Uses efficient Exists() subqueries.

Example request & response (Option A):

# Upcoming registered trips
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/?registered=true&startTimeAfter=2026-04-01&ordering=start_time"

# Past registered trips
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/?registered=true&startTimeBefore=2026-04-01&ordering=-start_time"

Expected impact: response size drops from ~3,305 trips (95 KB) to ~15-20 trips (~15 KB). Load time from 17-30s to <1s.

New/updated response fields (Option B — triphistory): Fields increased from 8 to 17: id, title, description, startTime, endTime, lead (object, serialized with ConciseMemberSerializer — returns only id and username), level (full object), checkedIn, image, meetingPoint (object), registeredCount, capacity, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, allowWaitlist, approvalStatus

Breaking changes: None — new fields are additive. Existing integrations unaffected.

Notes for frontend: - Use Option A for the "My Trips" portal page (registered/waitlisted tabs) - Use Option B for admin viewing of other members' trip history - Both filters require authentication. Unauthenticated requests ignore the filter. - registered=true and waitlisted=true can be combined (returns empty set since a user can't be both) - Default if neither is set: returns all trips (existing behaviour) - Ordering (ordering=start_time etc.) works alongside the new filters - See updated docs: reference-docs/api-docs/django-backend/trips.md, reference-docs/api-docs/django-backend/members.md

docs.title: #2 — Trailing-slash inconsistency across endpoints
docs.text: Priority: Medium Reported: Session #13 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Some endpoints require a trailing slash, others return 404 when a slash is present. This causes silent failures when the proxy or client guesses wrong.

Endpoint Without slash With slash Correct form /api/trips 403 (authenticated) 200 With slash /api/levels 301 redirect 200 With slash /api/vehicles 301 redirect 200 With slash /api/choices/carbrand 200 404 Without slash /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings 200 404 Without slash /api/members/request-deletion 200 404 Without slash

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Standardise all endpoints to accept both forms. Django's APPEND_SLASH setting should handle this, but some endpoints (particularly under /api/choices/ and /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings) appear to bypass it.

The frontend proxy currently works around this with redirect-following and 403/405 retry logic, but a consistent backend would be cleaner.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. Cross-referencing all backend docs reveals: - Endpoints WITH trailing slash (documented): /api/vehicles/, /api/vehicles/{id}/, /api/notifications/mark-as-read/, /api/feedback/, /api/meetingpoints/, /api/trips/, /api/members/. - Endpoints WITHOUT trailing slash (documented): /api/members/request-deletion, /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings. - Live-tested: notifications.md documents the mark-as-read body field as notificationIds (camelCase). Both notificationIds and notification_ids work (both return 204). The error message says notification_ids, so that's the canonical internal name. Both docs are technically correct. - Live-tested: vehicles.md references GET /api/choices/carbrands/ (plural, with slash) — THIS IS WRONG IN THE BACKEND DOCS. Only GET /api/choices/carbrand (singular, no slash) returns 200. All other variants (carbrands/, carbrands, carbrand/) return 404. Backend team must fix vehicles.md. - The trailing-slash inconsistency table in our Problem section is still accurate, and /api/choices/carbrand is another example.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ❌ Won't fix (confirmed by backend team 2026-04-01)

Resolution: The backend team confirmed this is by design: - Router-registered ViewSets (list/detail) — trailing slash required - Manual URL paths (search, choices, profile sub-endpoints) — no trailing slash

The pattern is consistent within each category. The proxy's redirect-follow + 403/405-retry mechanism (Lesson #23/#24) handles this transparently.

Notes for frontend: - Continue using the proxy's two-layer defence (redirect-follow + 405-retry) - Hook URLs should omit trailing slashes — the proxy handles it - See reference-docs/api-docs/django-backend/api-concepts.md for the updated trailing-slash table

docs.title: #3 — Members endpoint: server-side ordering is silently ignored
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/members/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The GET /api/members/ list endpoint silently ignores the ordering query parameter. All of the following return identical results:

GET /api/members/?ordering=username&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=-username&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=trip_count&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=-trip_count&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=tripCount&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=first_name&pageSize=5

Tested 2026-03-30: All six calls return the same 5 members in the same order (Admin, MegaMoe, khaiwi, iguana, Neo). Changing the page number confirms the overall order is fixed across pages.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text: The admin members table cannot offer column sorting (by username, name, level, trips, email, paid status). Admins managing 10,610+ members have no way to find the most active members, newest members, or sort alphabetically without using the search endpoint.

docs.title: Recommended fix
docs.text:
Add OrderingFilter to the members viewset. Minimum sortable fields:

ordering_fields = ['username', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'trip_count', 'level__numeric_level', 'date_joined', 'id']

Both ascending (ordering=username) and descending (ordering=-username) should work.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. members.md documents these filter parameters for GET /api/members/: car_brand, car_year, trip_count, phone, level__numeric_level, level__name, email, first_name, last_name, nationality, city — and pagination (page, page_size). No ordering parameter is documented. The backend genuinely has no OrderingFilter configured. - Note on parameter naming: The documented filter params use Django double-underscore syntax (e.g., level__numeric_level) and snake_case. The ordering param should follow the same convention.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete

What was changed: - Added OrderingFilter and SearchFilter to filter_backends in MemberViewSet (api/views/views_member.py) - Added ordering_fields list with 8 sortable fields - Added ordering = ['id'] as default (preserves existing behavior) - Also added DjangoFilterBackend explicitly to filter_backends (was previously implicit via filterset_class)

New/updated endpoint syntax:

Parameter Type Accepted values Default Notes ordering string username, -username, first_name, -first_name, last_name, -last_name, trip_count, -trip_count, level__numeric_level, -level__numeric_level, date_joined, -date_joined, id, -id, last_visited, -last_visited id Prefix with - for descending. Multi-field supported: ordering=-trip_count,username

Example request & response:

# Most active members first
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?ordering=-trip_count&pageSize=3"
→ { "count": 10610, "results": [{ "username": "khaiwi", "tripCount": 154 }, ...] }

# Least active members first
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?ordering=trip_count&pageSize=3"
→ { "count": 10610, "results": [{ "username": "Neo", "tripCount": 0 }, ...] }

# Alphabetical by username
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?ordering=username&pageSize=3"

Breaking changes: None. Default ordering remains id ascending (same as before).

Notes for frontend: - Param name is ordering (Django REST Framework standard) - Field names use snake_case with double underscores for relations (e.g., level__numeric_level). CamelCase field names (e.g., tripCount) do NOT work for ordering — use trip_count. - Invalid field names are silently ignored (falls back to default ordering). No 400 error. - Multi-field ordering is supported: ordering=-trip_count,username - See updated docs: docs/members.md

docs.title: #4 — ~~Members endpoint: level_NumericLevel filter returns 0 results~~ ❌ CLOSED — Not a bug
docs.text: Priority: ~~Medium~~ → Closed Endpoint: GET /api/members/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30) Resolved: Session #14 (2026-03-30) — Frontend misunderstanding, not a backend bug

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The API documentation lists level_NumericLevel as a supported integer filter, but it returns 0 results for every value:

GET /api/members/?level_NumericLevel=9&pageSize=1   -> count: 0  (expected: 13 Board members)
GET /api/members/?level_NumericLevel=1&pageSize=1   -> count: 0

Workarounds that DO work:

Filter Example Result level_Name (exact string) ?level_Name=Board%20member 13 results level_Name_Icontains ?level_Name_Icontains=board 13 results level_NumericLevel_Range ?level_NumericLevel_Range=600,900 113 results

The level_Name filter is what the frontend currently uses. However, level_NumericLevel should also work as documented.

docs.title: Recommended fix
docs.text: Check the DjangoFilterBackend configuration for the members viewset. The level_NumericLevel filter field may be misconfigured (wrong lookup type, or wrong field name mapping).

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text:
✅ RESOLVED — NOT A BACKEND BUG. This is a frontend misunderstanding.

Live-tested 2026-03-30 with all numericLevel values:

numericLevel level_NumericLevel= level__numeric_level= Result 5 (Club Event) 0 0 Correct — no members at this level 10 (Newbie+ANIT) 9,247 9,247 ✅ Works 100 (Intermediate) 650 650 ✅ Works 200 (Advanced) 526 526 ✅ Works 300 (Expert) 0 0 Correct — disabled level 400 (Explorer) 74 74 ✅ Works 600 (Marshal) 100 100 ✅ Works 800 (Board member) 13 13 ✅ Works

Both naming conventions work identically. The original bug report tested with level_NumericLevel=9 and level_NumericLevel=1 — these are NOT valid numericLevel values (they're database IDs). The valid values are 5, 10, 100, 200, 300, 400, 600, 800.

Root cause: The original tester confused database ID with numericLevel. numericLevel=9 doesn't exist — Board member has numericLevel=800 (database ID=9). The filter works perfectly.

Frontend action: No backend change needed. Update the frontend admin panel to use correct numericLevel values, not database IDs, when calling this filter. Consider fetching the level list from GET /api/levels/ to build the mapping dynamically.

Priority downgraded: ❌ Not a bug — can be closed.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ❌ Not a bug — closed

Resolution: The filter works correctly. The original test used database IDs (1, 9) instead of numericLevel values (10, 800). All valid numericLevel values (5, 10, 100, 200, 300, 400, 600, 800) return correct counts. Both level_NumericLevel and level__numeric_level naming conventions work identically.

Working filter parameters (verified 2026-03-30):

Parameter Type Example Result level_NumericLevel integer ?level_NumericLevel=800 13 (Board members) ✅ level__numeric_level integer ?level__numeric_level=800 13 ✅ level_NumericLevel_Range string ?level_NumericLevel_Range=600,900 113 ✅ level_Name string ?level_Name=Board%20member 13 ✅ level_Name_Icontains string ?level_Name_Icontains=board 13 ✅ level_Id integer ?level_Id=9 10,610 🔴 SILENTLY IGNORED level__id integer ?level__id=9 10,610 🔴 SILENTLY IGNORED

⚠️ New finding: While level_NumericLevel works, level_Id is silently ignored. The frontend admin panel should use level_NumericLevel or level_Name for filtering, never level_Id.

Notes for frontend: Fetch the level list from GET /api/levels/ to build the numericLevel → name mapping dynamically. Use numericLevel values when calling the members filter.

docs.title: #5 — Members endpoint: paidMember filter is silently ignored
docs.text: Priority: Medium Endpoint: GET /api/members/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
GET /api/members/?paidMember=true&pageSize=1   -> count: 10610  (same as unfiltered)
GET /api/members/?paidMember=false&pageSize=1  -> count: 10610  (same as unfiltered)
GET /api/members/?paid_member=true&pageSize=1  -> count: 10610  (same as unfiltered)

The paidMember field exists in the response objects but cannot be used as a filter. The admin panel needs to filter members by payment status.

docs.title: Recommended fix
docs.text:
Add paidMember (or paid_member) to the filter fields in the members viewset:

filterset_fields = {
    # existing fields...
    'paid_member': ['exact'],
}

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. members.md lists all available filter params: car_brand, car_year, trip_count, phone, level__numeric_level, level__name, email, first_name, last_name, nationality, city. paid_member / paidMember is NOT in the list. The field only exists in the response object, not as a filter. - The response field name is paidMember (camelCase), so the filter param should ideally match. However, given that all other filter params use snakecase with double underscores, the filter will likely be paid_member (snakecase).

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete

What was changed: - Added 'paid_member': ['exact'] to MembersFilter.Meta.fields in api/filters.py

New/updated endpoint syntax:

Parameter Type Accepted values Description paid_member boolean true / false Filter by payment status

Example request & response:

# Paid members only
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?paid_member=true&pageSize=2"
→ { "count": ???, "results": [{ "username": "...", "paidMember": true }, ...] }

# Unpaid members only
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?paid_member=false&pageSize=2"
→ { "count": ???, "results": [{ "username": "...", "paidMember": false }, ...] }

Breaking changes: None. Purely additive filter.

Notes for frontend: - The filter param name is paid_member (snake_case). The CamelCase middleware may also accept paidMember — verify after deployment. - The response field name remains paidMember (camelCase) as before. - The paid_member field has a database index, so this filter is performant. - See updated docs: docs/members.md

docs.title: #6 — Unified advanced search for the members admin panel
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/members/search and GET /api/members/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The frontend admin panel currently needs to use two different endpoints with different capabilities:

Capability /api/members/ (list) /api/members/search (search) Browse all members Yes No (query is mandatory, min 3 chars) Text search (username, name) No (silently ignored) Yes Filter by level name Yes (level_Name) No Filter by level ID No Yes (level) Filter by min/max level No Yes (minLevel, maxLevel) Server-side ordering No (silently ignored) Not tested Filter by paid status No (silently ignored) Not tested

This forces complex frontend logic to switch between endpoints depending on whether the user has typed a search query or not, using different parameter names for the same concept (level filtering).

docs.title: Recommended enhancement — unified search and filter
docs.text:
Ideally, a single endpoint should handle all admin member queries. Two options:

Option A (preferred): Enhance GET /api/members/ to support text search

Add a search or q parameter to the list endpoint that searches across username, firstname, and lastname (case-insensitive partial match). Combined with the existing level_Name filter and new ordering support, this would cover all admin needs:

GET /api/members/?q=hani&level_Name=Marshal&ordering=-trip_count&paidMember=true&pageSize=20

Option B: Make query optional on GET /api/members/search

Allow the search endpoint to return all members when query is omitted, while retaining its level, minLevel, maxLevel filters. Add ordering support.

docs.title: Fields the admin panel needs to filter/sort by
docs.text: Field Filter Sort Notes Username Text search (partial, case-insensitive) Ascending/descending First name Text search (partial, case-insensitive) Ascending/descending Last name Text search (partial, case-insensitive) Ascending/descending Level Exact name or ID By numeric level Trip count Range filter Ascending/descending Useful to find most/least active Paid status Boolean exact Currently silently ignored Date joined Range filter Ascending/descending Newest/oldest members Last visited Range filter Ascending/descending See #7 — requires new field Email Text search City Exact or partial match Nationality Exact match Already works

docs.title: Frontend impact
docs.text: Once the backend implements unified search + filter + ordering on a single endpoint, the frontend will: 1. Remove the dual-endpoint switching logic in useMembers hook 2. Add clickable column headers for server-side sorting 3. Add paid status filter to the filter bar 4. Add date range filter for "joined date" 5. Add "Last Seen" column, activity indicators, and activity period filter (see #7) 6. Simplify the MembersParams interface to a single set of params

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. Backend docs confirm the two-endpoint split: - GET /api/members/ — filters but NO text search. - GET /api/members/search/ — text search (mandatory query ≥3 chars) with level, min_level, max_level. Requires SEARCH_MEMBERS permission (Newbie+, ANIT excluded). - Parameter naming inconsistency confirmed: List endpoint uses Django syntax (level__numeric_level, level__name). Search endpoint uses plain names (level, min_level, max_level). These are different naming conventions for the same concept. - Permission note: The search endpoint requires SEARCH_MEMBERS permission. If Option A is chosen (adding search to the list endpoint), ensure the text search respects this permission or document the new permission model. - All assumptions in our Problem section are valid.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete

Which option was implemented (A or B)? Option A — Added SearchFilter to GET /api/members/. The existing /api/members/search endpoint is unchanged (backward compatible).

What was changed: - Added drf_filters.SearchFilter to MemberViewSet.filter_backends in api/views/views_member.py - Added search_fields = ['username', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'email'] - This was done alongside #3 (ordering) in the same change

New/updated endpoint syntax:

Endpoint: GET /api/members/

The following parameters are now ALL available on a single endpoint:

Parameter Type Required Description search string No Text search across username, first name, last name, email (case-insensitive partial match). No minimum length. ordering string No Sort order (see #3 above for all accepted values). Default: id. paid_member boolean No Filter by payment status (see #5 above). level__name string No Filter by exact level name level__name__icontains string No Filter by partial level name level__id integer No Filter by level database ID level__numeric_level integer No Filter by exact numeric level level__numeric_level__range string No Filter by numeric level range (e.g., 100,400) trip_count integer No Filter by exact trip count trip_count__range string No Filter by trip count range (e.g., 5,20) first_name string No Filter by exact first name first_name__icontains string No Filter by partial first name last_name string No Filter by exact last name last_name__icontains string No Filter by partial last name email string No Filter by exact email email__icontains string No Filter by partial email nationality string No Filter by exact nationality code city string No Filter by exact city date_joined_after date No Members who joined after this date date_joined_before date No Members who joined before this date last_visited__isnull boolean No true = never visited, false = visited at least once last_visited_after datetime No Members who last visited after this datetime last_visited_before datetime No Members who last visited before this datetime page integer No Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No Results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Example request & response:

# Combined search + filter + ordering
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?search=hani&ordering=-trip_count&paid_member=true&pageSize=3"
→ { "count": 5, "next": null, "previous": null, "results": [
      { "id": 123, "username": "hani", "firstName": "Hani", "tripCount": 42, "paidMember": true, ... }
    ]}

# Browse all (no search) — existing behavior preserved
